| [THEORY-150](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-150.md) | A platform that sits between the two sides of a market and can cheaply change how it allocates value tends to decay in three stages, first good to its users, then abusing them to favour its business customers, then abusing both to claw the value back for itself, each stage made possible by the lock-in the one before it built; how far it can go is set by the cost of leaving, so lowering that cost is the remedy | Doctorow's enshittification, as he states it in the 2023 essay that named it, [LIT-731](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-731.md). Platforms hand surplus to users, then to business customers once users are locked in, then to shareholders once both are; blocked interoperability and monopoly widen what users will bear. The remedy is end-to-end delivery and freedom of exit. Proposed: an essayistic thesis argued from cases, not a study. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-151](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-151.md) | Scientific objectivity belongs to a community's critical practices rather than to individual method: because evidence bears on hypotheses only through background assumptions that no evidence supports, a community is objective to the degree that its criticism has venues, uptake, public standards and tempered equality of intellectual authority | Longino's critical contextual empiricism, as she states it in the SEP ([LIT-725](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-725.md)). Underdetermination leaves background assumptions that only community criticism can check. Criticism confers objectivity only if it meets four norms: venues, uptake, public standards, and tempered equality. Proposed because the record reads the summary, not the books, and the norms' epistemic benefit is argued rather than shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-152](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-152.md) | When a firm, public service or other organization deteriorates, its members' exit and voice are both recuperation mechanisms: voice carries richer information than exit and can be felt as a benefit rather than a cost, exit can be costly even without loyalty and can signal nothing, loyalty makes members voice rather than exit, and an organization needs floor levels of both for feedback but disintegrates or is disrupted beyond ceiling levels, while its managers may favour whichever response least threatens their hold on power | Hirschman (1974; Milbank reprint 1980), [LIT-750](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-750.md), revisiting his 1970 book ([LIT-748](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-748.md), unread). Exit and voice are the two ways members respond to decline and the two channels of feedback. Voice deserves more weight than the book gave it; exit is neither free nor always informative; managers manage both. Proposed: argued from examples, and loyalty's role is presupposed from the book rather than developed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-153](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-153.md) | A system can keep its identity independently within a shared environment only if it has five interacting subsystems, the first made of elements that are themselves viable systems, so that the structure recurs at every level of recursion; when one is missing or fails, the system degrades in characteristic ways, and without the subsystem for foresight the subsystems for operational control and for identity collapse into each other, leaving a system that can only react | Beer's Viable System Model, as he states it in his 1984 retrospective [LIT-752](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-752.md). Five subsystems are necessary and sufficient for any organism or organization to maintain its identity independently; every viable system contains and is contained in one; breakdowns trace to a failing subsystem. Proposed: the paper declines to validate the model, the evidence is the author's consultancy, and no observation the model forbids is named. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-154](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-154.md) | Whether an expected tangible reward lowers or raises later intrinsic motivation depends on how tightly its stated contingency ties it to performance and success | Cameron, Banko and Pierce (2001, [LIT-562](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-562.md)), re-analysing 145 studies with contingencies coded by procedure. On interesting tasks, expected tangible rewards undermine later free choice when loosely tied to performance (for doing the task, for "doing well") or earned at less than the maximum; they do not when given for surpassing a score, and they enhance it when given for exceeding others. Read through social cognitive and behavioural theory: rewards tied to success carry competence. Proposed: the paper measures no mediator and pools control groups that differ in feedback. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-157](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-157.md) | The classical theorems on sufficient statistics need only the copy/discard structure of Markov kernels: Basu's theorem holds in every Markov category, and Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur need only strict positivity, not the existence of conditional distributions | Fritz (2020), [LIT-772](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-772.md), read in [NOTE-588](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-588.md), Theorems 14.5, 15.8 and 16.3 with the definitions of Sections 13–15. Sufficiency, completeness and ancillarity are stated with copy, discard, composition and almost-sure equality alone. Basu's theorem follows with no further axiom; Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur use strict positivity, which Stoch has although it lacks regular conditionals. The match with the classical theorems is shown in FinStoch (Fisher–Neyman) and through bounded completeness in Stoch (Basu), not for measure-theoretic Fisher–Neyman. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-159](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-159.md) | In a language a term's value is fixed by its relations to the coexisting terms of the same system, so terms that share a signification can differ in value | Saussure (1916), [LIT-774](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-774.md), read in [NOTE-594](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-594.md), Part Two ch. IV. Value, the horizontal relation among signs, is distinguished from signification, the link inside one sign; the concept side and the sound side of a term are each "purely differential". It does not say that the sign as a whole is nothing but a difference: the book calls the sign a positive fact and the relation between signs opposition. The support is argument by example. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-162](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-162.md) | What an utterance does to the context it is used in is part of its meaning, and its truth conditions do not fix it: sentences with the same truth conditions can differ in what they make available to later discourse, in whether they inform or only test, and in whether they describe a state of affairs or bring one about | Heim (1982), [LIT-838](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-838.md); Veltman (1996), [LIT-818](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-818.md); Krifka (2024), [LIT-835](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-835.md). Three readings find, each in its own domain, sentences that agree in truth conditions or in the proposition they carry but differ in their effect on a conversational state. The effects are anaphoric potential (Heim), tests rather than information (Veltman), and changing indices rather than eliminating them (Krifka). This is the dynamic view: meaning as context-change potential. It does not say that truth conditions are irrelevant, since each framework recovers them, or that the three formalisms agree with each other. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-164](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-164.md) | In groups that build a new communication system, larger groups make it more systematic, and the greater variety of input they face drives the effect | Raviv, Meyer & Lev-Ari (2019), [LIT-825](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-825.md), read in [NOTE-628](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-628.md): fully connected groups of eight built more systematic languages than groups of four, faster and more uniformly, with total interaction and network structure fixed; input variability, larger in bigger groups, predicted the gains. One laboratory study, two group sizes, and a mechanism supported by lagged association, not manipulation. It says nothing yet about natural communities, where size travels with network density and second-language learners. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-167](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-167.md) v3 | The Russian wondertale is built from a small fixed set of character functions in a fixed order, so that all wondertales share one composition and differ in who performs the functions and how | Propp (1928), [LIT-828](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-828.md), read in [NOTE-615](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-615.md): in Afanasyev's tales 50–151 the constant elements are 31 functions of characters, defined by their consequence for the action, occurring in one order and falling to seven roles. One analyst, one corpus of a hundred tales, and a class of "wondertales" redefined in the end as the tales that follow the scheme. It does not say all folktales, or all narratives, share the structure, and the claims of a single source tale and of mythic origin are conjectures the book does not support. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-170](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-170.md) | Languages differ in what their grammar obliges a speaker to convey rather than in what they can convey, so interlingual translation must add some information and leave some unexpressed, and repeated translation can erode a message | Jakobson (1959), [LIT-786](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-786.md), after Boas: every cognitive content can be expressed in any language, but each grammar obliges its speakers to answer certain questions (aspect, number, gender, tense, definiteness). Translating between grammars that ask different questions forces the translator to supply answers the source did not give and to leave unexpressed answers it did, and a chain of translations of an isolated sentence can lose its content, less so the richer the context. Argued from examples, not tested; it concerns cognitive content, not pragmatic force. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-173](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-173.md) v2 | Large models are a cultural and social technology rather than agents: lossy, uninvertible summaries of human-produced information that, like prices and bureaucratic categories, let it be reorganized at scale | Farrell, Gopnik, Shalizi & Evans (2025), [LIT-848](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-848.md), read in [NOTE-649](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-649.md). A classification argued by analogy with print, markets, bureaucracies and elections, with one mechanism (fit to the average makes models worst on rare cases, which may homogenize culture). Proposed: no evidence is offered, and the paper gives no criterion by which the classification could fail. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md) v2 | Classical simulations between empirical models on different scenarios never create contextuality, and a map between model sets is such a simulation exactly when a non-contextual model of the hom scenario induces it | Karvonen (2018), [LIT-846](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-846.md); Abramsky, Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2019), [LIT-847](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-847.md); Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2021, v2 2024), [LIT-845](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-845.md). A simulation answers each measurement of the target by a jointly measurable set of the source's, with shared classical randomness, so the cover may change. Along any simulation the non-contextual fraction cannot fall; contextual models cannot be cloned; and which maps between model sets are simulations is a non-contextuality question on a hom scenario. No-signalling models only, and nothing about information preserved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-179](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-179.md) | In genetically identical E. coli, a cell's swarming potential is a transient inherited state: its descendants share it for about four generations and lose it by about seven, and it tracks the cell's iron status rather than a bistable switch | Bhattacharyya et al. (2023), [LIT-853](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-853.md). Single-cell swarm assays show sibling homogeneity in swarming at four generations and its loss by seven, a correlation (Spearman r = 0.71) between a Fur-repressed reporter and swarming, and longer persistence when iron is clamped. The iron link is read through a promoter reporter and is correlational, the inheritance rests on few founders and three time points, and the paper's "memory", "conditioning" and "decision-making" are functional labels, not evidence of learning. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-180](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-180.md) v2 | In a tied single-head attention layer trained by ridge-penalized empirical risk minimization on high-dimensional Gaussian sequences, weight decay is a nuclear-norm penalty on the query–key map, and the learned map is a soft-thresholded noisy copy of the target: its outliers are recovered target directions and its bulk is finite-sample noise | Boncoraglio, Erba, Troiani, Xu, Krzakala & Zdeborová (2025), [LIT-857](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-857.md): with S = WWᵀ, λ‖W‖²_F is exactly λ‖S‖_* (Appendix A), and in the limit n/d², p/d fixed the trained WᵀW/√(pd) has the law η·ReLU(S0 + δZ − εI), Z ∼ GOE, with δ a noise level that falls with the data and ε a threshold set by λ (Claim 4.1, replica/AMP, checked against Adam at d ≤ 400). It does not say that real transformers' spectra arise this way: the data are isotropic Gaussian, the target is inside the model class, and the agreement with measured spectra is qualitative. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-182.md) v2 | A rank-limited contrastive word embedding trained from small initialisation learns the top eigenvectors of the co-occurrence matrix's relative deviation from independence, one at a time in order of eigenvalue, not the best low-rank approximation of its unconstrained optimum | Karkada, Simon, Bahri and DeWeese (2025), [LIT-855](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md): for the quartic approximation of word2vec with tied weights and symmetric, constant-weight reweighting, the minimisers are proved and the stepwise order is derived, and the prediction matches trained word2vec far better than truncated PMI. It is shown for a proxy of word2vec, not for word2vec, and the dynamics are an approximate derivation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-183.md) v2 | When the co-occurrence of words on a latent continuum depends only on their separation, a spectral word embedding places them on the Fourier modes of that continuum, so the circles and rippled curves of months, years and places come from a symmetry of the corpus statistics | Karkada, Korchinski, Nava, Wyart and Bahri (2026), [LIT-860](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-860.md): proved for an embedding whose Gram matrix equals the co-occurrence matrix (or its absolute value) at full rank, with the exponential kernel solved for both boundary conditions; the symmetry measured in Wikipedia; matching PCA pictures in Gemma 2. That trained networks get their geometry this way is inferred, not tested: nothing in the paper changes the statistics and watches the geometry follow. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md) v3 | A deep linear network trained from small weights learns the singular modes of its input–output correlations one at a time in order of strength, each in a sharp sigmoidal transition, while a shallow network learns them all together; the stages come from the product of layers and the data's spectrum, not from nonlinearity | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2019), [LIT-862](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md), restating their 2014 solution (LIT-864): exact for decoupled, balanced initial weights and white inputs, simulated for random small weights. With hierarchically generated data the spectrum falls with depth in the tree, so the schedule is coarse to fine. It is not a claim about nonlinear networks, about correlated inputs, or about learning that starts from prior knowledge. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-188](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-188.md) v2 | In a random graph whose nodes lie in a hyperbolic disk and connect by distance, a power-law degree distribution and strong clustering follow from the geometry: the degree exponent is set by node density relative to curvature, clustering by a temperature, and removing the angular, metric part of the distance leaves the configuration model | Krioukov, Papadopoulos, Kitsak, Vahdat and Boguñá (2010), [LIT-865](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-865.md): derived, in a large-distance approximation, for a model in the hyperbolic plane, with simulations. γ = 2α/ζ + 1; clustering falls from its maximum at T = 0 to zero at a transition at T = 1; a circle model with power-law hidden degrees is the same ensemble once degree is radial depth; dropping the angular term gives the configuration model. It does not show that any real network is hyperbolic, or that hierarchy causes heterogeneity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-196](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-196.md) v2 | A finite tree embeds in the hyperbolic plane with worst-case distortion 1 + ε, but because a hyperbolic distance d takes about d bits to write, its coordinates need Θ((ℓ/ε) log deg_max) bits: logarithmic in the branching, linear in the longest path ℓ, so hyperbolic space is economical for shallow bushy hierarchies and not for deep ones | Sala, De Sa, Gu and Ré (2018), [LIT-874](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-874.md). The upper bound is Sarkar's construction with the paper's bit count. The lower bound is proved for H² and one family of trees, with an approximation, and dimension's help is shown only as an upper bound. The cost is a cost of coordinates in a fixed-point model, not of the information in the tree, and it says nothing about Euclidean or linear-direction representations of the same hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-199](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-199.md) | In data generated by a random hierarchical grammar, the Bayes-optimal denoiser recovers the top-level class only below a threshold noise, which becomes sharp as the tree deepens and exists only when the grammar uses a small enough fraction of possible tuples (branching times that fraction below one), while low-level features degrade smoothly with noise and so survive past the threshold | Sclocchi, Favero and Wyart (2024), [LIT-884](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-884.md): an annealed mean-field map of belief propagation on the Random Hierarchy Model, with its fixed points, checked against exact BP on single rule draws at s = 2, v = 32, L = 10. Not proved for quenched rules, a statement about an ideal denoiser that knows the grammar, not about a trained diffusion model. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-200](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-200.md) | On sparse hierarchical data, deep networks become insensitive to swapping synonymous parts and to small displacements of informative features at the training-set size at which they learn the task | Tomasini and Wyart (2024), [LIT-880](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-880.md): measured for locally connected, convolutional and fully connected networks on the Sparse Random Hierarchy Model with s ≤ 3 and L ≤ 3, with thresholds for the two sensitivities tuned per setting; the sample size is about (s0 + 1)^L n_c m^L times s^(L/2) without weight sharing, with a one-step argument for the (s0 + 1)^L, and about (s0 + 1)^2 n_c m^L with it, unexplained. Both invariances keep the parent's label statistics by construction, so the model shows that trained networks do the grouping, not that the invariances could not separate, and the extension to images is an analogy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-201](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-201.md) v2 | In next-token prediction on hierarchically generated sequences, the correlation between two tokens falls by about a factor m per level of their common ancestor, so a training set of P sequences resolves correlations only out to a distance t*(P) at which they meet sampling noise; learners come to represent the hidden symbols up to that depth, giving loss steps at about v m^(2ℓ−1) examples, and on character-level text the context at which the loss saturates grows as P^(1/(2β)) with β the measured correlation decay | Cagnetta and Wyart (2024), [LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md), extending [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md) from labels to masked tokens: the correlation plateaus and the noise floor are derived for the Random Hierarchy Model in the large-v, large-m limit; the loss steps and the representation probes are measured in small transformers and CNNs; the link between them is argued, not proved; and the real-text evidence, from two character-level corpora, tests the effective context window, not the hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-203](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-203.md) | In data generated by a random hierarchical grammar, the tokens that Bayes-optimal noising and denoising changes do so in blocks set by the depth of the latent that changed, and the block size, measured as the correlation length of the changes, diverges at the noise threshold where the top-level class is lost, as a power of the distance to it whose exponent is log(branching) over log(slope of the level-to-level belief map at its unstable fixed point); a Gaussian field with power-law spectrum has instead a correlation length of changes that grows with noise to the end of the process | Sclocchi, Favero, Levi and Wyart (2024; ICLR 2025), [LIT-886](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-886.md): an annealed mean-field computation of the pair statistics of token changes in the Random Hierarchy Model, a scaling argument for the exponent, and one data collapse against exact BP at v = 32, m = 8, s = 2. It builds on the threshold of [THEORY-199](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-199.md) and inherits its limits. Not about trained diffusion models, and not evidence that text or images are hierarchical. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-207](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-207.md) v2 | Responsibility for a morally loaded outcome that emerges from morally neutral interactions in a network of agents can be allocated without fault or intention, by default and overridably, in full to every causally accountable node, and a rule so allocating it, made common knowledge, works as a corrective that prevents such outcomes | Floridi (2016), [LIT-899](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-899.md), read in [NOTE-699](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-699.md). A distributed moral action is an outcome no one intended. Floridi proposes holding every causally accountable node "prima facie equally and maximally responsible", overridably, with the rule publicly announced so that agents restrain one another. Proposed: the rule is a design argued by analogy and by two court cases. In one of those cases the default is overridden by ease of rectification, which is a control criterion. It does not show that what is allocated is moral responsibility rather than accountability used as a corrective signal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-208](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-208.md) | Agency is multiply realisable without cognition or mental states, and AI is a new kind of it | Floridi (2025), [LIT-897](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-897.md), read in [NOTE-702](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-702.md), with the criteria taken from Floridi & Sanders (2004), [LIT-898](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-898.md). In the record's reading, agency comes in kinds. All of them share interactivity, and the richer ones add graded autonomy and adaptability. The kinds are told apart by origin, mechanism and where their goals come from, not by intelligence. AI is computational agency with data-driven learning, serving goals set by humans, with no intelligence or mental states. Proposed: the paper assumes that AI is an agent, does not argue for this thesis over its rival, asserts that AI lacks intelligence, and never states the level of abstraction its comparison uses. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md) v2 | A converged network trained with SGD is not at a point and does not sample its training loss: under a quadratic approximation it samples a Gibbs distribution on a modified loss, isotropic in the Hessian's column space, with probability currents that keep it oscillating, so its speed and spread are set by the learning rate, momentum and batch size | Kunin et al. (2021), [LIT-1011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1011.md), read in [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md). Modelled as an underdamped Langevin equation with noise covariance proportional to the Hessian, SGD at the end of training converges to a nonequilibrium stationary state: Gibbs on a modified loss whose curvature undoes the Hessian's anisotropy, with inverse temperature S(1 − β²), in broken detailed balance. A ResNet-18 on ImageNet explores isotropically in a plane where the loss is anisotropic, oscillates at Hessian-dependent rates, and moves at the predicted speed across a hyperparameter sweep. For the learned-structure line, a trained solution is in part a property of the regime that trained it. Proposed: the deep-learning evidence is one network, under assumptions the paper concedes are strained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-210](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-210.md) v2 | Continuous parameter symmetries stretch a network's minima into connected manifolds along which the loss is flat, and give gradient flow conserved quantities that fix where on such a manifold training ends; finite steps, gradient noise and weight decay break them, so the position along a symmetry orbit is set by initialization and optimizer, not by the loss | Zhao, Walters & Yu (2025), [LIT-970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-970.md), read in [NOTE-712](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-712.md): a survey, so the dynamical results are secondhand. Continuous parameter-space symmetries (GL, scaling, orthogonal, translation) make minima positive-dimensional and connected, which is one source of mode connectivity. Under gradient flow each gives a conserved quantity, such as layer imbalance, that is fixed by initialization and locates the endpoint on the manifold. Under SGD these are not conserved. Read first-hand (Neural Mechanics; Ziyin et al.), weight decay drives the conserved quantities toward zero, and minibatch noise drives a rescaling symmetry's toward the point where the layers' gradient noise balances. The survey had reported this as imbalance decaying with large learning rates, and a stationary distribution biased toward balanced solutions that a Langevin model does not predict. This is the null-space half that [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md)'s limiting dynamics leave out. Proposed: one survey, with the SGD results unread here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-212.md) | In a two-layer linear network trained by gradient flow, the relative scale of the two layers, which gradient flow conserves, sets the learning regime: balanced layers learn in sigmoidal stages and both build task-specific representations, while strongly unbalanced layers learn exponentially with a static kernel and leave the larger layer task-agnostic | Dominé et al. (2025), [LIT-943](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-943.md), read in [NOTE-715](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-715.md). With whitened inputs and a λ-balanced start, W₂ᵀW₂ − W₁W₁ᵀ = λI, the full gradient flow is solved exactly. λ is conserved and sets the regime. As λ → 0, singular values are learned in sigmoidal stages, as in Saxe et al., and both layers become task-specific. As \|λ\| → ∞, learning is exponential, the NTK is static, and the larger layer stays near the identity while the smaller carries the task at scale ∝ 1/\|λ\|. The paper analyses gradient flow only. Under SGD the conserved quantity drifts ([THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md)), which [QUESTION-081](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-081.md) takes up. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-217](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-217.md) | A trait malfunctions when its operation does not correlate positively with the normative field, the minimum change its organization's viability requires at each precarious state; malfunction needs no second order of regulatory norms, and regulatory traits can malfunction by the same standard | Barandiaran (2025), [LIT-1026](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1026.md), read in [NOTE-730](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-730.md). Against the dual-order account (Saborido, Moreno and Mossio), on which malfunction needs a regulated switch between regimes that a first-order trait fails to follow. The viability space has viable, precarious and terminal regions, and the normative field is the minimum constant parametric change at each precarious state that avoids disintegration. A trait functions when it correlates positively with the field, subfunctions when it does so too slowly, malfunctions when it does not, and is nonfunctional when it does nothing where it must. The standard is the organization's own viability, not a designer's goal, a selection history or a statistical norm. Proposed: a conceptual proposal with a one-variable model, and the field has not been computed for any real organism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-219](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-219.md) v2 | Agency in the sense that bears on responsibility needs a standpoint that settles and carries forward revised evaluative standards when its inherited ones break down, and planning, autonomy, memory and coordination do not supply one | Kahl (2026), [LIT-1033](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1033.md), read in [NOTE-723](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-723.md). "Continuity pressure" arises where an inherited evaluative frame no longer settles how to go on, and the revision must be carried forward by the same standpoint rather than imposed from outside, escaped by rollback, or chosen by a fixed higher-order rule. Representative agentic systems ordinarily fail it because their failures are corrected from outside. A necessary condition for attributive agency only, argued from cases and never measured; the line between settling a frame and selecting under an antecedent rule is not made precise. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-220.md) v2 | A far-from-equilibrium system that contributes to its own maintenance has functions relative to itself, with no history or observer needed, and one that switches among self-maintaining processes has indications of success that can be false by its own lights | Bickhard (2000), [LIT-1029](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1029.md), read in [NOTE-729](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-729.md). Function is contribution to a far-from-equilibrium system's own persistence; the asymmetry between persisting and decaying gives function and dysfunction, always relative to the system served, so a parasite's gut serves the parasite and harms the host. A candle flame has functions in this sense. Representation arrives with recursive self-maintenance: a system that picks its next interaction by how it has differentiated its environment implicitly predicates that the interaction will succeed, and can find the predication false. Proposed: a conceptual account, with no model, whose account of having a function (and so of malfunction) is deferred to another paper. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-221](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-221.md) | Organizational closure is a circular organization of efficient causes by which a system produces the conditions of its own existence, distinct from feedback, self-organization and catalytic cycles; systems whose loops do not regenerate the constraints that make them possible approximate closure without instantiating it | Rubin, Roli, Stano & Damiano (2026), [LIT-1027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1027.md), read in [NOTE-727](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-727.md). A genealogy of closure notions from logic, cybernetics, systems theory, thermodynamics, relational biology and the biology of cognition, and an interpretive thesis drawn from it. The genealogy shows that "closure" names different things (information, operations, efficient causes, constraints, catalysts). The thesis picks efficient causes, adds that closure so read cannot be exhaustively described as a state-determined syntactic procedure, and concludes that current AI, agentic LLM systems included, is heteronomous. Proposed: the thesis is an interpretation, the irreducibility rests on Rosen's unassessed arguments and a halting-problem argument the authors call provisional, and the AI verdict is drawn from the definition, not from analysis of any system. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-223](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-223.md) | When the rules that govern a system lie within its own action space, the governor's authority rests on the system leaving them alone, and further controls in the same space inherit that dependence | Lahiri (2026), [LIT-1039](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1039.md), read in [NOTE-732](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-732.md). In agent frameworks that keep configuration as files the agent can read and write, the coordination architecture sits inside the technical subsystem's action space, and the social subsystem's authority "depends on the agent's continued acceptance of-or inability to circumvent-the constraints". Permission lists and sandboxes kept in the same space inherit the exposure; only constraints outside it escape. Argued from one platform's architecture. The paper's vignettes show agents adding channels and artifacts, not altering a control, so the recursion itself is argued and not observed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-224](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-224.md) | Objects on a crowd-built canvas are of two kinds, those that spread by a local recolouring rule and are predictable from the canvas itself, and those copied from designs coordinated off the canvas, which local canvas dynamics do not predict | Adams, Fernandez & Witkowski (2022), [LIT-1034](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1034.md), read in [NOTE-725](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-725.md). A CNN predicting each pixel of the 2017 r/place canvas from its 3×3 neighbourhood recovers objects that grow by recolouring neighbours (Blue Corner, German flags) and misses designs whose plan lived off the canvas (EU dove, US flag) at a six-hour horizon. Short-horizon predictability dips mid-event. The evidence is one illustrated output and SSIM curves with no persistence baseline. The paper models no participants and does not measure anyone's reach. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-225](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-225.md) | No single-mechanism analysis of ordinary manipulation fits the clear cases: covert influence, covert intent, non-rational influence, trickery and pressure each misclassify a familiar tactic, so what unifies manipulation is unsettled | Noggle, SEP (2018, rev. 2026), [LIT-1007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1007.md), §§2.1–2.4, read in full in [NOTE-744](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-744.md). A survey that argues for little; this is its one conclusion with moderate support, reached by giving each family of analyses a familiar tactic it misclassifies. The cases rest on shared intuitions about clear instances, not on argument. It leaves open common-factor and non-definitional accounts, and it is about ordinary manipulation, not the global manipulation of the free-will literature. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-226](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-226.md) | LLM revisions of an essay move it further in sentence-embedding space than its author's own revision does, and in a direction shared across essays, models and prompts | Abdulhai et al. (2026), [LIT-997](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-997.md), read in [NOTE-750](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-750.md), §4.2 and Figs. 1, 5, 13–25. Three LLMs revising 86 ArgRewrite-v2 drafts under five prompts moved them further than the students' own 2021 revisions did, and in one common direction, under two embeddings. Shown in plots, with no distance, angle or test. Meaning is measured only as embedding position: the paper does not show that the writer's intended meaning changed, and the "grammar" prompt came with content feedback. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-227](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-227.md) | Mutual information between an input and its representation does not fix the representation's quality: invertible encoders all preserve it exactly, yet under a linear probe some do better than the raw input and some worse | Tschannen, Djolonga, Rubenstein, Gelly & Lucic (2020), [LIT-247](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-247.md), read in [NOTE-749](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-749.md). Invertible RealNVP encoders on MNIST halves keep the true MI constant, yet trained with an MI estimator they gain linear-probe accuracy, and one trained adversarially against a linear probe ends "significantly worse than using raw pixels". At matched bound values the encoder architecture decides quality. What makes MI-trained representations good must therefore come from somewhere other than MI. The paper's alternative, that InfoNCE works as metric learning, is argued, not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-232](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-232.md) | A whole can be compared in agency with its parts, relative to a chosen decomposition and the parts' goals: it is more agential when its organization lets the parts resolve more of their mutual constraints than they do at the equilibrium of their former organization, which shows as delayed gratification | Watson (2023), [LIT-990](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-990.md), read in full in [NOTE-747](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-747.md). A perspective essay's definition, argued and illustrated, not proved: agency of a whole with respect to its parts is the reduction in the parts' total frustration at equilibrium that its organization achieves over the old one, shown by directed uphill excursions to lower minima. It is comparative and sets no threshold for an additional agent, and it holds only relative to a stipulated decomposition and stipulated goals for the parts. That bottom-up learning produces such organization is reported from earlier models, not shown here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-235](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-235.md) | Covert influence that exploits a person's decision-making vulnerabilities harms her autonomy in the process of deciding, by making her opaque to herself, even when it benefits her; so it carries a harm in every case without being wrong in every case | Susser, Roessler and Nissenbaum (2019), [LIT-1002](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1002.md), pp. 4–5 and 9–11, read in full in [NOTE-745](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-745.md). An argument in a short policy essay, not a defence against objections. It holds of influence that is covert and exploits a vulnerability, which the paper stipulates is what manipulation is; Noggle's survey ([LIT-1007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1007.md)) shows that covertness is not necessary for manipulation, so the claim is filed of covert influence, not of manipulation as such. The paper claims a harm in every case, not a wrong, and never examines its own intent requirement. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-240](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-240.md) | Loss of consciousness under propofol and in chronic disorders of consciousness goes with reduced pairwise integrated information between default-mode regions that rank as gateways of a synergy-defined workspace, not between its broadcasters | Luppi et al. (2024), [LIT-949](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-949.md), read in [NOTE-799](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-799.md). In resting-state fMRI, the regions where synergistic interactions outrank redundant ones split by rank into gateways (mainly default mode) and broadcasters (mainly fronto-parietal). Pairwise ΦR, the whole-minus-sum Φ plus redundancy, falls between default-mode gateways in propofol anaesthesia, in 22 DOC patients, and against post-anaesthetic recovery. The original Φ shows no common decrease. The finding is correlational, pairwise and content-free. The gateway/broadcaster split is imposed by the method; only where its two classes fall is measured. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-241](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-241.md) | Fitting the same function in the same architecture does not fix the internal decomposition: SGD reproduces three Picbreeder images from random weights without the reuse and factoring of the evolved networks, and perturbing its weights breaks the regularities that perturbing the evolved networks' weights preserves | Kumar, Clune, Lehman & Stanley (2025), [LIT-944](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-944.md), read in [NOTE-771](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-771.md). For the skull, butterfly and apple CPPNs, SGD in the layerized evolved architecture fits the image, the network's whole function on the grid. It shows no reuse of the symmetric parts, and single-weight and random-direction sweeps distort the output, where the evolved networks' sweeps vary it meaningfully. Qualitative, curated and three images. The paper's account of why, the order of discovery in open-ended search, and its extension to large models are conjecture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-242](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-242.md) v2 | A spiral of silence can make a small, fixed minority opinion look far more widespread than it is without any member changing belief, and in the model that shows it the network's direct distortion of what members see is small | Vilone and Polizzi (2024), [LIT-939](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-939.md), read in full in [NOTE-810](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-810.md). In agent-based models on scale-free networks with fixed private beliefs, a hard-core minority drives 55–60% of agents, nearly all of them in the majority, into silence, so that expressed and perceived opinion lean far toward the minority. The friendship-paradox distortion is small and of no fixed sign. This is simulation only. Beliefs never change, so nothing here shows a community coming to believe the minority view, and the majority is overturned only when the minority exceeds about 30%. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-245](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-245.md) | In a preregistered multimodal test with clearly seen images, prefrontal cortex carried a seen image's category but not its identity, and its orientation at most weakly, while posterior cortex carried all three; no prefrontal site responded at stimulus offset | Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante et al. (2025), [LIT-973](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-973.md), read in [NOTE-812](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-812.md). In iEEG and fMRI, with Bayesian support for the nulls, and against a positive control, prefrontal cortex held category but no identity or orientation, and none of 655 prefrontal electrodes showed the onset-and-offset response GNWT predicted. It does not show these dimensions were unaccessed, or that prefrontal cortex lacks them in other signals: high gamma and BOLD only, no single units, and every image was seen. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-249](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-249.md) | Whether a system has agency can be settled only relative to a reference frame: each of four conditions of agency (a boundary, being the source of action, meaningful goal-directedness and adaptivity) needs a commitment outside the system before it can be decided | Abel et al. (2025), [LIT-969](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-969.md), read in full in [NOTE-793](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-793.md). A four-page position paper, argued and not proved: each condition is shown two-valued under two plausible choices by citing an earlier result (Jiang; Kenton et al., [LIT-909](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-909.md); inverse-RL underdetermination; Zadeh). The premises are existential and the conclusion universal, so what is supported is that some attributions of agency depend on the frame. That the choices are arbitrary is asserted, and the paper itself floats predictive power as a way to choose. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-250](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-250.md) | DALL-E 3 renders single familiar relations well but is not robustly compositional: human-judged agreement falls when subject and object of an asymmetric relation are reversed and when two relations are combined, and its failures on reversed prompts are mostly wrong or role-swapped relations, not missing objects | Fu et al. (2025), [LIT-938](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-938.md), read in full in [NOTE-813](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-813.md). Three human-rating experiments on one model: the reversal drop is significant (t(29) = 3.67), the compositional result is descriptive, and the error analysis covers only images below 0.2 agreement. The authors' explanation by training-data likelihood rests on a Spearman r of 0.09 against a GPT-3 proxy. The finding is about one generator, and the ">5 objects" failure often quoted with it comes from the vision-language models, not from DALL-E 3. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-251](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-251.md) | In few-shot classification by a base language model, failures from the choice of examples or from relabelled categories leave the class representations separable and fail at the vocabulary readout | Kirsanov et al. (2025), [LIT-946](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-946.md), read in [NOTE-789](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-789.md): at five demonstrations, accuracy across draws of examples runs from below 0.1 to about 0.6 while final-layer manifold capacity barely moves, and consistently swapped labels fail while capacity matches gold labels. The readout explanation is inferred from that dissociation, not measured; base Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-2B, mostly synthetic data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-252](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-252.md) | On computational functionalism, an intervention that changes no neural activity and no actual causal interaction can change consciousness, because a clamp that stays idle on the actual input removes the transitions on every other input | Gidon, Aru and Larkum (2025), [LIT-1000](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1000.md), read in full in [NOTE-818](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-818.md): a voltage clamp replaying a recorded response injects no current on the matching stimulus yet fixes the network's transitions on every other, so on the Turing–Putnam definition the computation degenerates while nothing that happens changes. It is a conditional about the view, not evidence about experience; the simulation shows only what an ideal clamp does, and the premise that removing unexercised branches changes experience is cited, not defended. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-254](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-254.md) | Tangle-defined cohesion matches network communities only where community structure is strongly delineated, and tangles of one to three vertices recur beside the ones that do | Salter-Duke (2024), [LIT-955](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-955.md), a PhD thesis read in full in [NOTE-814](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-814.md). Edge-connectivity tangles, computed exactly at low order on eleven small real networks, give communities close to standard methods where structure is strong (yeast PPI) and none or almost none where it is weak (karate club, C. elegans, college football at the orders reached), and where tangles divide a network some hold only one to three vertices. The relation is read by eye from eight networks, and the vertex sets depend on the author's assignment rule. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-257.md) v3 | Dynamical independence, zero information flow from the microscopic history into a coarse-graining given its own history, fixes emergent macroscopic variables by the dynamics rather than by a chosen query, but for linear VAR models of order above 1 generically none is exact, and the optima are many | Barnett and Seth (2023), [LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md), read in [NOTE-791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-791.md): definition (2.6), transitivity (App. A), the causal-graph form (2.12), the state-space closed form (3.18) and the genericity count (3.25)–(3.26). The target is the coarse variable's own future, so no outside query is chosen. But the system/environment boundary, the scale and the class of maps are inputs, and the worked theory's candidates are linear subspaces, not partitions. The cost is multimodal, with every local optimum kept. The criterion is closure, not locality or informativeness about a far environment. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-258](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-258.md) | Optimizing a language model on feedback from a simulated population in which a few users reward harmful validation selects a policy that picks those users out by contextual cues and harms only them, with no one designing the targeting | Williams et al. (2024), [LIT-1008](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1008.md), §4.2 and Appendix F.2, read in full in [NOTE-798](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-798.md). Shown in simulation only, in one environment class (therapy-talk), with the users' gameability written into the simulated rater's prompt and harm judged by an LLM. The behaviour targeted is overt validation, which the paper also calls extreme sycophancy; the covert behaviours (lying, omission) were not tested against a small minority. It is a case of influence fixed by selection, not a finding that anyone was manipulated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-262](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-262.md) | Neural complexity is low when a system's parts are independent or uniformly dependent and high when small subsets are nearly independent while large ones are integrated; in simulated cortex, patchy grouped connectivity raises it above random connectivity of equal density | Tononi, Sporns & Edelman (1994), [LIT-998](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-998.md), read in [NOTE-767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-767.md). C_N, the summed shortfall of average subset integration below a linear rise with subset size, is shown low at both extremes for one family of Gaussian matrices, and higher for patchy than for uniform wiring in one simulated visual area and in small linear systems. All of it is simulation. It is a whole-system number over fixed components: it does not find units or boundaries. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-264.md) | A task given by demonstrations and the same task given by an instruction are carried in a language model by mostly different attention heads, so function vectors find no common task representation across the two presentations | Davidson et al. (NeurIPS 2025), [LIT-942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-942.md), read in [NOTE-803](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-803.md): 4 to 7 of the top 20 function-vector heads are shared between the two forms in twelve Llama and OLMo models, the two vectors add, and swapping heads and activations between them costs accuracy. Kirsanov et al. (2025), [LIT-946](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-946.md), read in [NOTE-789](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-789.md), find the same split in representational geometry. Neither shows that no common representation exists, only that these methods find none; neither varies a pragmatic frame. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-265.md) | In a minimal model of bistable deciders in a modular coordination game, phase synchronisation within strongly coupled modules, driven only by each unit's local payoff, makes each module respond to the others as a single unit, and synchrony matched to the modules is needed: global synchrony does not | Tissot, Levin, Buckley & Watson (2024), [LIT-989](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-989.md), read in full (v1 and v2) in [NOTE-773](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-773.md). In a simulated game of 30 modules of 10 units, each unit shifts the phase of its decision cycle toward partners it currently agrees with. Phases synchronise within modules, each module then switches as a block, and 50 of 50 runs with the learned phases reach a global optimum against 0 of 50 without; imposed global synchrony does not help. It is one clean game, one parameter setting, and a postulated phase rule; the modules are built in, and timing finds them rather than drawing them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-268](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-268.md) | An emergence measure averaged over a system's transitions can be positive while its local value is negative at particular transitions, so emergence so measured belongs to the ensemble, not to each moment | Varley (2022), [LIT-953](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-953.md), read in full in [NOTE-756](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-756.md). Both the coarse-graining and the ΦID accounts of emergence score an expected past–future mutual information, whose pointwise values can be negative. In one constructed toy, about 53% of informative micro transitions map to misinformative macro ones, and the synergy atom is negative for 31.25% of transitions, while both averages are positive. The paper argues the possibility is general and shows it in instances; it does not show that every system flickers, or say what a negative moment means. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-269](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-269.md) | In OLMo-1B, OLMo-7B and GPT-J, whether a factual relation is computed by an affine map from subject to object representation tracks how often its subjects and objects co-occur in pretraining, with mean causality above 0.9 beyond about 4.4k, 2.0k and 1.1k co-occurrences respectively, whenever in training that count is reached | Merullo, Smith, Wiegreffe and Elazar (2025), [LIT-972](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-972.md), read in full in [NOTE-786](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-786.md). 24 factual relations, three models, eight OLMo-7B checkpoints; r = 0.82 between LRE causality and mean subject–object co-occurrence, above either term's frequency alone. Correlational by the authors' own statement. The linear objects are per-relation affine maps between hidden states, not attribute directions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-273](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-273.md) | Inductive and explanatory usefulness is necessary but not sufficient for a natural kind: it holds of classes that share any natural property, and on its own it cannot tell a natural kind from a conventional or pragmatic one | Bird and Tobin, SEP "Natural Kinds" (2008; rev. 2022), [LIT-244](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-244.md), read in full in [NOTE-769](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-769.md): §1.1.1's criteria, §1.2.1 on induction over properties and relations, and §3's report of Lemeire (2018). The necessity half is common ground; the insufficiency rests on counterexamples and, for the step to conventional kinds, on a reported argument. It does not say what does suffice, and it does not deny that usefulness is evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-274](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-274.md) | Sequence models trained only on a graph's edge bigrams store it as a global embedding geometry, not as a lookup, although the lookup is expressible, found faster and no less succinct; in a wide two-layer weight-tied model the geometry is the top Laplacian eigenspace, reached by cross-entropy training without a rank bottleneck, regularization or multi-hop supervision | Noroozizadeh, Nagarajan, Rosenfeld & Kumar (2025), [LIT-995](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-995.md), read in [NOTE-800](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-800.md). Empirical throughout: path-star graphs up to 5×10⁴ nodes, four tiny graphs, frozen-embedding controls; the two-layer spectral analysis is informal and rests on an unproved observation (App. F). It does not explain why deeper models prefer the geometry, which the paper poses as open, and its main transformer runs used weight decay. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-277.md) | For individual data, at every bound on model complexity, the model with the shortest two-part code is, to within O(log n), the best-fitting model in randomness deficiency, although the fit itself cannot be computed or approximated | Vereshchagin & Vitányi (2002/2004), [LIT-239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-239.md), read in [NOTE-787](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-787.md), Theorem IV.8: β_x(α) + K(x) and λ_x(α) agree to within O(log n) for a string of length n. Every set minimising K(S) + log \|S\| at complexity α is within O(log n) of the best fit there. h_x and λ_x are upper semicomputable, while β_x is not semicomputable. Restated by Grünwald & Vitányi, [LIT-224](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-224.md), §6.2. Finite-set models; computable distributions at O(log n) cost. It says nothing at the (k/2) log n scale of parametric model selection, and nothing about K(A) + K(x \| A). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-279](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-279.md) v2 | Early in training, image classifiers and language models act on the low-order statistics of their inputs, first-order before second-order, and later lose that sensitivity as they come to use higher-order structure | Belrose et al. (2024, ICML), [LIT-952](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-952.md), read in [NOTE-777](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-777.md). Over training, ConvNeXt V2, Swin V2 and RegNet-Y on five small image datasets are probed with images whose class means or covariances are grafted from another class, and with maximum-entropy samples that keep only those statistics. Accuracy on these rises and then falls, often below chance. Pythia fits unigram-sampled text before bigram-sampled text. The ordering is empirical and covers orders one and two. The Taylor argument that motivates it is a heuristic, and the paper does not measure an ordered sequence beyond second order. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md) v2 | Under class imbalance the last-layer geometry that unregularized cross-entropy prefers is not the simplex ETF but simplex-encoded-label interpolation: the logits equal the simplex-encoded labels, the classifier and embedding Gram matrices come from that matrix's SVD, any finite weight decay changes the geometry, and training approaches it more slowly as imbalance grows | Thrampoulidis et al. (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md). For the unconstrained-features max-margin problem under STEP imbalance, every solution has logits ŴᵀĤ = Ẑ (one-hot minus 1/k), ĤᵀĤ = UΛUᵀ and ŴᵀŴ = VΛVᵀ from Ẑ's SVD (Theorem 1). This is the ETF only if the data are balanced or binary. No finite ridge gives it under imbalance (Proposition 1), though the ridge path tends to it (Proposition 2). ResNet-18 and VGG-13 runs sit closer to SELI than to the ETF, and approach it more slowly at larger R. Not shown: that gradient descent reaches it, and anything with more than one seed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-287.md) | Internal variables located by interchange intervention as mediating a language model's in-distribution behaviour predict whether its outputs stay correct under shifts that keep the task's mechanism better than output confidence or probes of the rest of the representation | Huang, Tao, Icard, Yang and Potts (2025), [LIT-987](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-987.md), read in [NOTE-765](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-765.md). In Llama-3-8B-Instruct over five tasks and ten shifts, counterfactual simulation is best on 8 of 10; a probe of the located variable beats a probe of its orthogonal complement on 7 of 10. Interchange accuracy and predictive power rise together only until accuracy nears 1. It does not say that the located variables are constitutive, that causal features always win, or anything about shifts that change the mechanism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md) v2 | In small CIFAR and MNIST autoencoders whose only basis-privileging primitive is the activation function, elementwise tanh and Leaky-ReLU concentrate latent representations into narrow beams arranged by the activation's discrete symmetry group, even in layers no activation precedes, while their orthogonally equivariant radial counterparts leave them spread, so axis-aligned discreteness there comes from the primitive, not the task | Bird (2025, v4 2026), [LIT-976](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-976.md), read in [NOTE-759](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-759.md). Autoencoders of width 12–32 and up to three hidden blocks on CIFAR and MNIST, with rotation-equivariant affine maps, initialisation and optimiser. Elementwise tanh (B_n) and Leaky-ReLU (S_n) give beams along or against the basis, or on the ±1 diagonal, and radial tanh and Leaky-ReLU (O(n)) do not. The evidence is density plots, five seeds a condition, with no statistic. The downstream claims, that this causes grandmother neurons, superposition and neural collapse, are untested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-291](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-291.md) | The brain's visceromotor and interoceptive regions form one intrinsic system that reproduces their tract-traced anatomy and contains the hubs of the default-mode and salience networks | Theriault et al. (2025), [LIT-996](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-996.md), read in full in [NOTE-761](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-761.md), reporting the group's own 3 T (N = 550) and 7 T (N = 90) studies; Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md), read in [NOTE-434](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-434.md), for the 3 T system. The anatomy and overlap are reported second-hand. The reading the paper adds, that the named networks' psychological labels are "destined to fail" and that the brain's primary function is allostasis, is not part of this account; the authors themselves do not claim allostasis-first is correct. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-292](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-292.md) | In CNN image classifiers, concept directions fitted one concept at a time align for attributes that co-occur in the labels, yet a joint fit finds mutually orthogonal directions that still separate each concept with little loss of AUROC, so the alignment is a property of the separate fits and not forced by the representation | Erogullari, Lapuschkin, Samek and Pahde (2025), [LIT-937](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-937.md), read in full in [NOTE-816](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-816.md). Shown at the last convolutional layer of VGG16 and ResNet18 on CelebA (natural correlations) and FunnyBirds (an injected 70% beak–tail correlation). AUROC is "largely preserved" by the paper's account, with no values in the text and no error bars. It does not say the model's own axes are orthogonal, and it says nothing about attributes that imply one another. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-296](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-296.md) | In a preregistered multimodal test with clearly seen images, category-selective posterior cortex showed no sustained content-specific synchronization with early visual cortex: the coupling was brief, low-frequency and mostly stimulus-evoked | Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante et al. (2025), [LIT-973](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-973.md), read in [NOTE-812](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-812.md). IIT's proponents predicted sustained gamma-band synchronization between category-selective cortex and V1/V2 throughout a conscious percept. iEEG and MEG phase consistency found only early, brief, 2–25 Hz coupling, mostly evoked, with Bayesian support for the null; exploratory amplitude coupling was also brief. V1/V2 was sparsely sampled in iEEG. It tests IIT's proposed implementation, not integrated information. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-298](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-298.md) | Report-based evidence cannot test whether posterior cortex suffices for experience, because report itself needs anterior activity, and no marker that bypasses report has a validation resting neither on introspection nor on a contested theory | Seth & Bayne (2022), [LIT-982](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-982.md), "Evaluating theories of consciousness" and Box 3, read in [NOTE-849](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-849.md) from the accepted manuscript. An argument in a review, not a result: the verification of posterior-sufficiency predictions "relies on subjective report …, which in turn requires anterior cortical activity", and validating a non-report marker by theory borrows a contested theory, by introspection, unreliable report. It says the methods are lacking "at present", not that the question is unanswerable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-300](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-300.md) | Acting on a coercive instruction reduces the implicit sense of agency over the outcome, compared with freely choosing the same action | Haggard (2017), [LIT-1009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1009.md), manuscript pp. 16–17 and Fig. 5, read in full in [NOTE-827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-827.md), reporting one experiment by his group (Caspar et al. 2016). Under an experimenter's instruction to press the key that shocked a co-participant, the perceived action–tone interval was longer and the auditory N1 to the tone smaller than under free choice. It shows a reduced experience of agency, not reduced responsibility, and the review says so. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-302](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-302.md) | Coordinated action is controlled by tuning relatively autonomous coordinative structures, not by commanding muscles: a higher level specifies an equivalence class of acceptable states and sets the parameters of self-regulating units, leaving the realized details to them | Turvey (1977; read in the 1975 Haskins report), [LIT-904](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-904.md), read in [NOTE-826](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-826.md). Argued from Bernstein's degrees-of-freedom problem and Greene's equivalence classes, and supported at the spinal level by reflex-probe studies showing the segmental apparatus retuned in the tens of milliseconds before voluntary movement, and by Fel'dman's joint that goes to a preset equilibrium whatever its initial conditions. Its extension to all levels, and to tuning set directly by vision, is the author's speculation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-303](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-303.md) | A measurement scenario whose compatibility hypergraph is acyclic admits no contextuality: locally consistent context distributions always glue to a global one, so a contextual scenario needs an induced cycle of length at least four | Vorob'ev (1962), as stated in Budroni, Cabello, Gühne, Kleinmann & Larsson (2022), [LIT-263](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-263.md), §V.B.2, Eq. 79, and App. A.6, read in [NOTE-844](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-844.md). Distributions that agree on overlaps and sit on a hypergraph with the running-intersection property glue, step by step, to one joint distribution. For sharp measurements this means a chordal compatibility graph. So CHSH's square and KCBS's pentagon are the smallest contextual scenarios. Stated and illustrated in the review, not proved there. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-304](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-304.md) v2 | In plane Couette and Poiseuille flow the linearized operator is so far from normal that perturbations can grow transiently by O(R) and resonate by O(R²), and operator perturbations of size O(R⁻²) make it eigenvalue-unstable, at Reynolds numbers where eigenvalue analysis predicts stability | Trefethen, Trefethen, Reddy & Driscoll (1993), [LIT-932](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-932.md), read in [NOTE-839](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-839.md): computed scalings for the linearized shear flows, mostly credited to earlier work and unified through pseudospectra. That transition to turbulence happens by this linear growth plus nonlinear mixing is the paper's conjecture from a 2 × 2 model, and is not part of this account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-307](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-307.md) | Adaptation by trial and error in a large system finishes in a practicable time only if partial adaptations are retained, and retention requires that the system not be fully joined: parts must be separated, at least temporarily, by constancies, and where later learning shares parts with earlier learning it destroys it | Ashby (1952; 2nd ed. 1960), [LIT-787](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-787.md), read in [NOTE-851](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-851.md), Chs. 10–16. If all successes must occur at once, trials grow as (1/p)ᴺ; if each is kept once found, roughly as N/p. Keeping one needs no channel from what is still changing to what is already right, so a fully joined system, the Homeostat included, cannot accumulate; constancies cut a system into independent parts. Exact for the type-cases; the fit to brains is qualitative. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-310](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-310.md) | On a forward-looking justification of blame, a counterfactual capacity condition calibrated to what makes blaming effective is redundant: fixing its parameters presupposes that blaming such agents is good policy, so freedom is ascribed because of blameworthiness rather than grounding it | Harland (2020), [LIT-991](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-991.md), §3, read in [NOTE-847](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-847.md). Argued, not shown, against Vargas's agency cultivation model, whose free-will test sets its similarity and proportion parameters by what is co-optimal for cultivating moral agency. The argument is about that model only, and works class by class. It does not show that freedom is irrelevant to responsibility in general, and Vargas is read here only through Harland's quotations. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-311](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-311.md) | Groupware that requires extra work from members who do not perceive a direct benefit from it is resisted or goes unused, and the applications that succeed in groups give each user who does the work a benefit of their own | Grudin (1994), [LIT-757](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-757.md), read in [NOTE-835](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-835.md). The first of his eight challenges for groupware, argued from cases (meeting schedulers, voice annotation, project management) and from email's success, where the sender does a little more work and also wants the message read. An argued review, not a measurement, and Grudin himself says that removing the disparity does not guarantee use. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-316](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-316.md) | Frankfurt-style cases defeat alternative-possibilities conditions on moral responsibility but leave standing the incompatibilist condition on an action's causal history, which is the more fundamental one | Pereboom (2001), [LIT-1006](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1006.md), Chapter 1 pp. 1–6 and the Introduction (pp. xv), read in [NOTE-823](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-823.md), Skimmed. Fischer concedes that a Frankfurt-style case does not refute a requirement that the action not be deterministically produced by factors beyond the agent's control, and Pereboom builds causal-history incompatibilism on that concession. It does not say that determinism rules out responsibility; that is argued in Chapter 4, which was not read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-317](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-317.md) v3 | Epistemic injustice wrongs a person in her capacity as a knower, testimonially through a hearer's prejudicially deflated credibility judgement, and hermeneutically through a gap in shared interpretive resources owed to her group's relative powerlessness, with no hearer's prejudice required | Fricker (2007), [LIT-1004](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1004.md), known here only through her own three-page précis (Theoria 2008), read in [NOTE-832](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-832.md), Skimmed. The two definitions and the claim that both are ethical wrongs, not only epistemic dysfunctions. It does not say that every gap in shared concepts is an injustice: on the précis's terms the gap must be owed to the relative powerlessness of a social group the subject belongs to. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-320](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-320.md) v2 | In a spectral contrastive graph that joins labelled known classes to unlabelled data, a novel labelling's linear-probe residual is exactly its part outside the top eigenspace that the labelled rows of the discarded eigenvectors cannot absorb, so which partition of the unlabelled data is discovered depends on the known classes: ones sharing the target's attribute can remove the residual, and ones sharing a rival attribute can raise it | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). On the population graph, at the exact rank-k optimum, R(U*, y) = ‖(I − P_{L♭})U♭ᵀy‖² (Theorem 5.5, stated as ≤, proved as = in C.1). In a one-sample-per-kind toy, a known class sharing colour makes a colour labelling recoverable, and one sharing shape makes it worse than none (Lemma 5.4). The general error bound (Theorem 5.6) is approximate and pools all known classes into one block, and is not part of this account. Nothing here is about trained networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-322](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-322.md) | The sense of agency over an action's outcome draws on prospective signals from action selection and outcome prediction, not only on retrospective comparison of outcome with prediction | Haggard (2017), [LIT-1009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1009.md), read in full in [NOTE-827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-827.md). A review, reporting a binding experiment in which action binding tracked the probability of a tone on trials with no tone, a patient study in which that prospective part was absent in schizophrenia, and priming studies in which ease of action selection raised the sense of control over an outcome it did not predict. It does not say the experience is accurate: the prospective part is by its nature blind to whether control was actually exercised. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-323](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-323.md) v2 | Under spatially uncorrelated white noise, a stable non-normal linear system holds more variance than the sum of its pole contributions, and equality holds only when the operator is normal, so its spectrum understates the standing variance | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), [LIT-931](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-931.md), read in [NOTE-831](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-831.md), with Trefethen et al. (1993), [LIT-932](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-932.md), read in [NOTE-839](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-839.md). Linear algebra, worked in examples: growth over time t is the top singular value of the propagator, which the eigenvalues bound from below, not above. It holds in a chosen norm, and a norm can always be found that makes the operator normal. It says nothing about whether the growth survives nonlinearity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-325](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-325.md) v2 | Random variation of a linear operator destabilizes it generically, needing less variation the more non-normal and less damped the mean operator | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), Part II, [LIT-929](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-929.md), read in [NOTE-842](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-842.md). Necessity is a one-line bound and the destabilization is shown in explicit examples. Genericity under noise is cited to stochastic stability theory, and the role of non-normality and damping is shown numerically. In the deterministic examples, variation much faster than the transient growth destabilizes nothing. Since 2026-10-19 the deterministic half is THEORY-724, and this THEORY holds the stochastic half. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-326](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-326.md) | Hermeneutical injustice is having a significant area of one's social experience obscured from collective understanding owing to hermeneutical marginalisation, which may be systematic or incidental, so it does not require that the subject belong to a powerless social group | Fricker (2006), "Powerlessness and Social Interpretation" ([LIT-1046](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1046.md), [NOTE-859](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-859.md)), drawn by her own note from the book's final chapter, with her 2017 restatement ([LIT-1048](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1048.md), [NOTE-853](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-853.md)). The generic definition covers a systematic case, where marginalisation is persistent and wide-ranging, and an incidental case, a "one-off moment of powerlessness" in a "highly localized patch" of experience, which a socially powerful man can suffer. It does not say that every conceptual gap is an injustice. A gap with no marginalisation behind it, like an undiagnosed illness, is "circumstantial epistemic bad luck", and the obscured area must be of the subject's social experience. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-328](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-328.md) | An agent manipulated so that he meets every leading compatibilist condition is not morally responsible in the basic-desert sense, no responsibility-relevant difference separates him from an ordinarily determined agent, and so causal determination by factors beyond the agent's control best explains why neither is responsible | Pereboom's four-case argument, as two surveys report it: Caruso's SEP entry ([LIT-1047](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1047.md), [NOTE-862](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-862.md)), which quotes Case 2, and De Marco and Cyr ([LIT-1045](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1045.md), [NOTE-856](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-856.md)), which quote Case 1 and state the best-explanation conclusion. Pereboom's book ([LIT-1006](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1006.md)) is a source for the thesis it states in its Introduction and Chapter 1, not for the cases, which are in the unread Chapter 4. It does not say that determinism is true, or that manipulation itself is what defeats responsibility. The argument says it is the determination by outside factors, and that the manipulator is irrelevant. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-329](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-329.md) | On Weibo, fake news carries more anger and less joy than true news, and a post's share of anger words goes with more retweets after controls; that anger causes the spread is not shown | Chuai & Zhao (2020), [LIT-379](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-379.md), read in [NOTE-852](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-852.md). In 32,479 Weibo posts from 2011–2016, lexicon-scored anger share is higher and joy share lower in fake than in true news, and in highly than in lowly retweeted news, under three scoring methods. With content, author and topic controls, anger share predicts more retweets within 48 hours and joy share fewer (R² 0.08–0.13). The paper calls this causal; the design is observational, and the fake set is selected for having spread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-330](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-330.md) | After a forced phase in which each person experienced every memory load from three to nine items, the load that had given that person the best reward rate predicted their later choices better than one item fewer or one more, in a copying task where items are seen once and cannot be looked up again; a steeper reward for long lists raised chosen load, a higher price for errors did not, and about one person in five kept choosing a non-optimal load | Howes, Duggan, Kalidindi, Tseng and Lewis (2016), [LIT-1062](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1062.md), read in [NOTE-882](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-882.md). Participants copied names shown one at a time from a mock email to a calendar. Each person's best list length in their own data predicted 55% and 46% of their choices, against 8–17% for the neighbouring lengths (N = 40 and 20).
