An exponential points schedule raised chosen length (6.99 against 5.07); forfeiting the whole trial on one error did not (5.00 against 5.05). 13 of 60 persistently chose a non-optimal length. There is no look-up and no model: the prediction is each person's empirical argmax. Lieder and Griffiths' description of it as a memorize-or-look-up trade ([LIT-1071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1071.md)) does not fit the task. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-331](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-331.md) | Counting the inference a model will serve as well as its training, the least-compute way to reach a fixed quality shifts toward up-front compute as expected inference volume grows: a smaller model trained on more data in Sardana et al., a larger pretrained model over test-time search in Snell et al.; test-time compute won only at low volume and on questions the small model already sometimes solved | Sardana et al. (2024; arXiv 2023), [LIT-1070](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1070.md), read in [NOTE-881](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-881.md), and Snell et al. (2024), [LIT-1063](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1063.md), read in [NOTE-869](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-869.md). Sardana et al. minimise training plus lifetime inference FLOPs at a fixed loss under a Chinchilla-fitted law: the optimum moves to smaller models trained longer as known demand grows (28% fewer FLOPs at 30B quality and 10^13 inference tokens), and 47 runs show loss still falling at extreme ratios but more slowly than the law predicts. Snell et al. match FLOPs between a small model with test-time search or revision and a ~14× larger model on MATH: test-time compute wins at a low ratio of inference to pretraining tokens on easier questions and loses at a high ratio, and on the hardest at every ratio. Both take expected use as a known aggregate; neither has staleness or uncertainty about demand, and Snell's evidence is one model family on 500 questions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md) | An ideal observer is optimal relative to the information it is given, so a constrained ideal is the optimal decoder of a degraded input, not a restricted decoder of the full one; comparing real observers with ideals taken at successive stages of the visual system places losses by stage, and in early-vision tasks human performance is reported to parallel the retinal-stage ideal across conditions while falling well below it | Geisler (2011), [LIT-1055](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1055.md), read in [NOTE-870](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-870.md). A review that defines the ideal observer as optimal "given the available information and any specified constraints", and writes it as an expected-utility argmax over the posterior given the stimulus S or a constrained representation Z = g(S;θ). Constraints are added one at a time (optics, receptor sampling and noise, ganglion-cell summation), and human performance that parallels the retinal-stage ideal while falling below it is read as loss in central factors. The empirical parts are the review's account of studies the record has not read. The review gives no formula for efficiency and no notion of an optimum over a restricted class of computations. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-339](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-339.md) | People's answers to a probability query depend on their own answers to an earlier query whose result it can use: a person's sub-answer predicts their later answer only when asked first, and a bias induced in a first judgment carries into a second only when the two share part of a hypothesis space, so reuse carries the earlier error with it; that reuse saves computation rests on one small response-time study and one secondary-task result | Dasgupta, Schulz, Goodman and Gershman (2018), [LIT-1074](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1074.md), read in [NOTE-875](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-875.md); Gershman and Goodman (2014), [LIT-1056](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1056.md), read in [NOTE-886](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-886.md); Dasgupta and Gershman (2021), [LIT-1077](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1077.md), read in [NOTE-865](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-865.md). In five small online experiments, an earlier answer shapes a later one only when the later query can use it, and errors in the first carry into the second. The authors call this amortized inference, reuse of past computation bought at a cost in bias. The speed benefit is shown once (median log-RT facilitation, n ≈ 50 per order) and otherwise assumed; storage and retrieval are free in the models; the 2021 review adds stale cached values from the planning literature, second-hand. No paper prices when reuse pays or touches stores outside the head. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-342](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-342.md) | In AlphaZero on 9×9 Hex, at fixed playing strength, training compute and tree-search compute substitute along a straight line in log–log space, about 15× less search for each 10× more training over about two decades of training compute, down to a one-node search; the trade is measured for one search and counts no games played | Jones (2021), [LIT-1069](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1069.md), read in [NOTE-884](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-884.md). Across about 200 AlphaZero models on Hex boards 3×3 to 9×9, the best Elo for a given training compute follows one change-point curve, shifted by a fixed factor of compute per board row. On 9×9 only, iso-Elo contours of training against test-time search compute are straight in log–log space (fit: log test = −1.2·log train + 0.004·Elo + 29) over roughly 1e14–1e16 FLOPS-seconds of training, ending at a one-node search. One game, one nonstandard implementation, no uncertainty on the fitted coefficients, and no count of how many searches the trained agent will run, so it gives an exchange rate, not an amortization. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-343](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-343.md) | In laboratory choice tasks, people offload cognition more as a task's internal demand rises, but the choice follows their evaluation of the demand rather than its benefit: they offload where it gives no gain and more when less confident at equal ability, and offloading can lower memory for what was offloaded | Risko & Gilbert (2016), [LIT-1059](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1059.md), read in [NOTE-887](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-887.md). A review: in choice/no-choice studies of rotated displays, delayed intentions and short-term memory, spontaneous offloading rises with internal demand, but it also occurs where it gives no gain (writing items down about 40% of the time at a two-item load already at ceiling), rises with lower confidence after ability is controlled, and differs between displays of equal measured demand. Expecting to have a result stored externally went with poorer memory for it. The review reports no effect sizes, the cited studies were not read, and its metacognitive model is an unformalised box diagram; the drift toward external reliance is a prediction, not a finding. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-344](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-344.md) | An access method's read, update and memory overheads, each a ratio to the base data alone with a floor of 1.0, are conjectured to trade so that bounding any two forces a lower bound on the third; the conjecture is unproved, its formal wording says no more than the floor already does, and the paper's extreme designs show conflicts between pairs, read against memory and update against read, not a symmetric three-way trade | Athanassoulis et al. (2016), [LIT-1085](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1085.md), read in [NOTE-888](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-888.md). A six-page vision paper defines read, update and memory amplification and conjectures that an access method optimal on one cannot be optimal on both others. Its evidence is three one-paragraph propositions about extreme designs on an integer array, a qualitative triangle and a table of asymptotic I/O costs. The formal statement asserts only some lower bound on the third overhead, which every design has. The extremes are not symmetric: the memory-minimal design is also update-minimal. Build cost, workload and time are outside the triangle. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-351](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-351.md) | In a two-pilot airliner cockpit, setting the approach speeds as bugs on the airspeed indicators, prepared 25 to 30 minutes ahead in a low-workload phase from a card selected by the displayed gross weight, turns recall and scale reading at the moment of use into a judgement of spatial proximity, so the cockpit system remembers the speeds without either pilot's memory being improved; this is argued by task analysis of mandated procedure, not measured | Hutchins (1995), [LIT-1066](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1066.md), read in [NOTE-867](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-867.md). A stylized task analysis of one airline's MD-80 procedure, informed by observation but reporting no measurements. The speed-card booklet, filtered by the displayed gross weight, is the system's long-term memory; the values pass through speech to bugs on two airspeed indicators, and on approach the pilots judge the needle's nearness to a bug instead of recalling and reading speeds. The paper concludes that the memory is "not made primarily of pilot memory". It analyses only success, for an anticipated, mandated and invariant task with a few values needed in a fixed order, so it says nothing about search for one item among many under a deadline. Cognition in the Wild ([LIT-1060](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1060.md)) is Unavailable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-355](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-355.md) | Agents arrange their surroundings so that perception and choice take the place of internal search, changing how much thinking a task needs without changing what can physically be done; the set-up is paid once and recovered over the later choice points the arrangement serves, so an arrangement whose scope is the whole task can repay a large set-up and a narrow one must repay within the next few actions, and the arrangement decays unless maintained; the savings are argued and piloted, not measured | Kirsh (1995), [LIT-1076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1076.md), read in [NOTE-871](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-871.md), and Kirsh (1996), [LIT-1057](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1057.md), read in [NOTE-872](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-872.md). From video of cooks, assemblers and baggers and from informal observation, Kirsh classifies arrangements that simplify choice, perception and internal computation, frames their savings in search-complexity terms, and ties set-up cost to the number of choice points an arrangement serves. The 1996 paper adds a verbal investment rule with an interest factor for risk, one risk being that the change is not still present later, and upkeep against scatter. Neither paper gives a cost model or a measured saving; the 1995 paper says the savings do not "in general" admit meaningful quantitative estimation, and the 1996 paper puts mental cost outside its formalism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-359](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-359.md) | Cognitive mechanisms can be derived as the one, among those a brain can execute, that best trades the expected utility of its result against the opportunity cost of the time and resources it uses; the review shows the derivation reproducing many heuristics and biases, not that people are optimal, and the objective is per episode | Lieder & Griffiths (2020; online 2019), [LIT-1071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1071.md), read in [NOTE-873](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-873.md). Resource rationality picks the heuristic that maximizes expected utility of its result minus the expected opportunity cost of the time and resources it uses (Eq. 3), averaged over environments consistent with what is known (Eq. 4), and a five-step method derives process models from it. The support is a review of others' models recast in this frame, with numbers from those studies. The authors offer optimality as a methodological device, not a claim about people, and the method lets constraints be refitted to data. The objective is per episode, with no terms for storing, retrieving or reusing a result, or for its going stale. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-375](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-375.md) | In one simulator evicting whole query-shaped cache regions, no replacement value function was best on every workload: a value based on distance from the current query beat LRU where queries clustered around a hot region or wandered with loops, while MRU beat both, by up to 2.3 times, on regular cyclic paths larger than the cache; none of the functions weighs what a region would cost to fetch again, and nothing is proved | Dar, Franklin, Jónsson, Srivastava and Tan (1996), [LIT-1113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1113.md), read in [NOTE-904](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-904.md). With semantic regions as the unit of eviction, Manhattan distance from the most recent query beat LRU at every query size on a skewed selection workload, and a directional variant was best or tied on random map paths (LRU within 1.06) and on lollipop paths circling a square five or more times; MRU won on a single circuit and on plain squares (Manhattan 2.29 and LRU 9.57 on the 32 × 32 square). The study is simulation only, with synthetic paths and no refetch cost in any value; it shows that the best forecast of reuse depends on the workload, not that semantic distance is a robust rule. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-383](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-383.md) | On one Apache and Informix server answering cheap indexed selections, a page whose query result was stored in the DBMS and refreshed on every update answered more slowly than one recomputed on each request whenever updates arrived, because reading the stored result cost about as much as recomputing it and its refresh loaded the same DBMS, while a finished page stored at the web server and rewritten on every update answered 10 to 230 times faster than either | Labrinidis and Roussopoulos (2000), [LIT-1118](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1118.md), read in [NOTE-908](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-908.md). Three ways to serve a database-generated page under online updates, with no stale reads allowed: compute on request, store the query result in the DBMS, or store the finished page at the web server. A cost model sums access and update costs by frequency; the per-page selection problem is stated and not solved. On their testbed the page stored at the web server won at every load, and the result stored in the DBMS lost to recomputation once there were updates. The reading the evidence does not support: that storing an answer pays whenever it is reused enough. Where it is stored decided the outcome, and the generalization to other systems is the authors' expectation, not a measurement. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-402](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-402.md) | Collective intelligence is resource-bounded computation with a larger but modular budget: a group has more sensing, state, processing and action than any member, and pays coordination and cooperation costs because those resources sit in autonomous members, so the same trade-off yields groups that do better than their members on some tasks, groups that run qualitatively different algorithms, and groups that do worse | Pilgrim et al. (2025), [LIT-046](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-046.md), read in [NOTE-055](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-055.md), with Dreyer et al. (2024), [LIT-075](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-075.md) ([NOTE-040](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-040.md)), as its clearest instance. The paper offers a four-dimensional resource inventory, a catalogue of constraints and a mapping to mechanisms, and calls the known forms of collective intelligence "aspects of a single unifying principle". [NOTE-055](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-055.md) judges it a vocabulary, not a derivation: the resources have no metric, so the framework cannot say in advance when costs outweigh gains, and its "predictions" are research questions. Filed Proposed as the account the vocabulary states. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-406](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-406.md) | Self-presentations that differ by audience coexist without trouble while the audiences are kept apart by spatial, social and temporal boundaries, and collide when a medium removes the boundaries; networked publics make the collision frequent and often unseen by the person it happens to | boyd (2008), [LIT-1001](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1001.md), after Meyrowitz (1985), read in part in [NOTE-710](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-710.md) (Skimmed: §1.5, §4.4, the Top Friends passage and every passage on context, segmentation, collision and Goffman). An ethnography of US teenagers in 2004–2008: the dynamic is documented with interviews and examples, not measured, and the paradigm case, Stokely Carmichael's two rhetorical styles, reaches the record secondhand through Meyrowitz, who is unread. Proposed because it rests on a skim and on unmeasured evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-409](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-409.md) | A person's mind is normally a system of parts that take protective roles, managers, exiles and firefighters, forced on them by experience and not part of their nature; beneath the parts is a Self, distinct from all of them and present from the start, which appears with calm, curiosity and compassion when the parts step back and which heals by leading the system | Schwartz, [LIT-579](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-579.md) (the IFS Institute's "Evolution" essay, read in [NOTE-453](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-453.md)) and [LIT-591](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-591.md) (Internal Family Systems Therapy, chapter 1 only, [NOTE-457](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-457.md), Skimmed). The model in its developer's words. Its evidence is clinical: clients' reports of parts, the founding "step back" case, and "hundreds of clients for more than two decades". No study is reported in either source, and the book's research chapter was not read. It is filed as the account IFS offers, not as an account the record has tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-410](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-410.md) | Brain–computer interface decoding does not show intentions to be causes distinct from their neural realisers: what is many-to-one realised there is a coarse cortical variable over single-neuron patterns, and each intention matches one value of it, so under proportional difference-making the evidence fits identifying the intention with that variable | Pernu (2018), [LIT-147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md), read in [NOTE-091](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-091.md). A conceptual argument that turns on an empirical premise the paper asserts and does not examine: that each intention corresponds to one ensemble-average firing value. Real decoders are not simple averages, and whether the mapping holds across sessions or subjects is not checked. It is scoped by its own footnote 1 to difference-making with proportionality. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-411](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-411.md) | In Sen's capability approach the weighting of functionings is left to public reasoning, and evaluation can still guide action without agreement on weights: where every weighting in an agreed range, or every view by its own argument, ranks one option above another, that ranking holds, so the approach is deliberately incomplete and yields a partial ordering | Wells, IEP "Sen's Capability Approach" (2012), [LIT-284](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-284.md), read in [NOTE-257](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-257.md), §3b; with Sen (1979), [LIT-289](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-289.md) ([NOTE-258](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-258.md)), whose index is already "a partial ordering" supplemented by "conventions of relative importance" (p. 219). The arithmetic is trivial and holds; the attribution of the intersection and ranges-of-weights devices to a particular Sen text is not given by the IEP, and the SEP ([LIT-283](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-283.md)) says Sen "has never explained in detail" how selection should be done. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-412](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-412.md) v2 | Driven matter tends toward states that look adapted to the drive, with no replication needed: of two outcomes of a system driven by a fixed external field, equal in internal entropy and in the probability of reversal, the likelier is the one whose formation absorbed work from the drive and dissipated it more reliably | Perunov, Marsland & England (2014; Phys. Rev. X 2016), [LIT-518](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-518.md), read in [NOTE-416](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-416.md), on England's macrostate relation ([LIT-515](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-515.md)). The log-odds of two driven outcomes decompose exactly into an internal-entropy term, a reversal term and Ψ − Φ = −ln⟨e^{−βΔQ}⟩. The "tendency towards adaptation" needs the first two held equal. The paper does that only in two single-particle hopping models, argues the many-body case, and reports a driven-chemistry simulation without showing it. The reading judged the claim too weak to source a THEORY; it is filed as Proposed for that reason. "Adapted" here means absorbing the drive's work, nothing more. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-413](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-413.md) | 'Unit of selection' names four separable roles, interactor, reproducer, manifestor of adaptation and beneficiary, and being an interactor at a level does not require engineering adaptations at that level, so showing that a level lacks them does not show it is not a unit of selection | Lloyd's SEP entry (2005, revised 2024), [LIT-160](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-160.md), read in [NOTE-184](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-184.md). Her own programme, stated in the first person, and advocacy as well as a map. The four-question anatomy is the firm part. The diagnosis that conflating interactor and manifestor is "the most common error" is asserted, not counted. Its rulings on kin and group selection, the cheater problem and the Price equation are one school's, not consensus. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-414](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-414.md) | Institutions are rules in equilibrium, correlated equilibria of coordination games with several equilibria that the players represent to themselves as rules, and a constitutive rule 'X counts as Y in C' is a regulative rule split by a coined term into a base rule and a status rule, so the term adds a name and cognitive economy but no new kind of fact | Hindriks & Guala (2015, online 2014), [LIT-481](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-481.md), read with the authors' reply to six commentators in [NOTE-395](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-395.md). The equilibrium half is a clear synthesis of Lewis, Aumann, Aoki and Greif. The reduction of Searle's constitutive rules is worked once, for a toy first-occupancy property, and asserted in general; it depends on a reading of "collective acceptance" loose enough to make the "counts as" biconditionals hold by construction, and on extensional equivalence of behaviour. The reply adds that a right is a bundle of others' regulative obligations. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-415](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-415.md) | Nothing has all four marks that qualia are said to have, being ineffable, intrinsic, private and directly apprehensible, because neither the subject nor an outside tester can tell a change in a quale from a change in the subject's reactions to it; what is real in their place is the practical ineffability and idiosyncrasy of information-rich property detection | Dennett (1988), [LIT-433](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-433.md), read in full in [NOTE-357](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-357.md). Argued by fifteen intuition pumps, not by proof, and the author says so. The central step rests on a stipulation that two surgeries, or two adaptation stories, produce identical introspective effects. [NOTE-357](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-357.md) filed no THEORY because the record does not hold the replies (Shoemaker 1981, Block 1980); this account states the claim as the reading supports it and leaves it Proposed for that reason. Its "there simply are no qualia at all" is a tactical choice of words by the author's endnote 2. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-416](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-416.md) | Quantum thermodynamics has at least four inequivalent notions of work, the ensemble average, the two-point-measurement random variable, the ε-deterministic single-shot work content and the resource-theory work, which answer different operational questions; only the two single-shot optima coincide, by identification of formulas and for energy-diagonal states | Vinjanampathy & Anders (2015/16), [LIT-010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-010.md), read in full in [NOTE-011](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-011.md). The review's one synthesis (§5.2, §7) sets four definitions side by side: ⟨W⟩ = ∫tr[ρḢ]dt (Eq. 2), W = E_m^(τ) − E_n^(0) (Eq. 24), A^ε ≈ −kT ln(Z_Λ*/Z) (Eq. 49) and w^max_ε = F^min_ε(ρ_S) − F(τ_S) (Eq. 50). Only the last two agree, and that agreement is an observation that two published formulas match, for states diagonal in energy. It is an informed judgement of a 2016 snapshot, not a theorem that the notions cannot be unified. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-418](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-418.md) | A collective becomes a new level of individuality, on this sketch, only when collaboration toward a shared goal, rather than coordination or cooperation, organizes it and some core interactions have become generatively entrenched so that it has organizational closure; such a community can then be reproduced only by exporting an organized sample of its roles and interactions, not of its members alone | Griesemer & Shavit (2023), [LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), read in [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md). A conceptual sketch, so called by its authors, with no model, data or operational criteria. The paper's two headline claims, that it describes evolutionary transitions non-circularly and that individuality is a special case of collectivity, appear only in the abstract and are not argued. Stage 3 is defined partly by a shared goal and a sense of belonging, which presuppose the group. The one argued conclusion, that inheritance at the new level evolves "in tandem", is hedged and in tension with §2. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-423](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-423.md) | Statements that are visibly false to anyone who checks, such as 'long-term' for a three-day study or 'assault' contradicted by video, persist in science, paid testimony and official statements when the community that hears them accepts them as terms of art and attaches no cost to them, so that those willing to make things up gain over those who are not | Gelman (2025), [LIT-014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-014.md), a blog post its author calls a rant, read in [NOTE-019](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-019.md). An incentive account from three to five anecdotes: false phrasing helps a case, a channel (journals, courts, media) carries it, insiders treat it as a term of art, and nothing follows, so by a Gresham's-law dynamic honest argument loses. Nothing is measured, and the post is inconsistent on whether the speakers know they are lying. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-426](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-426.md) | Evaluating expected free energy recursively over the beliefs an agent would hold after each plausible outcome makes active inference a pruned tree search over belief states, formally analogous to Bellman recursion, which lets the agent plan through short-term costs that one-step agents cannot; that the pruning keeps deep search tractable beyond toy problems is argued, not shown | Friston, Da Costa, Hafner, Hesp & Parr (2020), [LIT-577](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-577.md), read in [NOTE-454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-454.md) as prose: the equations were not recoverable from the text layer. The recursion is a construction (strong). That it plans through costs rests on single deterministic runs of a T-maze and an 8 × 8 maze. [NOTE-454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-454.md) declined a THEORY because the results are a construction plus illustrations; this one is filed Proposed under the owner's ruling, stating only the claim the reading supports. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-428](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-428.md) | A protest performed bodily inside a civic ritual can contest the ritual in its own grammar, keeping the ritual's reverence for its ideal while rebuking its present object, which is incivility in the Confucian sense of disruption aimed at harmonization; the reading of the gesture and the claim that its uptake makes it sagely are asserted | Walsh (2021), [LIT-209](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-209.md), read in [NOTE-164](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-164.md) from the accepted manuscript. Comparative-philosophy interpretation of Kaepernick's kneeling during the U.S. anthem. Its textual base is strong: classical Confucianism licenses incivility aimed at harmonization (after Kim 2011). Its own addition, that such incivility can be bodily and within the ritual, is moderately argued. That kneeling means reverence rather than defiance, and that sagely authority is uptake by others, are asserted, and the paper gives no criterion separating sagely uptake from virality. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-429](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-429.md) | Institutions are the humanly devised formal and informal constraints on interaction; with technology they fix the costs of transacting, organisations arise to exploit the opportunities they offer, and an economy grows when its framework rewards productive rather than redistributive activity, while increasing returns to the institutional matrix make frameworks path dependent, so that economies with different frameworks diverge and need not converge | North (1991), [LIT-489](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-489.md), read in full in [NOTE-392](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-392.md). A programmatic essay, not an argument. The definition is stipulated; the game-theoretic motive for third-party enforcement is one paragraph; the evidence is narrative history from secondary sources, with the staged sequence of exchange disclaimed as history (n. 1); path dependence is carried over from Arthur and David on technology by analogy. It leaves open why informal constraints bind, which is the question Hindriks and Guala put to rules accounts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-432](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-432.md) v2 | In Lévi-Straussian analysis of myth the group of transformations is not given by the material: which variants count as transforms of which, and by what operation, is cut by the analyst from a continuum, unlike transformations that develop an initial form by a rule, and the computational encodings of the method confirm this by taking the analyst's table of oppositions as input | Descola (2016), [LIT-822](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-822.md), read in [NOTE-641](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-641.md), distinguishes a Goethean regime (variants developed from an initial form by a rule, as in kinship) from a Thompsonian one (deformation between given forms, as in myth), and cites Lévi-Strauss's own admission that the myth group is a continuum the analyst cuts. Santucci, Doja and Capocchi (2020), [LIT-807](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-807.md), read in [NOTE-632](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-632.md), implement the method and concede that every inverse or opposite term "is not obtained from the software system". A keynote's argument and a software paper's concession; no test of the claim exists in the record. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-433](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-433.md) | Whether a machine thinks is best replaced by whether a digital computer can play the imitation game as well as a man, because the reasons for withholding thought from a machine that does would equally withhold it from other people, whose thinking we also infer from what they say; the objections from consciousness, mathematical limits and informality of behaviour fail on that test or rest on unproved premises | Turing (1950), [LIT-394](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-394.md), read in [NOTE-355](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-355.md). The imitation game is offered in place of a definition of thinking, not as a test of it, and Turing says he has "no very convincing arguments of a positive nature". The account's force is the other-minds parity of §6.4, which assumes, as §2 states and does not argue, that the machine's best strategy is to answer as a man would; a machine built to imitate human output is the case that assumption does not cover. It makes no claim about consciousness. Proposed, and a rival of Block's psychologism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-434](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-434.md) | Rawls's theory of justice is transcendental only in the formal sense that its principles state when a society is perfectly just; it already yields comparative judgements, prescribes no single set of institutions and sits inside a revisable reflective equilibrium, so Sen's case against 'transcendental institutionalism' misses Rawls, and what it shows is that the theory is incomplete, not that a new paradigm is needed | Valentini (2010), [LIT-290](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-290.md), read in [NOTE-262](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-262.md) from the 2010 working paper, with Zwolinski's review ([LIT-286](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-286.md), [NOTE-261](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-261.md)), which agrees with her on what the book says and disagrees on its worth. A one-sided Rawlsian rebuttal: two points are strong as textual claims (Rawls's principles are comparative; his method is reflective equilibrium), the rest moderate. The claims about *The Idea of Justice* are second-hand, and Sen's own reply is unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-436](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-436.md) | Pain is a functional state of a whole organism, possessing a certain functional organisation as a probabilistic automaton, rather than a brain state, and this is the more plausible empirical hypothesis because one pain predicate applies to physically different organisms; the hypothesis keeps swarms out only by a stipulated condition that no pain-feeler has parts that separately possess the organisation | Putnam (1967), [LIT-396](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-396.md), recorded as Skimmed in [NOTE-335](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-335.md) from a course excerpt of the 1975 reprint, which carries the four-clause hypothesis verbatim; the original is Unavailable here. Proposed, and resting on that excerpt and on a result discussed throughout the literature the record holds. Clause (1) is empty by Putnam's own admission, since everything is a probabilistic automaton under some description, and clause (3), the anti-nesting condition, is introduced with one motive, to rule out swarms of bees. The argument against the brain-state view is comparative plausibility, not evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-438](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-438.md) | The understanding deep networks reach is characteristically fractured: it can be real, by the test of stable tracking under structure-preserving perturbation, but it is symbolically misaligned, non-reductive, locally fractured, proxy-dependent and representationally fragmented, because the loss rewards any predictive patchwork and does not press it to unify | Freeborn (2026), [LIT-131](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-131.md), read in [NOTE-123](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-123.md). The Fractured Understanding Hypothesis is argued from four small demonstrations and cited literature, with no test of how common the five features are. The abstract names three features and §7.5 five. The paper also applies its own criteria inconsistently: its Othello verdict uses post hoc probes that it excludes from the agent. The definition of understanding it rests on is an explication, not a finding. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-440](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-440.md) | A democracy that breaks down under an elected incumbent need not become a dictatorship: elections, courts and a legal opposition can continue while the incumbent uses state power against opponents and tilts the field, giving competitive authoritarianism, in which competition is real but unfair and the decisive loss is the opposition that withdraws or never forms; Levitsky and Way forecast this for the second Trump term | Drezner (2025), [LIT-022](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-022.md), an opinion column read in [NOTE-001](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-001.md), which relays Levitsky and Way's Foreign Affairs forecast largely by quotation and endorses it ("hard to disagree") without independent argument. The concept of competitive authoritarianism is theirs and well established; the record holds it only through this relay. The forecast that US democracy will "likely break down" in the second term is rated weak in the reading, and the post's index figures are second-hand. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-442](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-442.md) | Where the non-epistemic consequences of error are foreseeable, sound scientific reasoning requires weighing them in the internal choices that carry inductive risk, and non-epistemic values then enter legitimately only indirectly, through the costs of error, never as reasons to think a claim true | Douglas (2000), [LIT-139](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-139.md), read in [NOTE-145](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-145.md). The normative half of the paper. It rests on a premise the paper declares "beyond the scope" and does not argue, that scientists are morally responsible for foreseeable consequences of error (p. 563). The direct/indirect line is drawn sharply in the conclusion but only sketched, and the reply that scientists could report uncertainty instead of accepting is not engaged. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-443](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-443.md) | Being a biological individual is not being an organism: evolutionary (Darwinian) individuality and physiological individuality come apart, and each is found among parts of organisms and groups of organisms as well as among organisms, so a part or a group can be an individual of one kind and not the other | Wilson and Barker (SEP, 2007; substantive revision 2024), [LIT-168](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-168.md), read in [NOTE-114](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-114.md). That organisms are not the only biological individuals is argued from examples; that evolutionary and physiological individuality is the most recognised distinction is a survey judgement. The nine-region framework that places each case is the authors' own and tentative, and its figures draw as disjoint the categories the text says overlap. It offers no criterion of parthood and leaves holobionts open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-444](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-444.md) | To mean something by an utterance, in the non-natural sense, is to intend it to produce an effect in an audience by means of the audience's recognition of that intention, where the recognition is meant to be a reason for the effect and not merely its cause; an intention to produce the effect, or to have it recognised, is not enough | Grice (1957), [LIT-1042](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1042.md), read in full in [NOTE-735](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-735.md). The analysis is reached by counterexamples to weaker conditions (the handkerchief, Herod and Salome, the photograph against the drawing) and stated "roughly". It is an analysis of speaker meaning on an occasion, not of illocutionary acts, and its extension to timeless and sentence meaning is "a first shot" with the red light admitted as awkward. Strawson's watcher case ([LIT-1043](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1043.md)) shows its three intentions are not sufficient. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-446](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-446.md) | Organism–environment reciprocal causation, taken diachronically, unrolls into an acyclic sequence of organism, environment and experienced-environment states joined by interventionist arrows; on that representation each niche-construction type has a characteristic causal pattern, and multi-species cases come apart only if organism and environment are kept distinct | Baedke, Fábregas-Tejeda & Prieto (2021), [LIT-110](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-110.md), read in [NOTE-111](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-111.md). A conceptual and visual model, worked by example for each type of niche construction and for two multi-species cases. There is no formal semantics, no completeness result and no empirical test; formalization is deferred. It sets synchronic co-constitution aside rather than refuting it, and the claim that the boundary is an "epistemic necessity" is stronger than the argument, which shows only that the model can draw one usefully. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-447](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-447.md) v2 | Granted that a person survives a brain transplant and that half a brain would do, each product of a division stands in all that matters in ordinary survival, so what matters is not identity, which is one-one and all-or-nothing, but psychological relations that can branch and come in degrees | Parfit (1971), [LIT-447](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-447.md), read in [NOTE-378](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-378.md), with the fission dilemma as Olson's survey states it, [LIT-454](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-454.md) ([NOTE-374](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-374.md)). The division argument is strong given its premises, and the premises are stated: brain-transplant survival is assumed, not argued. It does not say that connectedness matters more than continuity, which Parfit asserts for lack of space, or that a copy or a transcript is a survivor: the dependence q-memory needs is left "(whatever that is)". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-448](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-448.md) | On a substance ontology, a gestated foster that is part of the pregnant organism either is no substance, so that mammals begin at birth and the foster is not the later baby, or is part and substance at once, which leaves no consistent count; a process ontology keeps both parthood and foster–neonate identity, at the price of a count between one and two that it does not define | Meincke (2021), [LIT-142](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-142.md), read in [NOTE-115](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-115.md). The critique of the Parthood View under substance ontology holds on its own and is the paper's firm contribution. The positive view rests on five process-biology premises assumed for the sake of argument, and is programmatic by the paper's own word; "something in between one and two" has no formal content. It keeps parthood rather than rejecting it, and it draws no ethical conclusion. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-449](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-449.md) | If sentience comes in degrees, plants may be faintly sentient, and moral status is graded by degree of sentience, then plants have a partial moral status so low that animal interests outweigh theirs in most cases; all three premises are assumed, and the second rests on contested, second-hand evidence | Terrill & Veit (2024), [LIT-193](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-193.md), read in [NOTE-120](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-120.md). The conditional is valid; its premises A1 (graded sentience), A2 (plants may be quasi-sentient) and A3 (status graded by sentience) are assumed, and A2 is supported mainly by a popular book and commentaries. The paper gives no scale and no aggregation rule. It should not be cited as evidence of plant sentience, and the second author's later work leans against plant consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-451](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-451.md) | A singular causal claim, that C will contribute or did contribute to E in a particular setting, is warranted only by joint evidence on each step of the causal process there, its causal principle, its support factors and the absence of its derailers, which no single method supplies; a well-run RCT secures at most the study population's average effect, and often not even that rigorously, and its result is not by its method evidence about any other population | Cartwright (2021), [LIT-213](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-213.md), read in [NOTE-161](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-161.md). The point that RCT results are not by the method evidence about another population (save under random sampling from it) is strong and standard. That no method or handful of methods can warrant a singular claim is argued from the diversity of facts a causal-process theory of change needs, with one illustrative case. That such theories yield reliable predictions is asserted, with no track record; the paper gives no method for weighing the evidence and little on transport. The critique of RCT rigour is internal to the author's own reconstruction of "rigour". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-452](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-452.md) | A thing with many equally good candidate boundaries can be counted as one in two ways that cover each other's failures: supervaluation makes 'there is one cat' true on every precisification though no candidate is definitely the cat, and counting by almost-identity, meaning extensive mereological overlap, makes it true enough where the candidates overlap almost completely | Lewis (1993), [LIT-1015](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1015.md), read in full in [NOTE-722](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-722.md). Two answers to Unger's problem of the many, offered together. Supervaluation makes "there is one cat" super-true at the granted cost that nothing is super-truly the cat. Almost-identity, which is overlap and not similarity, makes the many candidates "almost one". It is not transitive and its threshold is left undecided. Each covers a case the other fails: Fred's house needs supervaluation, and supervaluation is natural only where the candidates differ little. It assumes semantic indecision, perdurance and no natural joint among the candidates. It has no metric, no dynamics and no threshold, so it is a precedent for counting by something weaker than identity, not evidence for any of the record's claims. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-453](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-453.md) | Basic physical objects can be nothing beyond the bearers of their relations: relations give them identity conditions wherever they discern them, and where nothing discerns them, as with entangled systems of one kind or points of a symmetric space-time, a primitive numerical diversity that is not a thisness suffices; general relativity's tensor and fibre-bundle formulations fit this reading but do not require it | Esfeld & Lam (2008), [LIT-895](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-895.md), read in full in [NOTE-695](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-695.md). Moderate structural realism: relations require relata, but relata need no fundamental intrinsic properties, and objects and relations depend on each other with no priority. Its distinctive move is primitive numerical diversity, which it says gives no identity of any sort. The GR sections show interpretive fit, not entailment. Identity is equivocal between §1, where symmetric space-times need primitive diversity, and §2, where the metric "completely determines" structural identity; the one concrete construction cited works only without symmetries and breaks the general covariance the view rests on. The no-priority argument assumes three options are exhaustive. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-454](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-454.md) | Perception is constitutively iconic, nonconceptual and nonpropositional and cognition paradigmatically discursive, and percepts are put to cognitive use only inside a 'cognitive envelope', the global workspace read as conceptualisation, where working memory holds recoded, task-dependent abstractions rather than the percepts themselves | Block (2024), [LIT-649](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-649.md), read in [NOTE-498](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-498.md): the précis of his 2023 book, not the book. The main thesis is stated and its arguments are in the book, unread here. The working-memory half is the update: nine cited lines of evidence that working-memory representations differ from perceptual ones and are task-dependent abstractions (moderate). The rereading of the workspace as conceptualisation rather than consciousness is asserted, not argued against the consciousness reading. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-457](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-457.md) | When people can choose their cooperation partners and have equal outside options, the stable division of jointly produced gains is in proportion to each partner's contribution, and partner choice selects for a genuine sense of fairness as proportionality | Baumard, André & Sperber (2013), [LIT-508](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-508.md), read in [NOTE-407](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-407.md), with its 28 commentaries and Response. The pairwise result is cited from another paper; the extension to effort and talent is unproven by the authors' own statement. The evidence is a reinterpretation of dictator, ultimatum, trust and public-goods results as allocation by entitlement. The authors disagree among themselves about whether purity, loyalty and kin care are moral at all. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-458](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-458.md) v2 | Within the minimal self, the sense that a movement or a thought is mine and the sense that I am its source are distinct and come apart, as in involuntary movement and thought insertion; on Frith's comparator model the sense of agency depends on a forward model that precedes action and ownership on sensory feedback, so failed forward monitoring would explain thought insertion and, by the same mechanism, why first-person reference ordinarily cannot misidentify its subject | Gallagher (2000), [LIT-453](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-453.md), read in [NOTE-377](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-377.md) from the preprint. A review with no new results: the dissociation and the comparator account are reported from Frith, Haggard and others, and the link to the immunity principle is Campbell's argument, adopted and left conditional. It is about the minimal self, not the narrative self, for which the review's own proposal is two paragraphs. It does not say which minimal self, embodied or reflective, the analysis concerns. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-459](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-459.md) | Exact duality between two models is incompatible with ontological emergence of one from the other, reductive or not, because a duality is an isomorphism and ontological emergence needs a non-injective linkage whose interpretation does not commute; the two combine only when emergence runs beside the duality, as along the radial direction in AdS/CFT, through an approximate duality, or as merely epistemic emergence | De Haro & Butterfield (2025), [LIT-199](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md), §14.3, read in [NOTE-178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md). A formal argument from equinumerosity and surjectivity, strictly proven for finite sets, with an argument on physical grounds for the infinite case (fn. 57). Emergence here is novel reference in the domain of application, a semantic condition, not an information measure. AdS/CFT is the exception only to incompatibility with non-epistemic emergence, not to "not indicative": on a theoretically equivalent reading, its "emergent gravity" "cannot be understood as ontological emergence". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-460](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-460.md) | Every leading reason to deny consciousness to current large language models except biology names a missing feature, recurrent processing, a global workspace, unified agency, world and self models or senses and embodiment, that engineering could add, so the case against current models is much stronger than the case against their extended successors; the one possibly permanent objection, biology, is the one the argument sets aside | Chalmers (2023), [LIT-411](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-411.md), read in full in [NOTE-345](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-345.md). A classification of objections as temporary or permanent, argued by naming simple systems that have each feature. The credences that follow, under 10% for current models and 25% or more for conscious extended models within a decade, are illustrative by the author's warning, multiply stipulated factors under a disclaimed independence assumption, and depend on "mainstream assumptions". Biology is set aside with a reference to earlier work. It adds no evidence about any model. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-461](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-461.md) | If a substantial class of mental states, interoceptive, affective, perceptual and bodily-agentive, depends on an animate body, then today's text-only chatbots lack them and their self-ascriptions of such states are systematically untrue, and users can engage them without false belief by make-believe, as a new kind of interactive, self-involving and blended fictional character | Roberts (2026), [LIT-207](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-207.md), read in [NOTE-157](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-157.md). The anti-realist half is a valid conditional whose antecedent, moderate embodied cognition, is assumed at prima facie strength. It covers body-dependent states only; footnote 8 allows realism about the chatbot as a disembodied thinker, so belief and reasoning are untouched. The fictionalist half shows the attitude permissible and apt, not required, and offers no evidence that users hold it. It is not a general denial that chatbots have minds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-462](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-462.md) | If commonsense knowledge includes defaults that later evidence displaces, a monotonic logic, in which an added axiom can never remove a theorem, cannot represent that displacement as it stands; Minsky's further claim, that no consistency-seeking logical system can carry commonsense knowledge, is asserted, not shown | Minsky (1974), the frames memo, [LIT-410](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-410.md), read in [NOTE-337](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-337.md). Its appendix argues that "logistic" systems fail for commonsense on five counts, of which monotonicity is a correct observation about classical logic. That no repair is possible is asserted ("I think such attempts will continue to fail"), and consistency being undesirable is argued by analogy. The reading says the memo is a source of hypotheses, not evidence; this account takes from it only the half that holds by definition and marks the rest as the memo's claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-464](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-464.md) | In the ethical questions that seem to turn on whether someone is the same person, among them prudential concern, responsibility, abortion, advance directives and the separateness of persons, the relation that decides is usually not numerical identity but one that comes apart from it, so the metaphysics of persistence constrains these questions and rarely settles them | Dufner (2025), [LIT-130](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-130.md), the SEP entry that replaced Shoemaker's, read in [NOTE-166](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-166.md). A survey that takes no side; the account is the reading's synthesis of what it reports, correcting a seeded summary that said the metaphysics "jointly settle" the ethics. It does not say identity never matters: uniqueness may matter for positional goods, and biological views support prohibiting abortion more strongly than psychological ones, without forcing it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-465](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-465.md) | Being reproduced does not entail reproducing: genes of multicellular organisms, like hearts, are reproducees with little reproductive autonomy and differ from hearts in reproductive causal control, and material overlap between parent and offspring is required of reproducers, which are whole life cycles, but not of reproducees | Bourrat (2025), [LIT-157](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-157.md), read in [NOTE-100](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-100.md). A definitional framework with no model or data. Both measures are recipes and neither is computed. The proxy for autonomy (conditional mutual information) measures resemblance given the environment, not the range of backgrounds the definition names, and the two recipes given for it differ. The overlap claim rests on a premise shown only for retroviruses, and the conclusion's "necessarily" outruns it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-467](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-467.md) | Rule-consequentialism that ranks codes by the expected good of teaching them to, and having them accepted by, new generations does not collapse into act-consequentialism, because teaching and internalisation costs favour codes simpler and less demanding than act-by-act optimisation, which therefore sometimes require sub-optimal acts | Hooker, SEP "Rule Consequentialism" (2003, revised 2023), [LIT-198](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-198.md), read in [NOTE-160](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-160.md). The view's leading defender argues that the collapse objection fails once codes are ranked by the costs of teaching and internalising them, plus the assurance and temptation effects of exception clauses (§8). The premises about human nature (children's partiality, per-rule cognitive cost) are asserted, not evidenced, and the incoherence reply holds only on the reflective-equilibrium route. An advocate's survey, argued and not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-468](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-468.md) | Morality is the set of solutions to recurrent problems of cooperation, so each of the seven cooperation problems game theory identifies yields a moral domain valued in every culture, and behaviour unrelated to cooperation is morally neutral | Curry (2016), [LIT-503](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-503.md), read in [NOTE-408](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-408.md), with its two tests, [LIT-047](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-047.md) ([NOTE-034](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-034.md)) and [LIT-496](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-496.md) ([NOTE-412](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-412.md)). The positive half has support: the seven are described as good wherever ethnographers record them, and questionnaire items for them form seven factors. The negative half, that nothing else is moralized, is the theory's own stated prediction (p. 40). No study in the programme has tested it blind, and where non-cooperative items appear, the programme's own data show them moralized. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-470](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-470.md) v2 | Platform decay of the enshittification kind is caused not by a change in the character of those who run platforms but by the weakening of four constraints that used to discipline them, competition, regulation, interoperability and the bargaining power of tech workers, so it is reversible if those constraints are durably restored | Doctorow (2024), [LIT-033](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-033.md), the crib of a DEF CON talk read in [NOTE-041](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-041.md). It keeps the three-stage cycle of [THEORY-150](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-150.md) and adds a cause: "Not because they used to be better people, but because they used to be subjected to discipline." Argued from examples chosen after the fact, with no counterfactual; most figures are unsourced, and the text misstates the court in United States v. Google and the legal form of the EU Digital Markets Act. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-476](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-476.md) | If continuant persons are maximal aggregates of person-stages interrelated by the psychological relation R, then the relation of belonging to one person is R itself, so Parfit's premises do not show that identity is not what matters; the price is that persons overlap in fission and are counted by a relation weaker than identity | Lewis (1976), [LIT-446](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-446.md), read in [NOTE-373](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-373.md). Shown: that identity being one-one and all-or-nothing, and what matters branching and coming in degrees, do not entail that identity is not what matters, once stages and continuants are told apart; and that under supervaluation degrees of I-relatedness equal degrees of R-relatedness. Stipulated: that persons are the maximal R-interrelated aggregates. Conceded as costly: counting persons by tensed identity, which "is not a kind of identity". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-480](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-480.md) | Where a general-search monopoly was kept by exclusive distribution deals, the court in United States v. Google treated the user-interaction data that scale produced as the fruit to be remedied, and held that sharing the raw data and index metadata, but not the engineered signals and models built from them, can restore rivals' ability to compete without breaking the firm up; that the sharing will work is the court's expectation, not a finding | Mehta (2025), [LIT-006](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-006.md), the remedies opinion, read in full in [NOTE-004](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-004.md). The court finds that exclusive distribution produced a scale advantage (9× the queries of all rivals; 93% of unique phrases seen only by Google), calls it a fruit of the violation, and remedies it with raw data and syndication rather than with divestiture, on a sliding scale of causal connection. Whether the shared data will let rivals compete is untested; the parameters that decide it were left to a Technical Committee. The opinion also finds no proof that search scale gives Google's GenAI a quality edge (op. p. 156), which is an absence of proof, not a finding that there is none. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-483](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-483.md) | Whether a person joins a fascist movement in a showdown is decided by inner disposition, whether she is secure and has a standard of her own that tells her what she likes and does not, and not by race, nationality, creed or class; humiliation, fear, spoilt entitlement and measuring worth by success make a person susceptible | Thompson (1941), [LIT-055](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-055.md), a Harper's essay read in [NOTE-056](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-056.md). A typology argued through vignettes of an imagined party, from a reporter who had watched Nazism rise in Germany, Austria and France. No case is verifiable, the typology is applied inconsistently (two "born Nazis"; one man both never and qualifiedly a Nazi), and its denial that class is the criterion sits badly with sketches that are mostly about class. It is filed for what Thompson argued, and the empirical literature that tested such typologies is not yet read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-484](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-484.md) | The brain implements hierarchical reinforcement learning with options: dorsolateral prefrontal cortex represents which option is active, dorsolateral striatum holds option-specific policies, orbitofrontal cortex holds option-specific values, and dopamine carries option-level prediction errors at subtask boundaries | Botvinick, Niv and Barto (2009), [LIT-581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-581.md), read in [NOTE-451](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-451.md). Four proposed extensions of the actor-critic mapping, each matched to existing correlational findings, and predictions the authors say "call for further experimental scrutiny". The evidence for prefrontal coding of subtask segments is "only indirect". The mapping assumes pseudo-reward; other frameworks (HAM, MAXQ) would predict differently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-485](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-485.md) | Wave-function realism falsifies causal closure restricted to spacetime but is compatible with closure relative to fundamental physics, so quantum ontology opens no causal gap for non-physical causes; what it forces on the physicalist is a criterion of the physical and a bridge from dynamical to causal completeness | Poltorak (2026), [LIT-164](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-164.md), an unrefereed preprint read in full in [NOTE-112](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-112.md). "Every physical effect has a sufficient physical cause" has two tacit parameters, a domain and a completeness relation. With the domain set to spacetime the principle fails under wave-function realism; with it set to the ontology of a complete fundamental theory it survives. The move to a breach needs a premise that wave-function realists deny. The conclusions are modest and close to analytic once the terms are defined. The target is conceded to be a picture, not a published argument, and the dynamical-to-causal bridge is asserted, not argued. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-486](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-486.md) | For exact Betti Lagrangians in the cotangent bundle of a punctured surface, a finite creative spectral network exists, a point lies on its active walls exactly when a pseudo-holomorphic strip survives the adiabatic limit, and the Family Floer functor equals Gaiotto–Moore–Neitzke non-abelianization there | Casals & Nho (2025), [LIT-017](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-017.md), an unrefereed v1 preprint read in full in [NOTE-022](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-022.md) by a reader who is not a Floer theorist. Theorems 1–3 are stated for any rank and for positive-braid asymptotics. The proofs cover exact Betti Lagrangians with finite creative networks; the meromorphic case adds hypotheses in prose, and the Family Floer functor is not built there. The analytic core is taken by citation from Ekholm 2007, which the authors patch, and from the second author's own preprint. Theorem 5, on networks from Demazure weaves, has no written proof and is not part of this account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-487](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-487.md) | Social ontology asks two separable questions about a social category: what grounds a fact of that kind, the conditions something must meet, and what anchors those conditions, the facts that put them in place; theories of the field, such as convention, collective acceptance and practice, answer the second, and a theory can be individualist about one and not the other | Epstein (2018; rev. 2024), the SEP entry Social Ontology, [LIT-487](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-487.md), read in [NOTE-393](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-393.md) with the author's précis of The Ant Trap ([LIT-478](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-478.md), otherwise unread). A survey organised by its author's own distinction, likened to semantics and metasemantics. It rests on a survey that reports the dissents (Hawley, Schaffer, Haslanger) in a sentence each and argues the distinction by example. Whether anchoring is a relation distinct from grounding is reported as the author's view and as disputed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-488](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-488.md) | Russian military writers of 2015–2020 use 'hybrid war' for a category of war marked off by its objective, reshaping a target state's governance, geostrategic orientation and worldview, in which every action up to conventional military force is subordinate to an information campaign, and not, as in Western usage, for a set of means below the threshold of armed conflict | Clark (2020), [LIT-023](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-023.md), an ISW report read in [NOTE-012](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-012.md). A synthesis of open Russian military journals, official press and speeches, 2015–2020, with no stated method for choosing sources; the definition is the author's synthesis of several writers, not a doctrinal text. The reading rates the definition moderate, the claim that it is institutional weak to moderate, and the US policy recommendations advocacy. Written before the 2022 invasion. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-490](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-490.md) v2 | What a chat agent's 'I' refers to is fixed by the context of use, not by the system: the agent role-plays characters that carry the self-conception the corpus and the conversation give them, and its uses of 'I' can pick out the model, present in many simultaneous instances, or the single conversation, none of them the self by nature | Shanahan (2025), [LIT-466](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-466.md), read in [NOTE-376](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-376.md), with Shanahan, McDonell and Reynolds (2023), [LIT-460](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-460.md), read for the self in [NOTE-370](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-370.md). The candidate sites of an LLM's "I", and the fact that a conversation-bound self is literally a transcript and a program, are solid. That both the model and the conversation are legitimate referents rests on two invented usages. It does not say that there is "no-one at home" or that no candidate is a self, which the papers assert without a criterion, and its subject is a 2024-vintage chat agent without tools or memory across conversations. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-491](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-491.md) | Of the five standard arguments that randomisation gives a clinical trial special evidential weight, only the selection-bias argument is sound, and it supports only taking allocation out of the experimenters' hands; given balance on plausible confounders, a placebo or active control and blinding, randomisation is argued to add nothing, since balance on unknown confounders is not even probable in the one division a trial makes | Worrall (2007), [LIT-175](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-175.md), read in [NOTE-126](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-126.md). The case against the unknown-confounders argument is conceptual: frequentist balance is a long-run claim about repeated divisions, and a trial divides once. It does not show that randomised designs are no more reliable in practice than matched ones, and the meta-research cited is mixed. The selection-bias argument is conceded as "cast-iron", so the account does not say randomisation is worthless. Haphazard allocation is asserted to serve as well, without discussing whether such rules are predictable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-492](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-492.md) | Life was forced into existence by geochemistry: core metabolism, rooted in the reductive citric-acid cycle, formed as a channel relieving the free-energy stresses abiotic processes keep building, as lightning relieves a charge separation, so its early steps would recur on any similar planet and selection on metabolism came before replication | Morowitz & Smith (2006 working paper; Complexity 2007), [LIT-528](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-528.md), read in [NOTE-425](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-425.md). An essay with no calculation, which says itself that the thesis "has not been quantitatively demonstrated". Its evidence is the structure of present-day core metabolism, read back into its origin. Its framework is Jaynesian entropy maximization over states that include currents, and it rejects entropy-production principles. The reading judged that no THEORY was indicated; this one is filed as Proposed, a conjecture with a stated research programme. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-494](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-494.md) | Puritanical norms against harmless bodily pleasures are cooperative morality: people believe cooperation needs self-control, which indulgence erodes and discipline trains, and condemn indulgence as an indirect threat to cooperation | Fitouchi, André & Baumard (2021), [LIT-101](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-101.md), read in [NOTE-132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-132.md). In the authors' vignette studies (N > 1,100), perceived loss of self-control mediated all of the perceived effect of indulgence on cooperativeness. The rest is a review: disgust does not amplify condemnation once harm is controlled, and a society's valuing of self-control predicts its hygiene norms better than pathogen threat. The account is agnostic about whether the norms work, excludes contamination purity by definition, and has shown that people hold the belief, not that the belief made the norms. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-495](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-495.md) | The human sense of obligation is internalized pressure from a joint agent 'we' to do what 'we' expect of me; it appears around age three inside joint commitments, where children, unlike chimpanzees, protest, repair, take leave and share equally with a committed partner as they do not with others | Tomasello (2019), [LIT-125](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-125.md), read in [NOTE-185](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-185.md). A synthesis of developmental and comparative experiments, mostly from the author's lab, on WEIRD children and chimpanzees; no new data. The behavioural contrasts between committed and side-by-side play are moderately supported. That they reflect felt obligation, rather than prosociality or learned scripts, is argued, not shown. It explains the sense of obligation, not what anyone is obliged to do, as the author concedes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-497](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-497.md) v3 | A macro feature can supervene on a system's present state and still carry information about its future that no small set of parts carries, because supervenience is instantaneous and prediction runs across time; on the integrated-information-decomposition account a system can host such a feature of order k exactly when its dynamics carry k-th-order synergy about their own future, relative to a fixed partition into parts and a chosen redundancy function | Mediano et al. (2022), [LIT-025](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md), read in [NOTE-010](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-010.md), a review of Rosas et al. (2020), which the record does not hold. A feature V_t is causally emergent of order k iff Un⁽ᵏ⁾(V_t; X_t′ \| X_t) > 0, and a system has one iff Syn⁽ᵏ⁾(X_t; X_t′) > 0, split as downward causation plus causal decoupling. The review proves none of this and names no redundancy function. The quantities change with the partition, which the review calls intended, and they are predictive, not interventional, unless p(X′ \| X) is a do()-distribution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-499](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-499.md) | The breakup of the Eulalia parent body beside the Jupiter 3:1 resonance, 785–965 Myr ago, can plausibly have supplied the cluster of large lunar craters dated near 800 Ma, but only in the most favourable of five model solutions, with an average largest lunar impactor too small for Copernicus, and with the cluster's absolute date inherited from Copernicus alone | Bottke, Vokrouhlický, Dykhuis & Zellner (2026), [LIT-009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-009.md), read in full in [NOTE-002](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-002.md). A chain of multiplied factors (family fit, J3:1 influx, WISE incompleteness, collisional loss, impact probabilities) gives, for Solution 5 only, about 7,000 D ≥ 2 km fragments into the resonance and a largest expected lunar impactor of ">3 km". A Monte Carlo puts the seven ~800 Ma craters "generally" within 1σ. It is an existence argument, not an estimate: one factor is tuned by eye, only the most favourable solution is propagated, and the seven craters are dated by N(1) against one sample-dated crater. The Earth, Mars and Venus links are the authors' own speculation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-500](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-500.md) | Ventromedial prefrontal cortex stores links between kinds of situation and the body states they produced, and re-enacting those states when an option is imagined marks it good or bad, overtly as a feeling or covertly as a bias, pruning the options before reasoning weighs them; without the marks, choice under uncertainty fails despite intact knowledge and intellect | Damasio (1996), [LIT-384](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-384.md), read in [NOTE-332](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-332.md), the somatic marker hypothesis stated by its author; Bechara, Damasio, Tranel and Damasio (1997), [LIT-383](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-383.md), read in [NOTE-331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-331.md), the experiment it is usually cited for. The robust result is a group difference: in the gambling task all 10 controls and none of 6 ventromedial patients developed anticipatory skin conductance responses. That controls chose well before they knew, and that the marker causes the choice, is not carried by the statistics. The mechanism is argued, not observed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-506](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-506.md) | Every well-developed theory of how mind fits into the cosmos is bizarre, contrary to what most people confidently believe, and none is epistemically compelling, because common sense about the metaphysics of mind is incoherent; so no coarse position, materialism included, deserves credence much above 50% | Schwitzgebel (2024), [LIT-216](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-216.md), read in full from the June 2022 final manuscript in [NOTE-188](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-188.md); the published body text was not reached. Chapter 3's Universal Bizarreness and Universal Dubiety, with the other chapters as case studies. Bizarreness is an abductive generalization over the theories actually developed, with a standing challenge to find a counterexample, not a result about all possible theories. Dubiety rests on expert disagreement, the lack of any method and cosmological uncertainty, and the 50% figure is the author's judgment. The author's own credences lean materialist, at about 55%. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-507](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-507.md) | Any system with the same fine-grained functional organisation as a conscious system has qualitatively the same experiences, with natural though not metaphysical necessity, because otherwise a neuron-by-neuron replacement would yield either a rational subject systematically wrong about its fading experience or experience that flips with a switch nobody could notice; the principle covers only isomorphs, so it says nothing about systems merely similar in kind to a conscious one | Chalmers (1995), [LIT-392](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-392.md), read in full in [NOTE-347](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-347.md), with the one-page sketch in "Facing Up", [LIT-406](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-406.md) ([NOTE-336](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-336.md)). A plausibility argument by the author's own account: the fading- and dancing-qualia conditionals are strong given the replacement series; their rejection rests on a premise about self-knowledge drawn from familiar cases. It extends to a population of people implementing a person's neurons, so it rules out absolute anti-nesting for isomorphs. It does not reach any system that is not an isomorph of something conscious, which includes every actual AI system and every group. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-510](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-510.md) | How much of an ImageNet image a crop must keep for its label to survive varies widely by class, with architectures agreeing on which classes are fragile, and strengthening random crop raises mean accuracy while some classes lose 20 points or more; how many classes lose is not established | Balestriero, Bottou & LeCun (2022), [LIT-234](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-234.md), read in [NOTE-845](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-845.md). Six pretrained models on cropped test images keep some classes recognisable at an 8% crop and lose others below about 50%, and agree on which. Over 20 ResNet-50 runs, moving the crop lower bound from 100% to 8% raises mean accuracy from about 70% to 76% while "academic gown" falls from about 62% to 40%.
