The classes shown are hand-picked; the per-class test rejects for 4.4% of classes at the 5% level, uncorrected for 1,000 tests, which alone is not more than chance; and evaluation-set noise is not counted. Theorem 1 does not reach which classes pay. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-511](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-511.md) | Illocutionary acts that are not essentially conventional, such as warning, entreating and objecting, are individuated by a wholly overt, audience-directed intention, Grice's three intentions with a fourth that the audience recognise the second, and are performed when that intention is understood; acts such as verdicts and umpires' calls exist only within rule-governed procedures and fall outside the scheme | Strawson (1964), [LIT-1043](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1043.md), read in full in [NOTE-736](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-736.md), amending Grice (1957), [LIT-1042](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1042.md). Against Austin, some illocutions need no convention beyond the linguistic; their force is an overt intention meant to be understood, and uptake is the audience's recognition of it, an aim rather than an achievement. Orders fit "with some strain"; verdicts, umpires' calls and marriages do not fit at all. The scheme predicts no non-institutional case in which the overt intention is fixed and the act changes, which gives [QUESTION-073](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-073.md) a definite rival to test. The amended analysis is offered as necessary, not sufficient. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-512](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-512.md) | The extended-mind thesis worth disputing is that external entities partly constitute a subject's mental states in virtue of the subject's sensorimotor interaction with them; so stated it can reach standing belief but not consciousness, if consciousness needs information directly available for global control, since perception makes availability indirect | Chalmers (2019), [LIT-415](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-415.md), read in [NOTE-356](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-356.md), and his foreword to Clark's book (2008), [LIT-421](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-421.md), read in [NOTE-369](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-369.md). The 1998 thesis is satisfied by wired-in "extended circuits" that its critics accept, so the controversial thesis is constitution through perception and action. The perception-action boundary is then the strongest objection, met by revisionism, not refuted. Consciousness does not extend this way, on an imported criterion (direct availability, "not mediated by other mental states") and on the absence of any working twin case. Both halves are proposals defended against a few cases; the criterion is the author's earlier correlate of consciousness, not an argument made here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-514](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-514.md) | Self-maintenance through closure of constraints does not single out organisms, since colonies, holobionts, symbioses and ecosystems meet it too, so a persister criterion applied at whatever level meets it turns organisms into parts; what is proposed to mark organisms is that they can also induce, control and come through phases of destabilised organisation and reach a new closure regime, though that only organisms can do so is asserted | Baedke (2025), [LIT-167](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-167.md), read in full in [NOTE-148](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-148.md). The negative half, that persister criteria are too permissive, is argued from the literature: closure has been applied to symbioses, ecosystems and eusocial colonies, and Mossio (2024) concedes that "organized systems are not necessarily organisms". The positive half, the overcomer, is drawn "with rough brushstrokes" (p. 51) from three cases, two of which are lineage-level evolution or colony-triggered plasticity, and its uniqueness to organisms is asserted, with the one contrast (colony against ant) presupposing its verdict. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-517](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-517.md) | Life raises the Earth's entropy production, chiefly by increasing the absorption of sunlight, and if the planet is held at maximum entropy production, the negative feedbacks of that state would give the homeostasis the Gaia hypothesis postulates | Kleidon (2009), [LIT-519](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-519.md), read in [NOTE-423](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-423.md). The Earth's entropy budget is dominated by the absorption of sunlight, and model studies, mostly the author's, find that biotic activity raises it. The step to Gaia is explicitly conditional on MEP, which the same review says is not established, and its feedback argument is a schematic figure. It treats life as the most effective of the Earth's dissipative processes, and gives no criterion separating a living dissipator from a convection cell. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-518](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-518.md) | If a word's meaning in a distributional model is read differentially, as its relations to its nearest neighbours rather than its coordinates, then adding text moves every similarity value slightly but leaves the neighbourhoods of frequent, consistently used words intact and shifts those of rare words that the new text uses heavily, so the instability that holism implies is local and graded rather than total | Grindrod, Porter and Hansen (2024), [LIT-208](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-208.md), read in full in [NOTE-158](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-158.md). The conceptual reply to the instability objection is argued; the empirical half is four hand-picked words in two before-and-after demonstrations (a count model on Stein plus a Hemingway story; Word2vec on Wikipedia plus the SEP), top-10 lists, one run each, no metric. The abstract's proportionality of resistance to frequency is not measured, the criterion used (a preserved neighbour list) is not the one defined (relative distances), and static embeddings only are tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-520](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-520.md) | When coordination between two autonomous agents and the continuation of their encounter shape each other, the interaction gains an autonomy of its own, a precarious self-sustaining organization that lasts only while both agents stay autonomous; coordinating movement then coordinates sense-making, so some social understanding, such as recognising a partner, is a property of the interaction's dynamics and not of either individual | De Jaegher and Di Paolo (2007), [LIT-571](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-571.md), read in [NOTE-456](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-456.md). A conceptual account built on coordination dynamics, with illustrative evidence: the corridor, charades, mother–infant timing and the perceptual-crossing experiments of Auvray et al., reported, not new. [NOTE-456](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-456.md) declined a THEORY because the source carries no claim beyond its definition. The claim with some support is the perceptual-crossing one; the autonomy of the interaction is a definition, and the implications are called "speculative at this stage" by the authors. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-521](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-521.md) | In the thermodynamic limit, with examples and capacity growing together at fixed load, generalization error can jump discontinuously with the load when the entropy of hypotheses just above the best error vanishes faster than the training-error energy grows: a spherical perceptron's error falls smoothly as 1/α, an Ising perceptron's drops to zero at a critical load | Martin & Mahoney (2017), [LIT-672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-672.md), read in [NOTE-542](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-542.md), restating Seung, Sompolinsky & Tishby (1992) and Haussler, Kearns, Seung & Tishby (1996), which the record does not hold. Generalization is set by maximizing s(ε) − α ln(1/(1 − ε)). For weights on a sphere s(ε) ~ ln ε and ε ~ 1/α; for ±1 weights s(ε) ~ −(π²/2)ε² ln ε, the first-order condition has no solution past a critical load, and the error drops to zero. Uniform bounds that see a class only through its size or VC dimension are smooth and blind to this. That deep networks have such a phase diagram is the authors' conjecture, and their mapping of label noise to load and early stopping to temperature is an analogy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-523](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-523.md) | IIT 4.0's measure of integrated information is undefined for any system that has a non-Markovian graining, which brains are said to have under the grainings in use, and it has never been computed for a real physical system; so empirical measures such as PCI are proxies for it, not approximations, and their success is evidence for IIT's intuitions about integration, not for Φ | Barrett, Milinkovic, Mediano, Rosas, Bor, Barnett & Seth (2026), [LIT-185](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-185.md), read in full in [NOTE-122](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-122.md). A position paper by sympathetic insiders, with no new formal result. The ill-definedness is restated from Barrett & Mediano (2019), which the record does not hold. That brains are non-Markovian under typical grainings rests on one 1998 citation about ion-channel currents. The proxy point follows from a definition: an approximation needs a well-defined target and an error bound. The paper's defences of IIT (the multi-dimensional measure, the "proto-consciousness" panpsychism) are revisions of the theory, not readings of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-525](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-525.md) | In fan–celebrity parasocial relationships the celebrity mostly directs fans' identities and the fans mostly interpret the celebrity's, so a mass audience that refuses uptake of a legitimately presented change of persona holds one person's identity fixed, which is a failure of recognition respect that restricts the celebrity's agency | Archer & Robb (2025), [LIT-172](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-172.md), read in [NOTE-186](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-186.md). Three structural asymmetries (attention, communication, epistemic) yield an identity asymmetry, after Cocking & Kennett's directive and interpretive influence; on Darwall's and Lindemann's accounts, refusing uptake of a presented self is a wrong. Informal argument from one main case (Taylor Swift, 2018). The duties derived are fans' only, though the abstract promises celebrities' too. It needs a person on the far side, so it does not carry over to AI companions without an argument about their moral status. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-528](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-528.md) | The cases offered for extended cognition are explained at least as well by embedded cognition, on which the organism leans heavily on external props, and memory research finds that external stores lack the interference, generation effect and power-law learning and forgetting of internal memory, so a kind spanning both does no explanatory work and conservatism favours the embedded account | Rupert (2004), [LIT-422](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-422.md), read in [NOTE-343](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-343.md). The past-endorsement dilemma is strong: without it, directory assistance makes Otto believe every listed number; with it, the organism's endorsement is the final authority. The memory comparisons are moderate: the internal side is cited research, the external side is thought experiment, and no experiment on an external store is run or cited. The step from "different fine-grained kinds" to "no useful coarse kind" is a challenge plus conservatism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-529](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-529.md) | A state is shown to be a representation by adaptation for transmitting information efficiently, near the optimal trade-off of rate, distortion and coder complexity under a teleofunctionally fixed distortion measure, rather than by correlation or mutual information alone, which nearly any causal link supplies and which cannot increase along a processing chain | Martínez (2025), [LIT-149](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-149.md), read in [NOTE-165](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-165.md): a position paper with no new theorem or data. Its sharpest point is a standard result: by the data-processing inequality, mutual information about a car/no-car decision can only fall from retina to IT, so a mutual-information criterion would place the decision at the earliest stage; explicitness is better read as ease of decoding. The rest is a proposal supported by selected examples. Complexity has no operational measure, teleofunctions are needed to fix the distortion measure or every system is efficient for some loss, and misrepresentation and engineered systems are not addressed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-531](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-531.md) v2 | Told in the third person, a transfer of memories and character between two bodies reads as the persons exchanging bodies; told in the first person, no predicted psychological change removes the subject's reason to fear pain to his own body, and the step that completes the exchange happens only to the other man, so the two tellings support opposite criteria | Williams (1970), [LIT-462](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-462.md), read in [NOTE-387](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-387.md). The strongest step is shown given its premise: the last step of the series that turns amnesia into a body exchange changes nothing for the subject. The premise, that psychological change cannot remove the reason to fear pain, is argued from cases. Williams claims no criterion of identity, calls his resolution "rather shaky" and "risky", and does not treat fission. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-532](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-532.md) | Systems pushed from equilibrium develop structures that degrade the applied gradient faster, and living systems and maturing ecosystems are such structures, continuous with convection cells and vortices, so the second law is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for life | Schneider & Kay (1994), [LIT-533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-533.md), read in [NOTE-415](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-415.md). A "restated second law" (systems moved from equilibrium "utilize all avenues available to counter the applied gradients") is offered as a corollary of Kestin's equilibrium stability result and not derived from it. Bénard convection and a draining vortex show organized structures raising dissipation. One stressed marsh, airborne thermal scans and a satellite comparison are read as ecosystems developing to degrade more sunlight; all are correlational and confounded with water. The reading judged the claims too weak to source a THEORY; filed as Proposed. The paper itself says thermodynamics cannot tell the living from the non-living. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-533](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-533.md) | When a President can end a funding lapse selectively, paying the parts of government he favours from funds named by no appropriation, a shutdown stops checking him and instead hands him the choice of what to fund; each payment left unchallenged becomes a precedent, and a Speaker who lets it stand gives up his own chamber's power of the purse | Moynihan (2026), [LIT-061](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-061.md), a commentary post read in [NOTE-084](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-084.md). The memo of 27 March 2026 directs payment of TSA staff from "funds that have a reasonable and logical nexus to TSA operations", citing 31 U.S.C. 1301(a) but naming no account; that much is confirmed. That the payment is illegal rests on quoted scholars, with no GAO or court ruling, and the post does not engage the memo's own appeal to §1301(a). The binary choice it gives the Speaker is the author's framing. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-535](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-535.md) | Quantum systems read as bundles of property-instances with no principle of individuality can have their kinds and their number stated in quasi-set theory, so that N indistinguishable particles get a definite quasi-cardinal without labels; the construction covers kinds and counting only, not states, actualization or dynamics | Holik, Jorge, Krause & Lombardi (2021), [LIT-107](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-107.md), read in full from the preprint in [NOTE-127](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-127.md). The Lombardi–da Costa ontology of properties makes a quantum system a bundle of instances of universal type-properties, with no principle of individuality. Krause's quasi-set theory Q, reinterpreted over property-instances, represents an atomic bundle as a qset taking one instance from each qset of indiscernibles, guaranteed by Q's Axiom of Choice, and N particles as a subqset of quasi-cardinal N. The new formal content is about two pages (§6), the printed proofs contain errors, and states, actualization and dynamics are not formalized. The claims about Kochen–Specker and non-separability are recharacterizations by definition, not results. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-536](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-536.md) | A group agent's attitudes are real and non-redundant: each group belief needs members' role-based acceptance, by assent in the group's name or by acting on it in an executive role, but that acceptance does not explain or reduce the group belief, because which members' acceptance counts, and that it plays the role of belief, is fixed only from the group-level view | List & Pettit (2012), [LIT-730](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-730.md), their replies to an Episteme symposium on Group Agency, read in [NOTE-582](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-582.md). The claim is argued in a few pages against one commentator, Sylvan, whose paper was not read, and it points to the book ([LIT-391](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-391.md), unread). The authors grant that non-redundancy is a matter of degree and that the book takes the existence of group agents "mostly ... for granted". A position on explanation, not a proof, and not a claim that groups have experiences. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-537](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-537.md) | Warrant for a type-level causal claim in biomedical and social science comes from eliminating the relevant alternative accounts of its support, not from the kind of study that produced the data, so a randomised trial earns its standing only by eliminating many alternatives at once | Reiss (2015), [LIT-118](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-118.md), read in [NOTE-197](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-197.md) from the 2015 Durham working paper; the refereed version was not read. A conceptual proposal with one historical illustration, the 1950s smoking and lung cancer controversy, which the author says is not a test. What counts as relevant, and when to stop probing, is handed to context, and the four grades of warrant are admitted to be arbitrary. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-538](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-538.md) | A system believes and desires when its behaviour is reliably and voluminously predictable by treating it as a rational agent with the beliefs and desires it ought to have, and the success of that strategy is an objective fact though adopting it is free; the more richly a system is connected to its world, the fewer interpretations fit, so thermostat and person differ in degree | Dennett, "True Believers", [LIT-398](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-398.md), read in [NOTE-353](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-353.md) in the revised text of 1987/1997. The criterion is substrate-neutral and silent on experience. Its adverbs are not quantified, the lectern is excluded only by gain over a baseline the essay leaves informal, and the Martian argument is an intuition pump that assumes the intentional patterns are not captured physically. "Most beliefs are true" rests on a way of counting beliefs Dennett doubts exists. Proposed, and a rival of both Block's psychologism and Searle's causal-powers account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-539](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-539.md) | Moral judgment draws on several innately prepared intuitive foundations, at least Care, Fairness, Loyalty, Authority and Sanctity, each a response to a different adaptive challenge, and Sanctity descends from pathogen avoidance rather than from cooperation | Graham, Haidt et al. (2013), [LIT-499](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-499.md), read in [NOTE-396](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-396.md); its first statement, Haidt & Joseph (2004), [LIT-502](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-502.md) ([NOTE-400](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-400.md)); and the MFQ-2, Atari et al. (2023), [LIT-500](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-500.md) ([NOTE-398](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-398.md)). Pluralism has moderate support. The particular list does not: its evidence table gives Sanctity no primate or infant evidence and Authority no infant evidence, the foundations were matched to existing evolutionary models rather than derived, and the disgust findings behind Sanctity were later disputed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-540](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-540.md) | For moral purposes the body is bounded below by depth: objects whose real definitions are too microphysically committal are not body parts though they are parts in the ordinary sense, and bodily rights and interests concern only events that change the body's high-level properties, so a brain-computer interface user's implemented software can be a body part while the third-party server running it is not | Register (2025), [LIT-138](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-138.md), read in full in [NOTE-151](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-151.md). An argument from cases. It assumes that BCIs can be body parts and that no part of a person may be owned by another, and uses depth to reconcile the user's unqualified bodily ownership with the operator's property in the server. The two moral principles are its operative premises, and it says they do not depend on the real-definition ontology, which only explains them. The threshold for "high-level" is context-sensitive and unfixed, and the step that software and server are distinct coinciding objects is hedged. The conflict over servers is narrowed, not dissolved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-541](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-541.md) | A model of discovery or analogy that is given representations built with the answer in view has been given most of the answer, as BACON was with Kepler's data and SME with its solar system and atom, and representation-building cannot be postponed to a separate module, because which representation is right depends on the task and on the analogy being made | Chalmers, French & Hofstadter (1992), [LIT-414](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-414.md), read in [NOTE-359](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-359.md) from the preprint, with Burns's review of Fluid Concepts (1995), [LIT-457](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-457.md), read in [NOTE-375](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-375.md). The BACON critique is strong; the SME critique moderate, with no alternative encoding run; the two arguments against a representation module informal. Burns turns the charges on Copycat: its Slipnet holds the domain's relevant relations, and the symbol-grounding objection to SME applies to it equally. Nothing is measured in either text. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-542](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-542.md) | A word learner that infers speakers' referential intentions jointly with the lexicon, and lets words be uttered non-referentially, learns object names from child-directed video more precisely than co-occurrence and translation models, and mutual exclusivity, word-guided object individuation and intention-guided mapping follow from it without principles built in for them | Frank, Goodman & Tenenbaum (2009), [LIT-815](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-815.md), read in [NOTE-611](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-611.md). On about twenty minutes of video from two dyads, annotated by the authors, the intentional model's lexicon scores precision .67 and F .55 against .06–.15 and .10–.22 for five baselines. The behavioural fits are qualitative, the baselines also produce mutual exclusivity, and the Baldwin case supplies the intention rather than inferring it. The reading said no THEORY, because the findings are specific to a small corpus and the record held nothing they correct; this account is filed Proposed for that reason. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-546](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-546.md) v2 | A person persists by psychological continuity, not by sameness of substance or of the human animal; Locke's sameness of consciousness, which he leaves undefined, meets the charges of circularity, intransitivity and gaps when recast as overlapping chains of causally dependent psychological states with quasi-memory, and fission then needs either a clause against branching or multiple occupancy | Locke (1694), [LIT-464](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-464.md), read in [NOTE-385](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-385.md), with the repairs as Olson's survey ([LIT-454](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-454.md), [NOTE-374](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-374.md)) and Parfit ([LIT-447](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-447.md), [NOTE-378](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-378.md)) give them. Locke shows that same man, same substance and same person can be given different conditions; that the person's are those of consciousness he asserts and illustrates. The repaired criterion is the majority view in the survey, and its author, an animalist, argues it implies two thinkers in every chair. It is a criterion of persistence, not an account of what matters or of what we are made of. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-547](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-547.md) | A language model idealized as continuing any text with a plausible next word from the collection of all plausible texts follows narrative coherence and not truth, so its false statements are confabulations within the story the context sets up; whether trained and aligned chat models keep that nature is an open empirical question the idealization does not settle | Bottou & Schölkopf (2023), [LIT-178](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-178.md), read in [NOTE-102](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-102.md): an essay offering imagery, with no evidence beyond one Vicuna-13b transcript pair. For the "perfect language model" it defines, insensitivity to truth follows from the definition. That deployed chat models share it is assumed, and the essay's own §2 leaves open whether alignment can turn a fiction machine into a verification machine. It credits the machine with knowledge of what makes sense in the story, denies it truth-directedness and intention, and never uses the word "sycophancy". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-549](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-549.md) | A structured group is not identical to its members: two groups of one kind can have the same members at every time and still be two, which theories that identify a group with a plurality, fusion, aggregate or set of its members cannot allow, and a view of groups as realizations of structures with functionally defined nodes can | Ritchie (2013, online 2012), [LIT-479](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-479.md), read in [NOTE-390](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-390.md), with its 2018 sequel [LIT-486](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-486.md) ([NOTE-389](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-389.md)). Six criteria for a theory of groups, each defended by one example, rule out non-singular pluralities, Sider's fusions, Burge's aggregates and Effingham's sets; the decisive one is Coincidence. Groups as realized structures meet all six. The refutations are strong given the criteria; the criteria rest on single cases, and the positive view is a four-page sketch with no persistence conditions. It says nothing about agency or minds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-551](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-551.md) | The Russian narrative of a Western information war waged against Russia since the Cold War was politicised by academics, politicians and the public each for their own reasons, scholars promoting their ideas, politicians consolidating power and a public wanting its lost national pride explained, and not directed from the Kremlin; once adopted into rhetoric, doctrine and law, it drives behaviour whatever its origin | Fridman (2017), [LIT-088](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-088.md), read in [NOTE-070](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-070.md), traces the narrative to Messner, Dugin and Panarin and follows it into Putin's and Lavrov's rhetoric, the 2015 National Security Strategy, five laws and Levada polling. That it is present in official discourse is strongly supported; that its politicisation was not Kremlin-led rests on chronology that fails for Dugin, and the doctrine-to-law order is reversed for four of five laws. Clark (2020), [LIT-023](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-023.md), read in [NOTE-012](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-012.md), finds the same belief in military writing and also rejects the merely-cynical reading. The two share no evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-554](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-554.md) | On the grounds of moral standing now commonly accepted, together with scientific premises that are not unreasonable, the aggregate interests of insects or the interests of near-future AI could outweigh humanity's; no capacity yet proposed secures human priority, and the books that state those grounds retreat to moderate advice without a principle that supplies the stopping point | Schwitzgebel & Sinnott-Armstrong (2026), [LIT-166](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-166.md) ([NOTE-116](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-116.md)), with the SEP survey of animal moral status ([LIT-146](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-146.md), [NOTE-181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-181.md)) for the failure of capacity-based human exceptionalism. A conditional, defended as one: the reviewers "take no stand on ponens vs. tollens" (p. 6) and do "not endorse" the radical conclusion (p. 38). The scientific premises are called "not unreasonable" and not argued, so the account is only as strong as they are. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-556](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-556.md) | Clustering, abstraction and generative modelling can be how we come to identify natural kinds, essential properties and unrealized possibilities, but kinds, essences and possibilities are not by definition what such algorithms would find under ideal conditions, because nothing guarantees they are effectively computable; so an algorithm's output is evidence about a kind, neither objective nor vacuous, and not what makes it one | Watson (2023), [LIT-187](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-187.md), read in full in [NOTE-172](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-172.md). Three pairs of theses, one per task: the epistemic one (EC, EA, EG) accepted, the ontological one (OC, OA, OG) rejected, each on the same computability ground. The rejection is a bare possibility argument with no example of an uncomputable kind, and the acceptance is hedged ("or something very much like them") so far that it is hard to falsify. The pragmatic, context-relative view of kinds is asserted, not defended. Self-supervised learning and foundation models are outside its scope. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-557](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-557.md) | Low-loss paths between independently trained solutions are found outside supervised image classifiers: graph neural networks trained from different seeds on one graph are joined by quadratic Bezier curves where the straight line has a barrier, and one pair each of diffusion and contrastive models by chains of low-loss checkpoints | Li et al. (2025), [LIT-676](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-676.md), read in [NOTE-529](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-529.md): GCN node classifiers from different seeds, on 12 real graphs and synthetic CSBM graphs, show linear barriers that a fitted quadratic Bezier curve removes. Yao, Zhang & Tian (2026), [LIT-660](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-660.md), read in [NOTE-534](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-534.md): one pair of DDPMs and one pair of small CLIP models joined by chains of checkpoints whose training loss stays under a threshold, where AutoNEB's paths rise steeply on CLIP. The evidence is plots without barrier numbers in the first, one pair per model and retrained anchors in the second. Zhang & Blei's claim of flat paths between LDA's ELBO maxima ([LIT-677](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-677.md)) reports no results. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-558](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-558.md) | Moral judgment is usually caused by quick affective intuitions, and moral reasoning is usually a post-hoc search for supporting reasons that changes judgments mainly by triggering intuitions in other people | Haidt (2001), [LIT-511](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-511.md), read in [NOTE-403](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-403.md): the social intuitionist model. Its case rests mostly on non-moral evidence about automaticity, motivated reasoning and confabulation, carried over by argument. Its direct moral evidence is that harmless taboo violations are condemned and that affect predicts the condemnation better than perceived harm. The author calls it "a plausible alternative", not "an established fact". The disgust manipulations that were its direct causal evidence were later disputed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-560](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-560.md) | In rodents, gut microbes can drive stress and affect-related behaviour through vagal, immune, endocrine and metabolite routes, and faecal transplant from depressed people partly transfers the phenotype; in people, probiotics have so far shown at most small reductions in subjective stress in healthy volunteers, and strains with strong preclinical records have failed in controlled trials | Forssten et al. (2022), [LIT-915](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-915.md), read in [NOTE-703](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-703.md). A narrative review with no search method, by employees of a probiotics manufacturer, which documents its own translational failures: L. rhamnosus JB-1 had no effect on any outcome against placebo after "comprehensive preclinical evidence". The rodent half is well documented; the human half rests on one meta-analysis of healthy volunteers and trials with nulls. Proposed because the source is a narrative industry review; the gap it describes runs against its authors' interest. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-561](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-561.md) | If moral evaluation has thresholds below which effects are negligible, a system of agents can do good or evil that none of its members' interactions does, and the same thresholds make an environment tolerant of small evils and inert to small goods; on the examples offered the non-additivity lies in the evaluation, as a step function of summed impact, not in the actions | Floridi (2013), [LIT-901](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-901.md), read in [NOTE-698](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-698.md). A model with two moral thresholds and four positive examples; it proves nothing and reports no data. That morally loaded wholes can arise from negligible parts follows once thresholds are granted, and the reading rates it moderate. The analogy with distributed knowledge is inexact: every example sums like contributions, the threshold's value is left open, and so the line between distributed morality and a sum of loaded acts is a free parameter. Responsibility for such outcomes is not given here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-562](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-562.md) | In REST2 replica-exchange simulations of intrinsically disordered proteins, high swap acceptance and short round trips show that replicas mix along the temperature ladder, not that conformations are sampled, because the upper rungs collapse the chain; sampling shows only when independent demultiplexed replicas agree in their structural distributions | Koneru, Reid & Robustelli (2025), [LIT-076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-076.md), read in full in [NOTE-076](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-076.md). A how-to chapter whose one load-bearing methodological point is that high swap acceptance "is not, in isolation, sufficient evidence of robust conformational sampling or convergence" (p. 18). The reason the reading draws out is that REST2's upper rungs are unphysical Hamiltonians on which disordered chains over-collapse, so replicas can swap freely without the chain rearranging. The chapter argues this and shows a passing example; it shows no failed run, and its convergence criteria have no quantitative threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-563](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-563.md) | Consciousness is a real pattern in the brain's content-bearing states, a description that trades predictive accuracy for compression, and so coarse that describing the brain through it is metaphor; on that reading there is no Cartesian theatre, whether a given content was conscious can lack an answer when two descriptions compress and predict equally, and first-person reports are fallible as literal descriptions of the brain but authoritative as an author's | Taylor (2024), [LIT-461](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-461.md), read in full in [NOTE-379](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-379.md). An interpretation of Dennett offered as consistent, explicitly not as correct or as what Dennett meant. Its argument for indeterminacy in masking rests on Dennett's idealised description of the cases, which Taylor calls "somewhat simplistic". It does not say which real pattern consciousness is, or what makes a real pattern a conscious one rather than a belief pattern. Filed as the account the reading states, at the strength the reading gives it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-564](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-564.md) | A bounded generative model can learn its own structure with no machinery beyond inference and learning: spare hidden-state slots with flat likelihoods get filled when an observation fits none of the learned causes, and Bayesian model reduction on the learned prior over states can return unneeded slots, though in a toy concept-learning task it recovers the true number of causes only 45–80% of the time unless the likelihood is given | Smith, Schwartenbeck, Parr and Friston (2020), [LIT-615](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-615.md), read in [NOTE-485](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-485.md). Expansion works in the toy domain over eight runs per condition, and only for novel stimuli. Reduction is the weak half: over 100 runs, the true number of concepts won in 45–80% of runs for four to seven, never for two or three, and in every run when the likelihood was given. Table 1 is the record's only measurement of how often reduction picks the generating structure when the parent model was itself learned. One initialisation; eight concepts, six binary features. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-565](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md) v2 | From a symmetric, positivity-preserving, positive semi-definite affinity, the normalized Markov operator is conjugate to a symmetric one, so its leading eigenfunctions scaled by powers of their eigenvalues embed the data with Euclidean distance equal to diffusion distance, and a density-corrected normalization recovers the Laplace–Beltrami operator independently of how the data were sampled | Coifman et al. (2005), [LIT-981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md), skimmed in [NOTE-784](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-784.md) from extracted text whose displayed equations were not visible. The construction and the embedding are standard. The convergence theorem and the α-family are stated without proof, which is deferred to a companion paper. [NOTE-784](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-784.md) filed no THEORY for those reasons. It is filed Proposed on the owner's ruling that a well-established result may rest on a skim when it is not wrong as stated. Self-adjointness comes from the kernel's symmetry, and the paper's "directed diffusion" is anisotropic, not a non-reversible chain. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-570](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-570.md) | An emotional state is a large-scale selection of mental resources, switched on and off by Selectors that Critics trigger on recognising a type of problem, and so of the same kind as an intellectual way to think; feelings are the mind's descriptions of these cascades, and the body is one more resource the brain uses, not the substance of emotion | Minsky (2006), The Emotion Machine, [LIT-432](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-432.md), read in [NOTE-348](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-348.md) from the author's 2005 draft. A design argued from examples, thought experiments and the author's own AI programs, with no experiment; Minsky marks several parts as his untested conjecture. It disagrees directly with the body-state views of emotion and of feeling. On Elliot it proposes the reverse causal order to Damasio's, with no evidence offered. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-571](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-571.md) | A brain state is better characterised by how its activity moves among a repertoire of weakly coupled metastable substates on a landscape constrained by the structural connectome, their occupancy, dwell times and transitions, than by static connectivity; health is a metastable balance, depression a landscape of over-deep attractors and psychedelic states a flattened one, at opposite ends of one spectrum | Vohryzek, Cabral, Vuust, Deco & Kringelbach (2022), [LIT-080](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-080.md), read in full in [NOTE-054](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-054.md). A perspective that reports no data: the landscape (Fig. 6) is illustrative, adapted from earlier work, and no study measures depressed and psychedelic states on a common scale. The psychedelic evidence is small cited studies of broader substate repertoires and higher signal diversity; the depression evidence is three studies, one in remitted patients, though the abstract calls depression "excessively rigid". The modelling section is heavily self-citing. Proposed: a framing, with the record's rival description of the same dynamics as continuous in [THEORY-088](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-088.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-572](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-572.md) | Where an effect is not yet well conceptualised, replication cannot say which effect exists: direct replication bears on random error, conceptual replication presupposes that two operationalisations pick out the same effect, and an effect is delineated instead by probing for systematic error | Feest (2019), [LIT-161](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-161.md), read in [NOTE-196](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-196.md) from the PSA 2018 manuscript; the version of record was not read. An informal argument with one historical case, the Mozart effect, declared "typical" without further evidence. The claim that direct replication says "nothing" about systematic error is overstated: multi-lab replications vary some tacit lab-level factors. The conclusion is scoped by the author to effects not yet well conceptualised, and to internal validity; the title and abstract drop that hedge. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-573](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-573.md) | Signals of processing quality from different senses, such as fluency, familiarity and coherence, pool into one content-nonspecific feeling, and that pooled feeling contributes to the unity of conscious experience across modalities, alongside the integration of specific features; in support, coherence in one modality shifts judgments of regularity, familiarity and possibility about unrelated targets in another | Winkielman, Ziembowicz & Nowak (2015), [LIT-190](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-190.md), read in full in [NOTE-146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-146.md). An opinion piece whose main evidence is the authors' own three experiments (Ziembowicz et al. 2013), summarised without statistics and not read by the record. The authors state that direct evidence is still needed that the effects run through changed experience and that its integration is causal. No study cited measures unity of experience. The LIT is itself Proposed; this account carries its promotion condition. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-575](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-575.md) | 'Social group' names two kinds of thing: organized social groups, such as teams, courts and families, are structured wholes whose people occupy the nodes of an internal social structure, while feature social groups, such as women, racial groups and classes, are social kinds, nodes in external social structures, and are not concrete wholes | Ritchie (2020, online 2018), [LIT-486](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-486.md), read in [NOTE-389](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-389.md), building on her 2013 view ([LIT-479](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-479.md)). A social structure is one constitutively, not merely causally, dependent on social factors. Organized groups realize internal structures; feature groups are positions in external ones, which can be intersectional. A framework offered to "motivate", in the author's word: accounts of gender are shown to fit it, not argued for against rivals, and the work of excluding arbitrary collections is done by a restriction the framework imports. Silent on agency; the record uses it to say which groups the agency questions are about. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-577](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-577.md) | Our judgments that consciousness poses a hard problem are behaviour, so explaining them is an easy problem that can be solved without mentioning consciousness; and a theory that names a mechanism as the basis of consciousness owes an account of how that mechanism produces those judgments, which IIT and biological theories struggle to give, since a functional duplicate with zero integrated information, or in silicon, would make the same reports | Chalmers (2018), [LIT-425](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-425.md), read in full in [NOTE-354](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-354.md). The meta-problem follows from the physical explicability of behaviour; the challenge is a constraint argued from it, "not a knockdown argument". It assumes that a zero-Φ simulation has the same intuitions on a functional reading, which an IIT theorist can deny. The paper's own favoured solution, opaque introspective models attributing primitive relations of acquaintance, is "closer to a fleshed-out explanandum" than an explanation, and the data the programme needs mostly do not exist. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-578](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-578.md) | Between two trained networks that compute nearly the same function, a chain of models minimising the summed Jensen–Shannon divergence between neighbours, a discretised Fisher–Rao geodesic found without labels, can be a low-loss path where the straight line in weights has a barrier | Tan, Long, Zhao & Laine (2023), [LIT-662](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-662.md), read in [NOTE-521](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-521.md). Two ResNet-20s at 4× width with LayerNorm, CIFAR-10, permuted by Git Re-Basin's weight matching: the straight line between them still has a large loss barrier, and a chain of 25 models optimised from it to minimise Σ JSD between neighbours on unlabelled training images keeps train and test loss low. One pair, one figure, no numbers in the text. The hypothesis that every geodesic between SGD solutions is mode-connecting is stated, not tested, and a chain whose neighbours agree in output may be low-loss almost by construction. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-579](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-579.md) | If belief is individuated by functional role, an external store that is constantly consulted, directly available and automatically endorsed can carry a standing belief, so the material vehicles of some mental states extend beyond the skin; the step from coupling to parthood rests on that premise and a parity principle the authors state rather than argue | Clark & Chalmers (1998), [LIT-097](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md), read in [NOTE-180](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-180.md), with Clark's reply to the critics (2005), [LIT-403](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-403.md), read in [NOTE-363](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-363.md). Otto's notebook plays for him the role Inga's memory plays for her, so on role-functionalism it carries his standing belief, and Twin Otto, a duplicate from the skin in, believes otherwise. The constitutive step is carried by role-functionalism, the parity sentence and explanatory simplicity, none of them defended; the four coupling features mark a clear case and are explicitly not necessary and sufficient. Proposed: the step from causal coupling to parthood is the open point. The thesis is about vehicles of standing beliefs, not about consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-583](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-583.md) | An agent is the set of parts that pursue a goal together, bounded by the farthest events it can sense and try to regulate; cells joined by bioelectric coupling share measurements and so form larger agents with larger goals without ceasing to be agents, so a living system is many nested agents, not one, and cancer is the larger agent shrinking back to the cell | Levin (2019), [LIT-439](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-439.md), a hypothesis-and-theory essay read in full in [NOTE-341](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-341.md). A definition of the Self as a goal-pursuing collective, tied to a mechanism, gap-junctional coupling, from cited experiments on patterning and cancer. It has no model, no measurement of the light cone and no new data. Its goals are cybernetic set points, so any homeostat is a Self. Its Self is an agent and an individual, not a subject. The sentence against IIT's single Self is a bracket, and the closing remarks on experience are labelled speculation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-586](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-586.md) | The ψ-ontology theorems exclude only overlap of the distributions that distinct quantum states induce over ontic states; overlap is sufficient but not necessary for reading ψ as knowledge, so a model in which the state is ψ-ontic in Harrigan and Spekkens' sense can still have ψ represent partial knowledge | Hance, Rarity & Ladyman (2021), [LIT-090](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-090.md), read in full in [NOTE-072](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-072.md). The formal ψ-ontic/ψ-epistemic split is contradictory by stipulation, while the informal "ontic" and "epistemic" are not exclusive. So PBR and the related theorems bound the geometry of µ_ψ, not the interpretation of ψ. The paper proves nothing; its positive criterion (Eq. 6) is predictive incompleteness, and its Appendix A makes claims the record's readings contradict. The defensible paraphrase of PBR is "not ψ-epistemic in the overlap sense, given preparation independence". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-588](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-588.md) | Lemma-based models of language production build in a lexicalist assumption, and the failure is algorithmic as well as representational: as long as retrieval of stored word-sized units and building of syntactic structure are separate stages, richer stored units cannot handle polysynthetic words, idioms whose parts syntax separates, or suppletion conditioned by an unplanned object | Krauska and Lau (2023), [LIT-031](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-031.md), read in full in [NOTE-029](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-029.md). A Hypothesis and Theory article with no new data and no implementation. Its diagnosis of named models (Levelt, the Consensus Model, lexically sized increments, treelets) is strong as textual analysis; the case that they fail on Inuktitut, Vietnamese collocations and Hiaki suppletion is argued from a few examples each, and Eberhard et al. are conceded to handle Hiaki in part. The 8-stage replacement model and its aphasia predictions are a verbal sketch, and this account does not rest on them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-589](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-589.md) | No principle of mereology is merely a fixing of what 'part' means: even reflexivity, transitivity and antisymmetry face counterexamples that do not rest on equivocation, and every principle beyond them is contested, so classical mereology is one substantive theory among several and not a neutral default | Varzi, SEP "Mereology", [LIT-124](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-124.md), read in full in [NOTE-163](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-163.md). The entry's verdict, reached by surveying counterexample families: Antisymmetry "can hardly be regarded as constitutive", and most ordinary-language objections to Reflexivity and Transitivity equivocate, leaving the metaphysical ones. It is the author's informal argument, and he is a known extensionalist who gives that side the last word on extensionality. Its headline that "all composition principles turn out to be controversial" is stronger than its own verdict that bounds for overlapping things are "rather uncontroversial". It corrects the record's earlier summary, which called the partial-order core uncontroversial. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-590](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-590.md) | The self whose governance makes action autonomous is not the self whose persistence is personal identity: governance by an essence of volitional necessities would make action authentic, not autonomous; losing a defining care costs one's grasp of who one is, not one's existence; and wholeheartedness won by extruding a desire is a defence, not health | Velleman (2002), [LIT-292](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-292.md), read in [NOTE-268](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-268.md). A critique of Frankfurt's late (1990s) view that autonomy is governance by the essential character of the will, an essence that is also the condition of one's identity. It argues by counterexample (Winnicott's False Self, the Agamemnon sequel), from Freud's Rat Man, and by debunking genealogy. The positive view, that "self" marks reflexivity and that autonomous action is motivated in part by the understanding, is stated "briefly" and argued elsewhere. Frankfurt's reply is unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-591](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-591.md) | Cognition has two necessary marks, involving non-derived content and a distinctive kind of causal processing, and as a contingent fact only processes in the brain have both, so notebooks, screens and tools coupled to a thinker are not parts of cognition, and human-plus-tool systems will support no science of their own | Adams & Aizawa (2001), [LIT-438](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-438.md), read in [NOTE-368](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-368.md), restated against Clark in 2010, [LIT-455](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-455.md), read in [NOTE-380](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-380.md) from a draft. Both marks are assumed: the first on a claimed consensus, the second on how mature sciences individuate kinds. The authors grant the parity principle and that cognition could extend; the claim is that it does not. The "no science of tool use" half is offered as a bet. Rupert, the other critic, rejects the derived-content argument as question-begging. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-593](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-593.md) | Perceptual learning can install perceiver-specific frames that change which objects a perceiver individuates from the same input, so cognition can shape the perceptual system over time while leaving open whether any single percept is cognitively penetrated | Ivy & Mroczko-Wąsowicz (2025), [LIT-099](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-099.md), read in [NOTE-150](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-150.md). A conceptual proposal: a frame is installed by learning, often top-down, and then runs as a perceiver-specific structural principle of objecthood, so the system-level and episode-level questions about cognitive penetration come apart. The support is others' results reread through the concept, and one eye-tracking study of the authors'. The paper does not say what "bottom-up" means once priors sit in early processing, calls a frame "a specific top-down prediction" in §3.iii, and shows different weightings, not different objects. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-594](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-594.md) | Unitarily inequivalent representations in quantum field theory need not refute ontic structural realism: what does physical work in spontaneous symmetry breaking and in the DHR derivation of quantum statistics is structure across representations, so a structural realist who takes structure to be modal and to span them can accept that work, though the modal conception is undeveloped and the removal of Howard's premise rests on Baker's sufficient condition for intertranslatability | French (2010 draft; SHPMP 2012), [LIT-170](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-170.md), read in [NOTE-162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-162.md) from the unpaginated preprint. Every technical step is imported (Wallace, Earman, Ruetsche, Halvorson & Müger, Baker); the paper's contribution is interpretive and informal. The DHR result that statistics and charge kinds follow from the algebra is strong physics; that it favours OSR is French's reading. The modal "trans-world" structure is proposed, not developed, and the combined third option "obviously requires further elaboration". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-596](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-596.md) | To ascribe beliefs and desires is to predict a system by assuming it is rational and its beliefs mostly true, so a wholly false belief system has no coherent intentional description and contradictory beliefs no stable one, and the believer, like the person built on that notion, is an idealisation that real creatures only approximate | Dennett (1971), [LIT-440](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-440.md), read in [NOTE-350](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-350.md), and his reply to Stich (1980), [LIT-456](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-456.md), read in [NOTE-371](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-371.md). Belief ascription presupposes optimal design relative to goals, so "a false belief system is a conceptual impossibility" and, following Quine, the evidence for ascribing p is the best evidence against ascribing a contradictory q. In 1980 Dennett concedes the price: the intentional system, and the person, is "an unrealizable idealization". Argued from the logic of ascription and from evolution by assertion; no data. It is a claim about what ascription requires, not about what is in heads. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-600](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-600.md) | A definition of health and disease by social justice alone cannot fix what counts as disease: with justice left undefined, a majority with other values could medicalise what the definition was meant to protect, and unless medicine is fixed from outside, the category drifts until health becomes justice | Veit (2025), [LIT-098](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-098.md), read in [NOTE-097](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-097.md) from the PhilSci-Archive preprint. The target is Kukla's institutional definition: a condition is a health condition iff medicalising it would be best for collective wellbeing. The argument is informal and has two horns. One is a thought experiment (p. 14). The other rests on an asserted, undocumented premise about how medical tools evolve (p. 15). The extension from Kukla to "any purely normativist account" is asserted, not shown case by case. Veit concedes the first horn bites only without moral consensus. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-604](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-604.md) v2 | Most mathematical dualities are adjunctions between one category and the opposite of another, which become dual equivalences on their fixed points; what makes them dualities rather than equivalences is the reversal of arrows, so many of the 'dualities' physicists name are, in the mathematician's sense, equivalences or symmetries | Corfield (2017), [LIT-115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-115.md), read in [NOTE-141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-141.md). A short programmatic paper. That most dualities of interest are covered by constructions around adjunction is shown by worked exposition of standard cases, not proved. There is unlikely to be "a single monolithic account" (pp. 59–60). Reserving "duality" for structural reversal is a stated preference, and the verdicts on string dualities are a paragraph each. The proposal that philosophers of physics need homotopy type theory is an expectation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-606](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-606.md) | If consciousness words have meaning only through what is public, an entity is a candidate for consciousness only if an encounter with it in a shared world can be engineered, at least in principle; then disembodied chat agents, even with tools and memory, are not candidates, robots and virtually embodied agents could be, and beyond what an informed community comes to say there is no further fact about their consciousness | Shanahan (2024), [LIT-465](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-465.md), read in full in [NOTE-382](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-382.md) from the arXiv v2 preprint. A conditional, and the condition is the paper's method: a later-Wittgensteinian reading of consciousness language, summarised, not defended. The candidature test is stipulated and illustrated by the octopus and an imagined alien cube. The verdict on chat agents follows from it. Calling functionalism and identity theory "dualistic" is a definition, not an argument. The two passages on the self (no "self worth preserving", no "person behind the mask") are asserted and are not part of this account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-607](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-607.md) | The individuals that appear in an evolutionary transition in individuality are a summary description of lower-level processes, not a new level of fact: a partition of particles defines collectives when predicting at the coarse grain matches predicting at the fine grain across many traits, and collectives become indispensable, and so quasi-ontological, only because finite measurement and computation make the fine-grained prediction unaffordable | Bourrat (2023), [LIT-049](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-049.md), read in full in [NOTE-064](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-064.md). The formal criterion is accuracy only: δC = C_T − C_P < θ across many traits, conditioned on the environment where ecology could fake coherence. As written it is degenerate, since the identity partition gives δC = 0. The cost that is meant to stop that is argued separately, by a 100-operation toy, and never put into the criterion. Nothing is computed on any model. The abstract's "cannot be dismissed as merely epistemic" is stronger than the body, which says one "pretend[s] as if" the level of selection changed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-610](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-610.md) | What survives radical theory change in a mature science, and so what its predictive success warrants belief in, is mathematical structure, equations carried over intact or recovered as limiting cases, and not the ontology that interpreted them, as Fresnel's reflection and refraction equations survive into Maxwell's theory while the elastic-solid ether does not | Worrall (1989), [LIT-315](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-315.md), read in [NOTE-297](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-297.md). Epistemic structural realism, credited to Poincaré, offered as the one position that keeps both the no-miracles argument and the pessimistic induction. The support is one worked case, which Worrall himself calls unrepresentative because the equations survive intact, and an appeal to the correspondence principle with one further example. "Structure" and "structural approximation" are undefined. The view is agnostic about what there is; the ontic turn, Ramsey sentences and the Newman objection belong to later work. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-612](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-612.md) | Natural selection cannot be both a cause and an effect of a process such as niche construction: if selection is an emergent population-level process, niche construction partly composes it, and a whole and its parts are not independently fixable and so not causally related; if selection is not emergent, it is either no cause at all or incoherently individual-level. Niche construction can still cause the product of selection | Hazelwood (2023), [LIT-156](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-156.md), read in full in [NOTE-137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-137.md). A dilemma against strong reciprocal causation in the extended evolutionary synthesis, aimed at Laland and colleagues. Emergence is Wilson's synchronic dependence plus autonomy, cashed out as composition; causation is Woodward's interventionism with independent fixability. Its force rests on a process/product split for selection and a compositional reading of realization, both defended by citation and flagged as contestable, and its second horn considers only two non-emergent options. The weak sense, that organisms and environments affect each other, is granted as unobjectionable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-613](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-613.md) | The Moral Foundations Questionnaire-2's six factors, Care, Equality, Proportionality, Loyalty, Authority and Purity, fit across 19 nations, Equality and Proportionality are nearly uncorrelated in WEIRD nations, and the US split between individualizing and binding foundations appears in only three national networks | Atari, Haidt, Graham, Koleva, Stevens & Dehghani (2023), [LIT-500](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-500.md), read in [NOTE-398](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-398.md). 36 items, developed in 25 populations, fit six factors in 19 nations (ESEM CFI .979). Equality and Proportionality correlate .21 on average, from .47 to −.04. Purity alone fails intercept invariance, and it carries the headline that Purity is the least WEIRD foundation. The samples are online and about 200 per nation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-614](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-614.md) v2 | If pretraining text is a mixture of hidden Markov models indexed by a latent concept and a model fits that distribution exactly, then a prompt of concatenated examples moves the posterior onto the prompt's concept, and the in-context predictor becomes Bayes-optimal as examples accumulate, whenever each example's evidence for the concept outweighs the cost of the improbable transitions between examples; whether trained networks learn in context this way is not shown | Xie, Raghunathan, Liang & Ma (2021), [LIT-797](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-797.md), read in [NOTE-633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-633.md). Theorem 1 is proved under Assumptions 1–5 and a distinguishability condition; Theorems 2–3 give roughly 1/k excess risk without it. The proofs were not followed in the reading. [NOTE-633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-633.md) declined a THEORY because the result is conditional on exact fit to a specific generative model, so it is a consequence of that model, not a fact about language models. It is filed Proposed under the owner's ruling, with the condition in the title. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-615](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-615.md) | Stubborn distrust of scientific experts can follow validly from the truster's position: one with little say in collective decisions, who has reason to think the experts' service ethos leaves out their core interests, has a reason to distrust an expert because of the expert's prestige, whatever the expert's competence or goodwill | Desmond (2022), [LIT-158](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-158.md), read in [NOTE-113](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-113.md). A "how-possibly" argument, not a demonstration: a five-step scheme (§6, pp. 16–17) from status vulnerability and service doubt to distrust "in virtue of" prestige. The paper says it shows validity only. It leaves open whether the premises ever hold in a liberal democracy, gives no data linking status to distrust, and does not compare its account with testimonial injustice or the empirical predictors of conspiracy belief. The abstract's "justifiably" claims more than the body. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-616](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-616.md) | If a system has beliefs and desires just when attributing them, with rationality, predicts its behaviour well enough against rival theories, then the bearer of a language model's attitudes is the instance created by one context, not the model, the case that instances have them is presumptive and rests on tractability, and the best current desire hypothesis is helpfulness, honesty and harmlessness plus intrinsic desires a prompt installs | Goldstein & Lederman (2025), [LIT-206](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-206.md), read in [NOTE-138](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-138.md) from the preprint. Conditional on objective interpretationism, which the authors do not defend. The instance thesis is moderately argued; the presumptive case for attitudes rests on a tractability comparison never operationalised or measured; HHH+0 is "provisional", and its discriminating test is a conjecture. All the empirical support is second-hand and qualitative. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-618](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-618.md) | Neural circuits that must represent hierarchically organised states in few dimensions use a hyperbolic geometry, three-dimensional where it has been measured, because hyperbolic space holds exponentially many well-separated states within a small radius; the argument from Zipf's law to this geometry does not hold, and the evidence is two Betti-curve studies tested only against uniform Euclidean nulls | Sharpee (2019), [LIT-875](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-875.md), read in [NOTE-670](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-670.md): a four-page programmatic review with no new result, whose reading filed no THEORY because its claims are conjectures. Filed here as Proposed because the record holds two tests of the conjecture, odour statistics ([LIT-872](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-872.md), [THEORY-191](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-191.md)) and CA1 place-cell correlations ([LIT-876](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-876.md), [THEORY-192](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-192.md)), and no general statement. The Zipf step shows a shared exponential count of states, which any system with extensive entropy has, not a shared metric, and the rigidity argument for three dimensions cites Mostow's theorem, which concerns finite-volume manifolds and says nothing about noisy point clouds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-621](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-621.md) | Indexing each quantum fact to the system it is a fact for, and computing probabilities only between facts relative to the same system, removes the contradiction between the collapse and unitary probability rules in Wigner's-friend cases; the price is that values are not held at all times or by all systems alike, there is no global view, and no quantum state of the universe | Rovelli (2021), [LIT-177](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-177.md), read in full in [NOTE-174](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-174.md). For a fact a and exclusive facts bᵢ, the collapse rule Σᵢ\|W(c,bᵢ)\|²\|W(bᵢ,a)\|² and the unitary rule \|Σᵢ W(c,bᵢ)W(bᵢ,a)\|² differ by interference; RQM applies the first only when the bᵢ and c are relative to the same system. Decoherence makes some relative facts stable. The core rule is postulated, not derived, and inter-observer consistency gets one sentence. The chapter is expository, and several of its headline claims outrun its support. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-622](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-622.md) | Spatial boundaries are bona fide where a spatial discontinuity or a heterogeneity of material is present and fiat where they exist only by demarcation; the two obey different topologies, distinct bodies are never in bona fide contact, so any whole of separate bodies is a fiat object, and real properties of the material still enable and constrain where fiat boundaries can be drawn | Smith & Varzi (2000), [LIT-1024](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1024.md), read in full in [NOTE-721](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-721.md). A typology with a formal sketch: ordinary closure topology for bona fide boundaries, and a Brentanian theory of coinciding boundaries for fiat ones, which are parts of what they bound. The test is whether a discontinuity is there, not who or what made it. The theory is spatial, synchronic and pitched at the common-sense level; it has no models or consistency result, and the typology is stipulated by examples. It does not map onto the record's produced/imposed distinction, and it classifies the record's combined forms as fiat without choosing among them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-624](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-624.md) | Whether an identified system is an agent or a device can be cast as Bayesian model comparison between descriptions of the function it optimises and descriptions of its input-output mapping, so the verdict is relative to the observer's prior; on toy gridworld trajectories goal-seeking comes out agent-like and wall-following device-like, and some priors make everything look like an agent | Orseau, McGill & Legg (2018), [LIT-911](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-911.md), read in [NOTE-705](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-705.md). A formal version of Dennett's choice of stance: the posterior probability that a system is an agent, from mixtures of goal-optimizing (inverse RL) and input-output descriptions. Illustrated on seven gridworld trajectories, with no human study. It presupposes an identified system, and its verdicts depend on the prior; under the speed prior everything may look like an agent. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-625](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-625.md) | Institutional facts are status functions, imposed by collective acceptance on things that cannot perform the function by their physical structure alone; the status carries deontic powers that give desire-independent reasons for action, and it exists only as represented, so institutions require language; 'X counts as Y in C' is the common case of the more general 'We accept (S has power (S does A))' | Searle (2006), [LIT-482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-482.md), read in [NOTE-388](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-388.md) in its Papers printing, the record's readable statement of The Construction of Social Reality ([LIT-485](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-485.md), unread). Conceptual analysis, not argument: the three primitives are asserted to suffice, collective intentionality is referred to an unread 1990 paper, and the animal line is hedged. The paper revises the book: some Y terms have no X, and the general form is "We accept (S has power (S does A))". Hindriks & Guala's rules-in-equilibrium account is its rival on what a constitutive rule adds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-626](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-626.md) | Moral judgments are made relative to the social relationship an act is taken to occur within: each of four relational models (communal sharing, authority ranking, equality matching, market pricing) carries a moral motive (Unity, Hierarchy, Equality, Proportionality), so the same act can be required under one and wrong under another | Rai & Fiske (2011), [LIT-507](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-507.md), read in [NOTE-405](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-405.md). A theoretical review with no new data. Its strongest support is cited work on relational framing and on morally motivated violence. Which model is in force is read off after the fact, so the central claim risks being unfalsifiable as stated. Purity and ingroup loyalty are assigned to one motive, Unity, by argument. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-627](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-627.md) | A nudge discovered by a learning system, unlike one a person designed, comes with no prior theory of why it works and may exploit a cognitive process no theory yet describes, so judging it by its outcomes cannot diagnose or repair its side effects; overseeing it needs inspection of which human processes it exploits, by people expert in human cognition | Schmauder et al. (2023), [LIT-179](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-179.md), read in [NOTE-171](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-171.md). An argument by analogy from Hausman's reply to Friedman: a test drive is not enough if you must repair the car. Its evidence is reported from others: an RL agent moved choices of a target lottery from 50% to 70% by exploiting documented biases (Dezfouli et al. 2020), and AI advisers learned dishonest advice against simulated clients. No case of an undocumented bias is given; that is the paper's conjecture, and its oversight proposal is unspecified. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-628](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-628.md) v2 | Self-production alone gives a system only an all-or-nothing norm, to go on or to die, and that distinction is available to an observer, not to the system; a graded norm the system itself has, by which viable states are better or worse for it, needs adaptivity, a further capacity to detect tendencies toward the boundary of its viability and to act so as to reverse them, and sense-making and agency need adaptivity | Di Paolo (2005), [LIT-1017](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1017.md), read in full in [NOTE-719](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-719.md). A conceptual argument against Weber and Varela: autopoiesis in its original formulation entails conservation, not active homeostasis, so a bacterium whose intake is below consumption does not seek food "just because" it is autopoietic, and balancing at a cliff edge and falling over it both conserve autopoiesis. Adaptivity is defined, graded and recursive; pathology becomes failure of adaptivity while autopoiesis continues. There is no formal model, and the viability set is defined in one sentence. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-630](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-630.md) | A protective measurement yields the expectation value ⟨A⟩ on a single system in the ideal limit, and with enough observables ψ up to a global phase; this shows ψ to be ontic only if the protection procedure carries no information about ψ, a premise that Zeno and adiabatic protection, which select ψ from a discrete eigenbasis the experimenter chose, do not meet | Gao (2016), [LIT-121](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-121.md), read in full in [NOTE-140](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-140.md). Under Zeno protection the pointer shifts by exactly ⟨A⟩ with no entanglement (eqs. 1.9–1.13), and projectors on regions plus a current operator give ρ and j (eqs. 1.14–1.16). Gao argues three routes from this to ψ-ontology, claimed to need no preparation independence. All three rest on the premise that the protection does not "know" ψ, which Gao's own fn. 10 partly concedes is false. The random-discontinuous-motion ontology and the collapse model built on it are further, weaker steps. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-631](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-631.md) | Standard unitary quantum theory and the general quantum theory of open systems are intertranslatable on their common domain, so neither dependence nor justification ranks them; the open theory comes out more fundamental only through premises about interpretation, that orthodox and Everettian readings exhaust the complete readings of the state vector, and that density operators precede state vectors in how states are assigned | Cuffaro & Hartmann (2021), [LIT-037](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-037.md), read in full in [NOTE-077](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-077.md). Stinespring dilation one way and dropping Lindblad terms the other make the two frameworks a tie on ontic dependence (OntFund-1) and on justification (EpFund-1). The verdict for the open theory comes from OntFund-2, which holds only if orthodox and Everettian readings are all that count, and from EpFund-2, which rests on imperfect preparation. Explanatory fundamentality is effectively abandoned. The paper proves nothing formal, and its "tout court" conclusion outruns §4. | Proposed |
