| [THEORY-633](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-633.md) | Experiences have no phenomenal properties: introspection represents physical, quasi-phenomenal properties of sensory states as phenomenal, so what needs explaining is why experiences seem to have phenomenal properties, not how a brain produces them; a weaker view that keeps a deflated phenomenal residue is unstable unless it can say what that residue is | Frankish (2016), [LIT-458](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-458.md), read in [NOTE-384](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-384.md), names the view and the "illusion problem"; Dennett's reply to Chalmers (1996), [LIT-397](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-397.md) ([NOTE-346](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-346.md)), gives its earlier form, that subtracting every function from one's consciousness leaves only a conviction; Frankish (2025), [LIT-103](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-103.md) ([NOTE-143](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-143.md)), applies it to valence. A research programme, not a theory: Frankish proposes no mechanism, the instability of weak illusionism is argued by challenge, the case is abductive, and Dennett's subtraction is an introspective assertion. It keeps consciousness in an inclusive, functional sense and denies only phenomenal properties. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-637](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-637.md) | Treating openness in science as the unlimited sharing of research objects, with transparency ranked before reproducibility and inclusion, can narrow the epistemic diversity of research and entrench epistemic injustice, and this lowers the reliability of what is learned, so sharing is neither a necessary starting point nor a sufficient condition for reliable open science | Leonelli (2023), [LIT-189](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-189.md), read in [NOTE-098](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-098.md). An openly normative argument from four illustrative cases (GISAID, software stigma, crop-data linkage, the reproducibility debate) and the author's earlier qualitative work. That sharing-first open science can reduce diversity and worsen injustice is moderately supported; that this degrades reliability is argued, not measured. The positive proposal, openness as judicious connection, gives no decision rule, and the critique targets an ideal type the author admits many initiatives do not fit. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-638](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-638.md) | Instantiating a formal program is never by itself sufficient for understanding or intentionality, since a person can carry out a program for answering questions in Chinese by hand without understanding Chinese; whatever thinks does so in virtue of causal powers at least equivalent to the brain's, and the reply that the whole system understands is answered only by an asserted internalisation | Searle (1980), [LIT-400](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-400.md), read in [NOTE-349](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-349.md) (target article only). The room is a full implementation run by a person, and his first-person verdict is read as the system's. The decisive step against the systems reply ("the system is just a part of him") is asserted, not shown, and which causal powers matter is left empirical. The argument is about understanding and intentionality, not consciousness, and it grants that machines, including artifacts with the brain's causal powers, could think. Proposed; Dennett's intentional strategy is its rival. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-643](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-643.md) | The restrictions on syntax reaching into words that a separate word-formation component was credited with are restrictions on heads versus phrases and on what individual affixes select, and phrases feed word formation, so a single combinatorial component can build both words and phrases | Bruening (2018), [LIT-071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-071.md), read in full in [NOTE-065](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-065.md). Phrases feed English word formation productively, ellipsis and focus reach sub-word units, and claimed differences of principle (locality, adjuncts, headedness, idiosyncrasy) fail; extraction, coordination and the no-phrase constraint are restated over X0 vs XP and affix selection, with no mention of "word". The English evidence of §§2–3 is the strong part. Several sub-arguments are provisional by the author's own account, and Müller's reply in the same volume disputes extraction, coordination and the resultative argument. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-644](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-644.md) | Panpsychism escapes dualism's problem of mental causation only in its constitutive Russellian form, where micro-experiences constitute macro-experience; that form meets three combination problems, of subjects, qualities and structure, and every response that avoids combining (emergent, autonomous or identity panpsychism) gives back the advantage in mental causation or revised physics, while the combinatorial responses remain unworked | Chalmers (2016/2017), [LIT-395](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-395.md), read in full in [NOTE-358](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-358.md) from the April 2015 draft. A map of the problem, not a solution or an impossibility proof, and the author says so. The dilemma is argued case by case; the strongest arguments against constitutive panpsychism, subject-summing and structural mismatch, rest on conceivability premises and on a structure-preservation principle called plausible, not shown. The verdicts on which responses are most promising are judgements of promise. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-646](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-646.md) | Skepticism about inner mental representations does not motivate fictionalism about folk psychology, because realism about beliefs as internal, intentional, causal states does not require the representational theory of mind; and a fictionalist who lets pretence yield genuine assertions about the overall state that causes behaviour is committed to that state | Drayson (2025), [LIT-112](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-112.md), read in [NOTE-117](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-117.md), against Toon's Mind As Metaphor (2023). Toon's negative argument needs "committed to internal, intentional, causal attitudes ⇒ committed to RTM", which non-representational functionalism (Lewis, Putnam, Loar) makes false; and his metasemantic case against inner representation mistakes one motivation for RTM for part of it. His positive argument faces a dilemma: a merely behavioural overall state gives fictionalism no causal advantage, and a causal one is a reason to identify it with the belief. It argues against two motivations, assumes fictionalism coherent, and sketches the functionalist alternative by citation in one paragraph. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-647](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-647.md) v2 | If outright belief is credence ultraclose to 1 relative to a context level, conjunction holds for any standard ('few') number of believed propositions and fails for an ultralarge number, which dissolves the Lottery Paradox as an accumulation of negligible rounding errors | Wenmackers (2011), [LIT-163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-163.md), chapter 3, read in [NOTE-139](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-139.md). Stratified Belief, B(x) iff P(x) ≃_V 1 in Hrbacek's relative analysis, satisfies a Stratified Conjunction Principle for a standard number of conjuncts (proved) and fails for an ultralarge number. The proofs hold inside the framework. That belief works this way is argued: any explicit threshold collapses the model back to the Lockean one, the author calls it "crude", and knowledge is set aside. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-648](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-648.md) | A social fact is a way of acting, thinking or feeling that exists outside individual consciousness and can constrain the individual from outside, shown by sanction or by the resistance it offers to violation; such a fact is general in a group because it is collective, not collective because general, so the group is its substrate | Durkheim (1894; book 1895), chapter I of Les Règles de la méthode sociologique, [LIT-484](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-484.md), read in French in [NOTE-391](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-391.md). A definition argued from examples, which its author calls "un simple résumé des données immédiates de l'observation" (n. 3). Its two load-bearing steps are asserted: that what is neither organic nor individual-psychic must have society as its substrate, and that constraint is present even where no one feels it. It is a claim about the object of sociology, not a group-mind thesis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-650](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-650.md) | Whether a self at one time is the same as a self at another has an answer only relative to a level of abstraction fixed by the purpose of asking, and asked at no such level it has none; the question with a substantive answer is what makes a self one thing at a time | Floridi (2011), [LIT-136](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-136.md), read in [NOTE-130](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-130.md). The deflation of diachronic identity is an informal argument from examples that rests on the method of levels of abstraction, assumed from elsewhere; that this "is not relativism" is one sentence, and that individuation comes before identification is asserted. It is not, as its title suggests, a criterion of personal identity, and its positive answer to the synchronic question, the three-membranes model, is "somewhat figurative" by its author's word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-651](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-651.md) | Disinformation incidents labelled with DISARM techniques can be carried in standard STIX 2.1 without extending it, as an intrusion set that uses attack patterns, is attributed to a threat actor and targets locations; the DISINFOX mapping that moved 118 incidents into OpenCTI this way drops their content, narratives, channels, evidence and the confidence of their attribution | Sánchez González et al. (2025), [LIT-083](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-083.md), an unreviewed preprint read in [NOTE-028](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-028.md). The mapping is explicit (four STIX object types, three relationship types) and was exercised end to end on 118 incidents; the reading rates that demonstration strong. Nothing beyond ingestion was measured. Attribution is one ungraded edge to an actor, typically a nation-state, which is the layer the EEAS's Exposure Matrix grades in four tiers. Proposed because the source is an unevaluated preprint and its claim of priority is narrower than its abstract says. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-655](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-655.md) v2 | Social behaviour evolves as if each individual valued a neighbour's fitness against its own by their coefficient of relationship, and its discriminations evolve to make that coefficient determinate; so kin are favoured and strangers met with hostility, relatives fight less, and haplodiploid sisters, related by 3/4, are predisposed to worker altruism | Hamilton (1964), Part II, [LIT-506](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-506.md), read in full in [NOTE-410](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-410.md), on Part I's model ([LIT-497](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-497.md)). Two general principles, offered as an "unrigorous" generalization, are applied to alarm calls, kin recognition in gulls and terns, clones and colonies, Hymenoptera, and fights. The evidence is anecdotal. The author calls his positive indications for distant relatives "rather few and feeble", reports Australian halictines and multiple mating as running against the hymenopteran hypothesis, and explains anomalies case by case. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-656](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-656.md) | A single holistic power of the universe's configuration, carried by bare matter points, cannot ground a subsystem's effective wave function without changing the ontology, because the masses in a decoupled subsystem's Hamiltonian must belong to that subsystem's particles; dispositions intrinsic to particles or events need no such change | Dorato (2015), [LIT-176](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-176.md), read in full in [NOTE-105](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-105.md). Against Esfeld et al.'s holistic dispositionalism: when a subsystem effectively decouples, its Hamiltonian's masses must be intrinsic dispositions of its particles, so the holistic view must alter its ontology between the universal and the effective wave function (pp. 14–15). The argument is moderate and posed partly as questions. The paper's wider thesis, that events are a common primitive ontology for GRW, Bohm and ψ-antirealist views, shows compatibility only, and Dorato concedes the difference from Esfeld could be verbal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-657](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-657.md) | If an emergent property is one that the parts lack, then the other marks commonly given for emergence are separate questions about each system and not consequences of it: established condensed-matter cases show novelty without a discontinuity, a discontinuity without novelty, novelty that was predicted first, and novelty with a rigorous reduction | McKenzie (2025), [LIT-141](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-141.md), read in full in [NOTE-124](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-124.md). The book stipulates novelty as the definition and runs twelve further characteristics over about thirty cases. The Kondo effect is novel and continuous; the liquid–gas transition is discontinuous and adiabatically connected; BKT and the hexatic phase were predicted before they were found; Butterfield's cases are novel and reduced. [NOTE-124](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-124.md) says no THEORY follows from the book as a whole, since its definition is stipulated and the logical relations among the characteristics are left open by its own account (§24). This is the part of it that the counterexamples carry. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-658](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-658.md) | Whether an account of organismal goal-directedness must separate genuine teleology from mere self-organisation, such as a candle flame, depends on what the account is for: a scientific model of agency need not and perhaps cannot draw the line, while an account of how mind and value fit into nature may have to, and need not be operationalisable | Nahas & Sachs (2023), [LIT-192](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-192.md), read in [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) from the accepted manuscript. A metatheoretical argument: naturalising teleology serves at least two relatively autonomous projects, advancing biology and settling the naturalism debate, with different success criteria. It is worked on one dispute, the demarcation from dissipative structures. The positive pluralism (Deacon for naturalism, Walsh and the organisational approach for biology) is only "tempting to suggest", and the boundary between the projects is never drawn. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-660](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-660.md) | The local branching geometry of physical tree networks, neurons, blood vessels, trees, corals and plants, is set by minimising the surface area of tubes that must keep a minimum circumference, not by minimising length: this predicts trifurcations once links are thick relative to their separation (χ = w/r above about 0.83) and orthogonal sprouts once one branch is much thinner than the other two (ρ = w′/w below about 0.6), both departures from Steiner trees that the data show qualitatively | Meng, Piazza, Both, Barzel & Barabási (2026), [LIT-069](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-069.md), read in full with the SI in [NOTE-075](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-075.md). Only two symmetric motifs are solved, each by a local, penalised optimiser started from the Steiner layout; the "exact" mapping to string worldsheets holds for a problem the paper does not solve. The random-terminal prediction is a sigmoid fitted to one tetrahedron, trifurcations are partly made by a merging rule, the one robustness check moves the key statistic 4.3-fold, and the sprouting breakpoints are chosen per dataset with no null. Real motifs are about 25% longer than Steiner, which the model leaves unexplained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-662](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-662.md) | The feeling of fluency is an inference about the precision of one's own processing, triggered by a change in precision against expectation; because its cause is internal and not given to introspection, a felt discrepancy is attributed to the most salient external source, as familiarity, liking or a sense of error | Brouillet and Friston (2023), [LIT-957](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-957.md), read in [NOTE-785](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-785.md). A perspective essay with no model and no new data. It joins Whittlesea's discrepancy-attribution hypothesis to precision-weighting. The part with moderate support is the reviewed finding that fluency judgements follow discrepancy from expected fluency (the hension effect and its extensions), reported secondhand. The precision reading and the felt/unfelt levels are proposals. "Felt" here means attended and reportable, not phenomenal, and fluency is not offered as affect. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-663](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-663.md) | Altruism between non-relatives can be selected when each act costs the giver less than it benefits the recipient, the same partners meet often and symmetrically, and help is withheld from those who do not return it; in humans, moralistic aggression, gratitude, sympathy and guilt are adaptations that regulate such exchange, and selection then favours sham versions of each and the ability to detect them | Trivers (1971), [LIT-510](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-510.md), read in full in [NOTE-402](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-402.md). A verbal model, with a Prisoner's Dilemma sketch Hamilton communicated, followed by a functional account of the human emotions that would regulate reciprocity. The model is plausible and was later formalized. The psychology is fitted to 1960s social-psychology findings, mostly on American students, and the heritability of the dispositions is assumed. Trivers knows "of no psychological studies on the detection of sham moralistic aggression and sham guilt" (p. 51). His "unfairness" is inequity in exchange, not the division of a disputed resource. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-665](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-665.md) | Asserting is undertaking a commitment that entitles others to reassert it and carries a responsibility to show entitlement if challenged; every interlocutor keeps score of everyone's commitments and entitlements, so the score is doubly perspectival, and a speech act's significance is the change it makes to the scores, fixed by its content's inferential role | Brandom (1994), [LIT-794](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-794.md), skimmed in [NOTE-622](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-622.md): the Preface and the core of chapter 3 only. This states the deontic scorekeeping model of assertion, not the book's arguments for it, and rests on a skim. By the author's account the model is an idealization limited to semantic inference, with implicature left to an outer shell. It gives no single objective score, only scores kept from each perspective. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-666](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-666.md) | A system that produces itself, a network of production that regenerates the components which produce it and constitute it as a distinguishable unity, has by that fact an intrinsic purpose, the maintenance of its identity, and with it a point of view, valence and a world as distinct from an environment, so that teleology in organisms is real and not an observer's as-if; the account is stated for the cell, and a multicellular organism is not itself autopoietic | Weber & Varela (2002), [LIT-1018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1018.md), read in full in [NOTE-720](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-720.md). An essay of exegesis and convergence: Kant's natural purposes read non-reductively, Jonas's metabolism-based philosophy of the organism, and autopoiesis. The step from self-production to purpose is asserted ("Bluntly stated"), the step to subjectivity is Jonas's phenomenological inversion, and no observable is proposed for the "empirical feature" the conclusion claims. What sets autopoiesis apart from dissipative structures is placed in "concern", not in organisation. One paragraph runs from self-maintenance to a right to life. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-667](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-667.md) | Gender and race, defined as a feminist and antiracist theory needs them, are hierarchical social positions: a woman is someone subordinated in part because she is taken to have bodily features presumed to show a female's reproductive role, a racialized group is one subordinated or privileged in part because its members are taken to have features presumed to show ancestry from a region, and on these definitions both are real, social and contingent | Haslanger (2000), [LIT-480](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-480.md), read in [NOTE-394](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-394.md). An explicitly ameliorative ("analytical") account: the definitions are chosen for what a critical theory needs, and the author is "less committed to saying that this is what gender is and what race is" (p. 52). It is tied to a descriptive claim, that our gender and race talk tracks social kinds obscured by its manifest content (p. 34), which the paper asserts and does not test. Its empirical premises about race are uncited. Not a discovery about bodies, and not a claim that every female is a woman in its sense. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-669](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-669.md) | Reading the universal quantum state as nomological escapes the costs of reading it as a field only by paying in the theory of laws: on the strong reading, modelled on the classical Hamiltonian, a time-dependent ψ makes laws time-indexed unless the universal state is time-independent, as Wheeler–DeWitt would make it; on the weak and functionalist readings ψ need be neither unique nor time-independent, but only within an extended Humeanism whose criterion would equally make classical fields nomological | Chen (2018), [LIT-204](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-204.md) ([NOTE-175](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-175.md)), maps the realist readings and splits the nomological one into strong and weak. Belot (2011), [LIT-100](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-100.md) ([NOTE-110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-110.md)), ranks the costs of ψ-as-law: time-indexed laws are the serious obstacle, grades of necessity tolerable. Allori (2021), [LIT-200](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-200.md) ([NOTE-154](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-154.md)), makes ψ an ingredient of the law, which may be time-dependent and non-unique, and so concedes Belot's point that ψ behaves like an initial condition. Each move is an informal argument. Chen reports, without endorsing, the objection that the weak reading is too cheap, and Allori's reply embraces the case it treats as a reductio. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-670](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-670.md) | Ordinary dispositions can be modelled as restricted possibilities individuated by their manifestation alone: 'fragile' as manifestation in a sufficient proportion of cases over maximally varied external circumstances, 'breakable' as plain possibility; grading by closeness to an ideal world fails for any choice of ideal | Vetter (2014), [LIT-109](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-109.md), read in full from the penultimate draft in [NOTE-125](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-125.md). A proposal, which the paper says it does not show superior to the conditional conception (pp. 6, 26). Its strongest part is negative: for any ideal world, an Achilles'-heel block that breaks only there counts as fragile, so closeness grading fails. The positive proportion measure is not defined, and the finite, maximally varied set of cases it counts over is admitted to be non-unique. The evidence is '-able' semantics and a COCA count in which none of 226 relevant uses of "disposed to" ascribes a standing tendency to an inanimate object. Finks and masks are left unsolved, and dispositions of fundamental science are set aside. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-671](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-671.md) | An open system with enough internal degrees of freedom settles, among its possible steady states, into the one of maximum entropy production; this selects among steady states, where Prigogine's minimum principle only describes relaxation toward one | Kleidon (2009), [LIT-519](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-519.md), read in [NOTE-423](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-423.md), states the principle and its Earth-system applications; Dewar (2003), [LIT-521](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-521.md), read in [NOTE-426](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-426.md), is the derivation it cites. The applications are model fits, mostly reported, many by the author. The derivation needs a mean-field step and an unargued assumption about path counts, and does not reach far from equilibrium ([THEORY-676](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-676.md)). "Sufficient degrees of freedom" is never made operational, so a failure can always be read as too few. The advocate's own verdict: "no one would argue that MEP is well established". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-673](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-673.md) v2 | The Price equation follows from any ancestor–descendant mapping in a closed population and is, like f = ma, a generalization-sketch: a schema that is empty of predictions until a specific model supplies entities, characters, time step and causes, whose value lies in unifying and guiding model construction, so the charges that it is a tautology or lacks predictive power and dynamic sufficiency ask of it what only its specialisations can supply | Luque (2016), [LIT-205](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-205.md), read in [NOTE-101](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-101.md) from the PhilSci manuscript. The derivation and the diallelic re-derivation are strong; the generalization-sketch reading is a moderate argument by analogy with f = ma plus two case studies, whose authors recovered results already derivable otherwise. The reply to "tautology" answers the word, not the critics' point, which Luque concedes in §7.2. The paper's prescription, that biologists should adopt the equation, is asserted without comparison. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-675](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-675.md) | Without a shared stable start, the linear barrier between solutions of one objective depends on the structure of the training data: between GCNs it falls with graph density and feature separability and is highest at middling homophily, and between federated-averaging models it grows with client heterogeneity and falls with width | Li et al. (2025), [LIT-676](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-676.md), read in [NOTE-529](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-529.md): on synthetic CSBM graphs the barrier between GCNs from different seeds falls with density and feature separability and peaks at middling homophily; GCN, GraphSAGE and GAT barriers are similar, an MLP's differ. Zhou, Zhang & Tsang (2023), [LIT-666](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-666.md), read in [NOTE-517](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-517.md): FedAvg global models from one random start under more heterogeneous clients are separated by a larger line barrier, joined by a one-bend chain, and the barrier falls with width. Both readings named this account and held it back. The GNN proofs are missing and its barriers are plots; the federated bound treats heterogeneity as isotropic noise, and its lemma and theorem conditions conflict as written. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-678](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-678.md) | In Stable Diffusion, a subject named in a two-subject prompt is left out of the image when its token governs no region of the cross-attention map early in sampling, and raising that token's smoothed peak attention during the first half of sampling, by gradient steps on the latent with no retraining, brings the subject back; that this also fixes attribute binding is argued, not measured by the paper | Chefer, Alaluf, Vinker, Wolf & Cohen-Or (2023), [LIT-806](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-806.md), read in [NOTE-639](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-639.md), with T2I-CompBench++ ([LIT-798](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-798.md), [NOTE-610](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-610.md)) for the binding measurement the paper lacks. Evidence is on 276 templated two-subject prompts by CLIP image–text similarity, BLIP-caption similarity and a 65-person preference study (77–91% preferred it); no neglect rate is reported, before or after. [NOTE-639](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-639.md) filed no THEORY, because the paper's method is machine-learning practice; the account of why subjects go missing is a finding about the model and is filed here as Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-680](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-680.md) | Emotion regulation is a set of processes distinct from emotion generation, by which people influence which emotions they have, when, and how they are experienced and expressed; regulatory acts can be sorted by the point in the generative sequence where they act, and acting before response tendencies form (reappraisal) has different consequences from acting after (suppression) | Gross (1998), [LIT-554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-554.md), read in [NOTE-429](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-429.md), the founding review. It reports no data. The five families (situation selection, situation modification, attentional deployment, cognitive change, response modulation) are "working distinctions". The antecedent and response contrast rests on a handful of film studies it cites: reappraisal lowered negative experience, suppression did not reliably do so and raised sympathetic activation. The paper's own first open problem is whether regulation can be told apart from generation at all. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-681](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-681.md) | If every real idea derives from an impression, there is no idea of a simple self persisting through life; the mind is a bundle of perceptions, and the identity ascribed to it is produced by the imagination passing easily along resemblance and causation, as with a rebuilt ship or a growing oak, though Hume's Appendix concedes that this does not explain what unites the perceptions | Hume (1739, with the Appendix of 1740), [LIT-451](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-451.md), read in [NOTE-386](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-386.md). The negative half is as strong as the copy principle. The mechanism of the fiction is argued by analogy from cases of usage. The account of what unites the bundle is withdrawn by its author, who names the two principles he cannot reconcile. It does not say there is no self in any sense, and it leaves identity "as it regards our passions" to Book 2. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-682](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-682.md) | The time-average of a single threshold (Hill) response to a periodic signal is independent of the signal's period for a fixed waveform, so a frequency cannot be read by one sigmoidal stage; two cascaded stages can read it, because the first changes the waveform with period; and a delayed kinesin–dynein signalling loop whose period grows with axon length, read out this way and coupled to protrusion and contraction, can hold an axon at a stable length | Folz, Wettmann, Morigi & Kruse (2018; PRE 2019), [LIT-034](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-034.md), read in full in [NOTE-067](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-067.md). The period independence is proved, for signals that differ by a time rescaling only; the two-stage readout is shown numerically and in the Heaviside limit; the loop's minimum length and ω ≈ √3 v/L for long axons come from linear stability analysis. The length control is a lumped delay-differential model with one parameter set and the motor velocity v never stated, so its absolute lengths, about 125 µm, cannot be reproduced. A proof of mechanism, not a model fitted to axons. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-684](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-684.md) | Experiencing oneself as a self that was there in the further past, seeking pattern in one's life, fitting it to a story and falsifying it in the telling are separable, and fitting it to a story suffices for narrativity; on testimony that some normal people are Episodic and live good lives, neither the claim that people experience their lives as narratives nor the claim that a good life or full personhood needs it holds in general | Strawson (2004), [LIT-452](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-452.md), read in [NOTE-383](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-383.md). The separation of Diachronicity, form-finding, story-telling and revision is strong as conceptual analysis. That many normal people are Episodic rests on testimony, the author's and that of writers he classifies, with no measure. It does not say that the remoter past did not happen to the human being, only to the self one now experiences oneself to be, and that metaphysical claim is asserted from earlier papers. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-687](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-687.md) | For empirically equivalent dual theories read naively, adding the common core as a candidate world does not break the underdetermination, and neither do super-empirical virtues or an overarching theory: each route to a single actual world needs a further metaphysical principle, such as the identity of indiscernibles | Le Bihan & Read (2018), [LIT-113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-113.md), read in [NOTE-152](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-152.md) from the accepted manuscript. A nontechnical survey whose central argument is informal. It assumes a duality relates empirically equivalent models (weaker than De Haro & Butterfield's isomorphism of a bare theory), that each model is read naively and internally, and that structuralism is set aside. Its reading said it supports no existing THEORY directly; this files the conditional verdict the survey argues for, and nothing more. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-690](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-690.md) | In the physical dualities examined, theoretically inequivalent duals turn out empirically inequivalent, so dualities yield no genuine in-principle underdetermination; where duals would contradict each other a cautious realist is warranted in committing only to their common core, and because the exact cases' common cores are rich rather than empty, dualities give no support to structural realism | De Haro & Butterfield (2025), [LIT-199](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md), read in [NOTE-178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md). A case-by-case argument over the book's examples, with a logico-semantic fallback (each dual entails the common core) for a hypothetical genuine case. The rich-core verdict is argued from exact cases (bosonization, electric–magnetic duality, T-duality) and does not reach AdS/CFT or M-theory, where structural-realist readings were proposed and the common core is "partial … ongoing work in physics!". The commitment holds only where an interpreted common core exists, which the authors say is not true in general. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-691](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-691.md) | A self is an abstractum like a centre of gravity, posited by interpreting a person's behaviour and talk, the brain's own autobiography included; it is as determinate as that story, it can be authored by a process with no self in it, and a body holds as many selves as the points the best story coheres around | Dennett (1992), [LIT-442](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-442.md), read in [NOTE-364](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-364.md) from a copy-edited transcription. Argued by analogy and by thought experiments whose premises are stipulated, notably that a mindless machine could write a passable novel. It does not say the self is an illusion: a centre of gravity is a legitimate posit that figures in explanations. It is a claim about selves, not about consciousness or about what makes a person persist. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-693](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-693.md) | In conversation, evaluating an object, positioning oneself and aligning with another speaker are three aspects of one stance act rather than three kinds of stance, because a stance takes a shared object and answers a prior stance, which are usually supplied by earlier turns; a resonant follow must mark its relation to the lead, with too or either in English | Du Bois (2007), [LIT-779](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-779.md), read in full in [NOTE-590](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-590.md). Argued from short excerpts of American English conversation (Santa Barbara and Longman corpora), with no counts. The co-occurrence of the three aspects is shown in chosen examples, not tested for separability; the too/either result rests on a separate study (Du Bois 2004) whose figures are not given. It does not treat a speaker who animates someone else's stance, which it sets aside for Goffman. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-694](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-694.md) | After every function associated with consciousness is explained (discrimination, integration, report, access, attention, control), why these functions are accompanied by experience remains open, because those phenomena are defined by their functions and experience, what it is like for the subject, is not; so experience cannot be reductively explained by any mechanism, though it may be related to the physical by further laws | Chalmers (1995), [LIT-406](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-406.md), read in full in [NOTE-336](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-336.md), with Nagel (1974), [LIT-096](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-096.md), read in [NOTE-089](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-089.md), for the subjective character it starts from. The test is whether "you have explained the function but not the phenomenon" is a conceptual mistake: it is for life and reportability, not for experience. The decisive premise, that any physical process could conceptually occur without experience, is asserted and deferred to a book the record holds unread. Nagel's conclusion is weaker than Chalmers's: physicalism not refuted but not yet understandable. Naturalistic dualism and the double-aspect theory of information are the proposals built on the gap, not part of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-699](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-699.md) | Adaptive self-maintenance across varied conditions is sufficient, without sentience, for having a good of one's own, so insentient plants and a self-maintaining machine are welfare subjects while thermostats are not; but the line against thermostats is argued as one of degree, and the reasons such welfare gives are extremely weak | Bruckner (2025), [LIT-120](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-120.md), read in [NOTE-093](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-093.md). Proposed by abduction from agreed cases, not deduced (§4): an entity that "sustains, maintains, and renews itself in a way that responds and adapts to its environmental conditions" is a welfare subject. Plants and the hypothetical car Tessler qualify; governors, thermostats and missiles do not. The "autopoiesis" is a loose behavioural notion, not Maturana and Varela's self-production, and the thermostat line is supported only comparatively. The answer to absurd obligations borrows Bradford 2023 and makes phenomenal consciousness decide how much such welfare matters. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-703](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-703.md) | Weak emergence of a macro variable from micro variables can be measured as its Granger autonomy from them times their mean Granger causation of it, which is zero if it is independent of them or fully predicted by them; in a boids model this measure, and Granger causation from the flock's centre of mass to each boid, are higher for flocking than for random or rigid motion; the measure is relative to the regression model and the variables included | Seth (2010), [LIT-1170](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1170.md), read in full in [NOTE-935](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-935.md). The definitions are exact; the evidence is two hand-built agent-based models. Seth concedes that the measure is epistemic: positive with missing micro factors or a limited predictor, zero with the system as predictor. Proposed until it is tested against an independent criterion. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-747](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-747.md) | In Fourier–Galerkin large-eddy simulation, a first-order finite-memory Mori–Zwanzig closure tracks filtered-DNS energy decay and dissipation on the viscous Burgers equation and on the incompressible Taylor–Green vortex, isotropic turbulence and channel flow about as well as dynamic Smagorinsky where that model is at home and better than Smagorinsky and the t-model on the transitional Taylor–Green vortex; the memory length that fits it is set by the cutoff, not by the flow alone, scaling in Burgers roughly as 0.2 over the spectral radius of the resolved variables' Jacobian | Parish and Duraisamy (2017), [LIT-1259](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1259.md), read in [NOTE-973](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-973.md). The closure is [THEORY-760](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-760.md)'s finite Markovian augmentation. Here is how it did, as far as the paper's plots show: close to filtered DNS in integral quantities, comparable to dynamic Smagorinsky in equilibrium turbulence, clearly better on a transitional flow, and with the subgrid transfer peaked at the cutoff where DNS puts it but about 40% too deep. The paper calls the predictions "excellent" with no numbers. Its fitted memory length shortens as the resolved dynamics speed up, so the memory belongs to the cutoff as much as to the flow. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-759](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-759.md) | A six-layer, 256-unit ReLU network trained by full-batch Adam to regress a sum of sinusoids at 5 to 50 cycles on [0, 1] fits the components in order of frequency, and keeps that order when the amplitudes rise tenfold with frequency, so in this setting the order of acquisition is set by the learner and not by the strength of the target's components | Rahaman et al. (2019), [LIT-1261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1261.md), Experiment 1, read in full in [NOTE-983](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-983.md). With equal amplitudes, and with amplitudes rising from 0.1 at 5 cycles to 1 at 50, the normalised fit \|f̃(k_i)\|/A_i reaches 1 at low frequency first. This is the reverse of the order by strength that [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md) gives for a deep linear network. One architecture, one optimiser, a 1-D input, ten runs averaged. The paper's theory gives a bound on speed, not this order. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md) v2 | For every α < 1/3 there is a nonzero weak solution of the 3D incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box, with velocity Hölder-continuous of exponent α in space and time, that vanishes outside a finite time interval; its energy is not conserved, so the energy flux across a mollification scale ε does not vanish as ε → 0, and it runs in both directions, out of the vanishing scales while the energy rises and into them while it falls | Isett (2018), [LIT-1255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1255.md), skimmed in [NOTE-974](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-974.md): the negative half of Onsager's conjecture. With [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md) (Constantin, E and Titi, the positive half) it makes 1/3 the threshold. For the record, its point is that below 1/3 the energy flux into vanishing scales can survive the limit, which is the half of A3's point that THEORY-749 could not give. It does not say that this flux is a dissipative cascade. Isett's solutions start from rest, gain energy and lose it again, so the surviving flux takes both signs. Nor does it say that such solutions are limits of Navier–Stokes or describe turbulence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-767](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-767.md) v2 | Body ownership draws on interoceptive as well as exteroceptive signals: a visual cue synchronous with one's heartbeat increases ownership of a virtual hand and identification with a virtual body, and lower interoceptive sensitivity goes with greater susceptibility to the rubber hand illusion | Seth (2013), [LIT-1263](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1263.md), read in full in [NOTE-1000](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1000.md). An opinion article that reports, at second hand, that a virtual hand pulsing with the heartbeat was owned more (Suzuki et al. 2013, the author's own group), that a virtual body pulsing with it was identified with more (Aspell et al. 2013), and that people with lower heartbeat-detection sensitivity are more susceptible to the rubber hand illusion (Tsakiris et al. 2011). None of the studies was read here, and no control separates the heartbeat from any other periodic signal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-768](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-768.md) v2 | Minimal selfhood is identification with the whole body, located where that body is felt to be and seen from inside it; owning a body part does not reach it, and bodily agency enables it causally without being part of it | Blanke & Metzinger (2009), [LIT-1274](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1274.md), read in full in [NOTE-1002](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1002.md), with Lenggenhager et al. (2007), [LIT-1279](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1279.md), read in full in [NOTE-999](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-999.md), for the full-body illusion it leans on. Minimal phenomenal selfhood is given three dimensions: global self-identification, self-location and a weak first-person perspective. Out-of-body experience, heautoscopy and full-body illusions vary them; the rubber hand illusion is said not to. The necessity and sufficiency claims are asserted, and the agency thesis rests on adults whose agency was intact. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-769](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-769.md) v2 | Ownership of a body part is a graded belief that it is the most probable common cause of correlated multisensory input, so that synchronous stimulation of another object moves some of that belief to the object and away from the real part | Apps & Tsakiris (2014), [LIT-1262](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1262.md), read in full in [NOTE-991](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-991.md), with Botvinick & Cohen (1998), [LIT-1277](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1277.md), for the illusion it explains. The rubber hand, enfacement and rubber-voice illusions are read as one inference: unimodal surprise from synchronous stimulation is explained away by shifting the probability that a part is "me". The account fits the findings; its authors grant there is little direct evidence and that it is hard to falsify with standard fMRI. It does not say why such a model is experienced as a self. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-772](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-772.md) v2 | For every β < 1/3 there is a weak solution of the 3D incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box, in C⁰_t(B^β_{3,∞} ∩ L^{1/(1−3β)}), whose Duchon–Robert dissipation is the smooth nonnegative density E(t, x) = −e(t)e′(t)ρ₀(x₁, x₂)² fixed at the construction's first step; for such a solution the local coarse-grained energy flux into scales below ℓ converges, as ℓ → 0 and as a distribution in space and time, to E, so the transfer into vanishing scales is one-way at every place and time in the limit, nonzero inside a periodic array of pipes and zero outside them; where and how fast energy is dissipated is chosen by the construction, not forced by the equations, and nothing is shown about the sign at any positive scale | Giri, Kwon and Novack (2023; Annals 2026), [LIT-1289](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1289.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1022](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1022.md): the L³-based strong Onsager theorem. Below 1/3, in Constantin, E and Titi's own scale of spaces ([THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md)), there are weak Euler solutions satisfying the local energy inequality. In the proof the Duchon–Robert measure is a prescribed smooth function, positive in a periodic array of pipes and zero elsewhere. So the coarse-grained flux into vanishing scales is one-signed locally in space and time, in the limit, and not only for the whole box as in [THEORY-776](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-776.md). Its location and rate are inputs of the construction; it is a smooth density on a few pipes, not concentrated on a thin set; nothing is said about the sign at a positive scale or about vanishing viscosity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-776](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-776.md) v3 | For every β < 1/3 and every smooth, strictly positive and strictly decreasing energy profile e(t) on [0, T], there is a weak solution of the 3D incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box, Hölder-continuous of exponent β in space and time, with ∫\|v(t)\|² = e(t) at every time; for such a solution the energy flux across a mollification scale ε, integrated over any time interval, tends as ε → 0 to ½ times the drop in e, which is strictly negative, so energy leaves the resolved field for vanishing scales on every interval; this is one-way for the energy of the whole box, not at every point, and it is chosen by the prescribed profile, not forced by the equations | Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol (2017; CPAM 2019), [LIT-1300](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1300.md), read in [NOTE-1013](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1013.md): the admissible version of Isett's negative half of Onsager's conjecture ([THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md)). Any smooth positive energy profile can be imposed on a C^β solution, β < 1/3, so a strictly decreasing one gives solutions whose total energy only falls. Through [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md)'s energy balance, the coarse-grained flux then runs into the vanishing scales on every time interval. That is the one-way transfer [THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md) could not give. It is one-way for the box as a whole, not at every point (no local energy inequality is proved); the same theorem gives increasing energy as readily, so the direction is a choice of the construction; and nothing ties these solutions to Navier–Stokes, to a constant-flux inertial range or to uniqueness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-777](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-777.md) | In Monte Carlo on a 64×64 periodic square-lattice Ising model at its critical point, parametrized by a field and 13 nearby couplings and observed only through the spins left after n checkerboard decimations (b = √2 per step, n ≤ 6), the two Fisher eigenvalues along the field and the gradient of T_c stay within a factor of about two of their microscopic values, while the others fall by up to about six decades, in three groups whose decay is consistent with b^(2y−d) per step for y = 0, −2 and −4 | Machta, Chachra, Transtrum and Sethna (2013), [LIT-1299](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1299.md), Fig. 3, read in [NOTE-1018](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1018.md). One lattice size, one temperature, at most six steps of b = √2 (so b^n ≤ 8), no error bars, and no fitted rates. The groups and their rates are bands the authors drew. The value y = 0 is not an operator of the 2D Ising model: it is the rate at which any direction without singular support loses information as sites are discarded. The caption's rate 2^(−d−y) disagrees with the bands and with the supplement's b^(2y−d). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-780](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-780.md) | Transcriptional regulation alone can give a bacterium's gene expression a memory: in E. coli, a transient knockdown or overexpression of one regulator, with the environment held fixed, can leave other genes in a different self-maintaining expression state after it is released, as Zhao, Wytock, Reynolds and Motter predict from a Boolean-network model of its regulatory core | Zhao, Wytock, Reynolds and Motter (2024), [LIT-854](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-854.md), read in full in [NOTE-655](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-655.md). Their abstract and discussion carry the model result to cells: one genotype may hold several heritable expression states without epigenetic marks, and history picks among them. They predict that a transient crp knockdown leaves zraR, melR or rhaRS changed ([NOTE-655](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-655.md), C8, untested). [THEORY-178](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-178.md) is the model result this rests on. No such perturbation has been done in cells ([QUESTION-172](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-172.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-781](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-781.md) | Strong gradient noise in SGD, like weight decay above a threshold, makes the subspace fixed by a mirror symmetry of a network's loss attracting even where it is a saddle, so that networks trained with SGD at large learning rates or small batches reach sparse, low-rank and identical-neuron solutions, as Ziyin proposes | Ziyin (2024), [LIT-1014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1014.md), read in [NOTE-716](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-716.md). Beyond the exact half that [THEORY-213](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-213.md) holds, the paper argues by a Lyapunov-exponent analysis that strong SGD noise makes a mirror's subspace attracting even at a strict saddle, and reads sparsity, low rank and identical neurons in trained networks as its result. That analysis rests on a second-order, diagonal- Hessian approximation, and the network evidence is a ResNet18's correlation blocks. The test is [QUESTION-206](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-206.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-782](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-782.md) | In networks that learn addition from summed embeddings, the critical training fraction of grokking is the fraction at which the training set's same-answer pairs come to fix the generalising representation up to translation and scale, at every group size, as Liu, Kitouni, Nolte, Michaud, Tegmark and Williams propose | Liu, Kitouni, Nolte, Michaud, Tegmark and Williams (2022), [LIT-858](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-858.md), read in [NOTE-662](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-662.md), with Power et al.'s critical fraction ([LIT-341](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-341.md)). The paper presents the critical training fraction as where the training set's equations fix the embedding. [THEORY-181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-181.md) holds the theorem for the ideal model and the match at the one size measured, p = 10 with 1D embeddings. Held to addition: for S₃ the networks generalise beyond this mechanism. The multi-size test is [QUESTION-199](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-199.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-783](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-783.md) v2 | In neural-network training, sign-descent-like optimizers such as Adam make independent skills of unequal frequency compete for coordinate signs, so that they are learned one after another where gradient descent would learn them together; this is one source of sequential skill onset, beside dependence between skills, as Liu, Liu, Michaud, Gore and Tegmark propose | Liu, Liu, Michaud, Gore and Tegmark (2025), [LIT-951](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-951.md), read in [NOTE-794](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-794.md). The paper explains the Domino effect, skills starting as others finish, by a coordinate-wise optimizer's competition for update signs. [THEORY-253](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-253.md) holds the simulation in their Geometry model and the rotated quadratic. The paper also shows dependent skills starting after their prerequisites (C5), so the optimizer is one source of sequential onset, not the only one. The test in a trained network is [QUESTION-193](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-193.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-784](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-784.md) | Language models trained on limited data show a test loss falling as P^(−γ/(2β)) because P training tokens resolve token correlations only out to a horizon growing as P^(1/(2β)), so that more data mainly lengthens the context a model can use, when the model learns within that horizon faster than it grows, as Cagnetta, Raventós, Ganguli and Wyart propose | Cagnetta, Raventós, Ganguli and Wyart (2026), [LIT-888](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-888.md), read in [NOTE-689](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-689.md), building on Cagnetta and Wyart's effective context window ([LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md)). The paper presents the horizon as the reason the data-limited exponent is γ/(2β). [THEORY-204](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-204.md) holds what it showed: the derivation under assumed scaling forms, and the measured overlap on TinyStories and WikiText-103 up to about 10^8 tokens. Whether the horizon is why is the test [QUESTION-233](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-233.md) asks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-785](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-785.md) | Listeners interpret an utterance by inverting a model of a speaker who chooses among alternatives by informativeness, so what a fixed form conveys depends on what else the speaker could have said, as the rational speech act account of Frank, Goodman and coauthors proposes | Frank and Goodman (2012), [LIT-821](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-821.md), and Goodman and Frank's review (2016), [LIT-816](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-816.md), present listener inference as the inversion of an informative speaker, the rational speech act account. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md), the fits of that model to mean bets in one-shot reference games and Bergen, Goodman and Levy's signalling-game result. This is the mechanism the fits were offered for, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-786](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-786.md) | Deep networks learn hierarchically generated data from a number of examples set by when the correlations between input patches and the class rise above sampling noise, so detecting those correlations is how they learn the grammar, as Cagnetta and coauthors propose | Cagnetta, Petrini, Tomasini, Favero and Wyart (2023), [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md), propose that deep networks learn compositional data by detecting the correlations between input patches and the class, and that the sample complexity is where those correlations emerge from sampling noise. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md), the measured law and the synonym-invariance it coincides with. This is the mechanism, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-787](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-787.md) | A system's causal structure can be most effective at a macro scale, so that causation emerges at a coarse-grained level and the macro description is the one at which the system's causes are found, as Hoel, Albantakis and Tononi propose from effective information | Hoel, Albantakis and Tononi (2013), [LIT-1038](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1038.md), argue that macro can beat micro: the scale at which effective information peaks is where a system's causal structure is, so causation can emerge at a macro level. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-222](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md), only the arithmetic: under uniform interventions imposed separately at each level, a macro description can have more effective information. This is the causal thesis, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-788](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-788.md) | Training a deep classifier past zero training error generally collapses its last-layer features onto their class means, drives the centred means toward a simplex equiangular tight frame aligned with the classifier, and makes the decision nearest class mean, as Papyan, Han and Donoho propose from their runs | Papyan, Han and Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), title their paper on the "prevalence" of neural collapse and present it as a pervasive outcome of the terminal phase of training. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md), only what their runs measured: three architectures with cross-entropy on seven balanced datasets without augmentation. This is the general law, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-789](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-789.md) | The block coarse-graining that maximizes mutual information with the system beyond a buffer picks out the renormalization-group-relevant variables in general, so those variables can be found from samples by information alone, without being known beforehand, as Koch-Janusz and Ringel propose | Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2017), [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md), propose that their mutual-information criterion finds a system's relevant degrees of freedom with no prior knowledge of them. What the record holds as shown, [THEORY-194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md), is that it recovered variables renormalization already uses, on 2D models whose answer was known. This is the general thesis that result was offered for, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-790](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-790.md) | In deep networks trained by SGD on real data, minibatch noise drives parameter groups related by a rescaling symmetry toward the point where their gradient noise balances, at a rate set by learning rate over batch size, so that at stationarity they sit neither where gradient flow would leave them nor spread out as under isotropic noise, as Ziyin, Li and Ueda propose | Ziyin, Li & Ueda, [LIT-1012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1012.md), read in [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md), with the Itô term from [LIT-1013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1013.md). The law of balance is proved in the SDE model of SGD, and that part is the Active [THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md). The authors present the law as general to networks with rescaling symmetry, but test it only on small synthetic networks. This THEORY holds the general claim, for deep networks on real data, which no measurement in the record yet supports. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-791](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-791.md) | The colour-naming systems of the world's languages lie near the information-bottleneck bound for compressing perceptual meanings into words, and differences in one trade-off parameter place each language along it, as Zaslavsky, Kemp, Regier and Tishby propose | Zaslavsky, Kemp, Regier & Tishby (2018), [LIT-810](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-810.md), read in [NOTE-631](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-631.md), using the bound of [LIT-338](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-338.md). Their fit covers the World Color Survey languages and English, with the need distribution over meanings estimated from the same naming data, and that measured part is the Active [THEORY-163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-163.md). The authors present the result as a property of the world's languages. This THEORY holds that general claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-792](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-792.md) | In a deep linear network trained by gradient descent from generic initial weights, not only from decoupled ones, depth slows learning through the initial end-to-end strength of each mode, so that random orthogonal weights, whose product is an isometry, learn in a number of iterations that stays bounded as depth grows, as Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli argue from simulation | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md), read in [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md). The exact depth law is proved only from decoupled, balanced starts, and that part is the Active [THEORY-187](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-187.md). Beyond it, the paper argues from MNIST runs and random-matrix simulations that random orthogonal layers are such a start in effect, because their product is an isometry, while scaled Gaussian layers are not. This THEORY holds that wider claim, which is argued and simulated and not derived. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-793](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-793.md) | Gradient flow on a symmetrized Barlow Twins loss with a linear or fixed-kernel model, from generic small initialization and not only from initialization aligned with the eigenvectors, learns the top eigenvectors of the pairs' symmetrized cross-correlation one at a time in order of eigenvalue and ends at a top spectral solution, as Simon and coauthors derive informally | Simon et al. (2023), [LIT-242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-242.md), read in [NOTE-741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-741.md). The stepwise dynamics, the minimum-norm end point and the kernel-PCA form are proved from aligned initialization, and that part is the Active [THEORY-229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-229.md). Generic small initialization rests on the paper's Result 4.6, which its authors style a result and derive informally in App. C, with numerical checks at d = 3. This THEORY holds that generic case. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-794](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-794.md) | In vision models, compositional generalization to unseen combinations of concepts is driven by the diversity of the combinations seen in training rather than by data volume, and arrives with representations that are linearly factored by concept, as Uselis, Dittadi and Oh propose | Uselis, Dittadi & Oh (2025), [LIT-667](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-667.md), read in [NOTE-525](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-525.md). Their title and abstract present diversity of combinations, not data volume, as what drives compositional generalization in vision models. Their evidence is ResNet-50s trained from scratch on two-concept grids, with checkpoints chosen on the unseen pairs, and that measured part, with the factorization theorem, is the Active [THEORY-117](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md). This THEORY holds the general causal claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-795](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-795.md) | On a contested shared canvas, the artworks that last are those whose coalitions keep repairing them under continual overwriting, not those left unattacked, as Wu and Silva propose from the 2017 r/place lifecycles | Wu & Silva (2024; v3 2026), [LIT-1032](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1032.md), read in [NOTE-724](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-724.md), claim C6 (weak). The persistence thesis drawn from ten illustrated lifecycles, filed apart from what the 2017 log measured ([THEORY-216](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-216.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. It is the population form of what [CLAIM-280](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-280.md) needs. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-796](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-796.md) | Question-order effects in surveys generally leave the probability of giving the same answer to both questions unchanged, the QQ equality that a projection model of judgment predicts, as Wang, Solloway, Shiffrin and Busemeyer propose | Wang, Solloway, Shiffrin & Busemeyer (2014), [LIT-795](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-795.md), after Wang & Busemeyer (2013), [LIT-834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-834.md). The general law the PNAS paper proposes, filed apart from what its 66 Pew surveys and 72 studies measured ([THEORY-166](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-166.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. The equality is a symmetry of Lüders projectors and a classical model with order events can meet it, so the law does not by itself favour quantum probability. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-797](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-797.md) | Deep classifiers trained with MSE loss stay near the least-squares classifier for their own features and move along the central path by the dynamics of continually renormalized gradient flow, whose equal-rate growth of the whitened class-separation singular values is how they reach neural collapse, as Han, Papyan and Donoho propose | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021; ICLR 2022), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). The paper's proposed explanation of neural collapse under MSE in real networks, filed apart from its measured central-path proximity and its derivation in a renormalized model ([THEORY-278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. Renormalization is imposed, not measured, and every experiment used weight decay, which the derivation excludes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-798](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-798.md) | Independently trained neural encoders of the same data learn latent spaces that differ mainly by an angle-preserving map, a rotation or reflection times a rescaling, so their cosine similarities to shared anchor samples agree across seeds, architectures and languages, as Moschella et al. propose | Moschella, Maiorca, Fumero, Norelli, Locatello & Rodolà (2022; ICLR 2023), [LIT-849](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-849.md), read in [NOTE-652](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-652.md). The hypothesis behind relative representations, filed apart from what their experiments measured ([THEORY-175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-175.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. The source assumes it and tests it only through its consequences; it never fits a map between two spaces. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-799](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-799.md) | Under geometric coarse-graining of the S¹ hidden-metric network model the average degree flows as r^ν, with ν = 2/(γ − 1) − 1 when the degree exponent γ sets it and 2/β − 1 when β does, so the coarse-grained networks run toward a complete graph for γ < 3 or β < 2 and toward a ring otherwise | The degree flow that [THEORY-190](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-190.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 048) narrowed it to the asymptotic closure of the S¹ connection law. García-Pérez, Boguñá and Serrano (2017), [LIT-869](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-869.md), derive it to first order by treating the coarse-grained graph as an S¹ model at every separation. The record's exact computation shows that treatment fails between nearby supernodes, so the flow is unproved. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-800](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-800.md) | A network of N threshold units with symmetric Hebbian couplings stores random patterns as attractors up to a load proportional to N, about 0.15N for all large N, past which recall fails for every pattern at once, and a provision for forgetting old memories, such as couplings that saturate, keeps the most recent ones retrievable however many are added | The large-N and forgetting clauses that [THEORY-272](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-272.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 051) narrowed it to Hopfield's simulations at N = 30 and 100. Hopfield (1982), [LIT-918](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-918.md), expects the 0.15N figure "for all large N" from a crosstalk estimate, and states in words that overload makes every memory irretrievable unless old ones are forgotten, with saturating couplings as the mechanism. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-801](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-801.md) | Agents are the systems that would adapt their policy were their actions to affect the world differently, so the agent is wherever that adaptation is: a thermostat is not an agent while it together with its design process is, an RL training process is while its learnt policy generally is not, and humans are | The definition and verdicts [THEORY-527](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-527.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 055) narrowed it to the recovery theorem. Kenton, Kumar, Farquhar, Richens, MacDermott and Everitt (2022), [LIT-909](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-909.md), propose the definition and argue the verdicts from it in §1 and §4; that it "reliably classifies humans as agents" is asserted. The verdicts are relative to the variables chosen, which the paper states. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-802](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-802.md) v2 | In trained networks as in constructed ones, interchange interventions on a fixed set of variables can be satisfied equally by alignments related by a change of basis, so which internal direction mediates a high-level variable is fixed only relative to a chosen decomposition into units, and complex models will generally have several distinct, fully correct abstractions | The general reading that [THEORY-243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the three-unit network it proves (batch 062). Wu et al. (2024), [LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md), conjecture that complex models have "multiple distinct fully correct abstractions" and that the causal-abstraction framework cannot settle structural equivalence; Makelov et al. (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), §8, grant that crossing component boundaries makes "illusory" tenuous, and answer by privileging components. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. Its only support is the constructed tie. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-803](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-803.md) | Real complex networks embedded in the hyperbolic plane are self-similar under geometric renormalization, their coarse-grained layers keeping the degree distribution, clustering and degree–degree correlations of the original, and this self-similarity is evidence that a hidden metric space underlies them | The empirical claim [THEORY-190](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-190.md) set aside when the promotion audit (batch 048) narrowed it to the model. García-Pérez, Boguñá and Serrano (2017), [LIT-869](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-869.md), find six embedded real networks self-similar under the renormalization and call this new evidence of hidden metric spaces. The collapse was judged by eye over two to five layers with no null ordering of the circle. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-804](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-804.md) | Ince's common change in surprisal is a correct measure of the redundancy among any number of sources, and the negative partial-information atoms it gives are local misinformation and mechanistic redundancy, not defects of the measure | The thesis [THEORY-714](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-714.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 056) corrected and narrowed it to what I_ccs is and which properties it has. Ince (2017), [LIT-1201](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1201.md), proposes I_ccs as the redundancy measure and reads its negative atoms as misinformation and mechanistic redundancy. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. The re-derivation found that I_ccs fails subset equality, the property Ince argues licenses the lattice, which counts against the thesis without settling it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-805](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-805.md) | Volume-maximizing joint-embedding objectives as a class, VICReg and SimCLR as well as MSN and SwAV, carry a prior toward equal-sized clusters, and that prior costs them semantic transfer when the pretraining data are class-imbalanced, including on naturally long-tailed data | The general reading that [THEORY-306](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-306.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the explicit priors of MSN and SwAV and to one experiment with two to eight classes per batch (batch 033). Assran et al. (2022), [LIT-231](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-231.md), read in [NOTE-850](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-850.md), argue the prior for the whole class, VICReg through an informal reduction to K-means and SimCLR through a cited equivalence, and read it as the cause of the degradation reported on real long-tailed data. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-806](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-806.md) | Translation without parallel data, as of an unknown animal communication system into a human language, is learnable from a plausibility prior over the target language alone, with error falling as the common ground between the languages grows and as the source language grows richer | The general reading that [THEORY-270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-270.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the common-nonsense model its bound is proved in (batch 044). Goldwasser, Gruber, Kalai and Paradise (NeurIPS 2023), [LIT-941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-941.md), read in [NOTE-804](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-804.md), motivate their framework by translating animal communication and state its lesson for translation in general, while saying their stylised models are not intended to capture natural language. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-807](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-807.md) | The guppy-type overextension in Hampton's membership data arises because a combined concept is in part a new, emergent concept and not only a logical combination of its parts, so human concept combination runs in two superposed layers, one classical and logical and one quantum and conceptual | Aerts's reading, which [THEORY-255](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-255.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit narrowed it (batch 018) to the impossibility Theorem 9 proves. Aerts (2009), [LIT-934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-934.md), read in [NOTE-808](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-808.md), fits the ∆-type deviations with one emergent subspace per pair and reads thought as two superposed layers. The narrowing was right that the theorem does not force an emergent concept, only dropping the meet or the monotone weight; this entry is the emergence reading as Aerts's thesis. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-808](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-808.md) | Transformers trained by next-token prediction on sequence processes whose latent dynamics factor as a tensor product learn to represent the belief state in approximately orthogonal per-factor subspaces of about the factored dimension rather than the joint one, and reach that factored representation first even when noise makes it lossy | The general reading that [THEORY-256](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-256.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the five Mess3 and Bloch Walk factors and the 4-layer GPT-2-style models tested (batch 019). Shai et al.
