(2026), [LIT-986](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-986.md), read in [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md), present next-token training (the paper is titled “Transformers learn factored representations”) as yielding factored, orthogonal belief representations; [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md)'s claims C2 to C4 are each shown on one family of synthetic processes. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. It does not include the paper's inference that the preference is architectural (C5), which App. D.4 leaves open, or the claim that the factored form persists at convergence under strong noise, which Fig. 12 contradicts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-809](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-809.md) | Language models trained by gradient descent on a mixture of random facts and other data reach the capacity-optimal allocation, so the model size and the mixing ratio at which they begin to learn the facts are those of an optimal capacity-bounded learner | The link that [THEORY-293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-293.md)'s title asserted before the promotion audit narrowed it (batch 036) to the optimal learner's theorem and the observation of a threshold in Pythia models. Gu, Lyu, Li and Zhang (2025), [LIT-984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-984.md), read in [NOTE-796](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-796.md), explain the trained models' thresholds by the optimal learner's. The one quantitative check, a size exponent of 1.152 against a predicted 1.283, is recorded against it. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-810](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-810.md) | Prediction-market prices keep much of an arbitrary price shock that no trader's information supports for weeks, rather than correcting it within a short transition phase | The general reading that [THEORY-267](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-267.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the 817 Manifold play-money markets measured. Rasooly and Rozzi (2025), [LIT-958](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-958.md), read in [NOTE-778](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-778.md), set the result against the received view (Wolfers and Zitzewitz, 2004) that manipulation matters only briefly, and offer it as a finding about prediction markets. Their evidence is one platform, at play-money stakes. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-811](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-811.md) | With a kernel normalised to unit diagonal, the kernel quantum relative entropy of two distributions is within O(σ²) of their Kullback–Leibler divergence as the bandwidth σ shrinks, for translation-invariant kernels on the torus generally and for kernels on other compact groups | The general reading that [THEORY-313](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-313.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the one kernel family on the torus that the rate is shown for. Bach (2022), [LIT-255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-255.md), read in [NOTE-837](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-837.md), asserts that other translation-invariant kernels and kernels on compact groups behave alike, and sketches a leverage-score argument without completing it. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-812](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-812.md) | As dimension grows with the undersampling and sparsity ratios fixed, the ℓ₁ phase transition for recovering sparse vectors from random measurements sits at the same curve for a broad class of random-matrix ensembles, those with a kind of orthogonality or weak independence, as for Gaussian matrices, while differing at finite size | The general reading that [THEORY-391](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-391.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to what 2,948,000 optimizations at three problem sizes showed. Donoho and Tanner (2009), [LIT-1160](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1160.md), read in [NOTE-933](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-933.md), state it as the hypothesis of "weak universality" and pose the class of ensembles it holds for as an open problem. Nothing about non-Gaussian ensembles is proved. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-813](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-813.md) | Training a wide network in the lazy, kernel regime does not make its features more collapsed than at initialization, so neural collapse, where it occurs, is something only feature learning produces | The general reading that [THEORY-294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-294.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the one-dimensional, zero-bias, two-class case it proves. Kothapalli and Tirer (2024), [LIT-985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-985.md), read in [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md), draw it as their conclusion: the lazy regime does not collapse anything, so the data-dependence of collapse has to come from a kernel that moves with the data. Beyond the solved case their support is simulation on two-class Gaussian data, where the NTK comes out less collapsed than the NNGP. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-814](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-814.md) | In scientific communities that settle on a consensus model by sound model comparisons, high reproducibility of results is not evidence that the consensus is true, because which alternatives get proposed can hold a false consensus whose results reproduce almost perfectly | The general reading that [THEORY-295](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-295.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the memoryless consensus model it proves. Devezer, Nardin, Baumgaertner and Buzbas (2019), [LIT-988](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-988.md), read in [NOTE-792](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-792.md), present the decoupling of reproducibility from truth as a lesson for science, not only for their model. Their model has no beliefs, no learning and no memory in the consensus. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-815](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-815.md) | Layering a navigable small-world graph on nested random subsets of the data, with links separated by length scale and each layer's degree capped, makes greedy nearest-neighbour search cost grow logarithmically with the number of items on data of low intrinsic dimension, where the single-layer graph's cost grows polylogarithmically | Malkov and Yashunin (2020), [LIT-1098](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1098.md), read in [NOTE-916](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-916.md), argue that HNSW's hierarchy is what makes greedy search logarithmic: constant cost per layer over O(log N) layers, against the polylogarithmic cost of their earlier flat graph. The record holds as measured, in [THEORY-365](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-365.md), logarithmic-or-better cost on uniform data in 8 dimensions and a saturating beam width in 4. The bound is derived only for exact Delaunay layers, which HNSW does not build, and on 200 million SIFT vectors the paper's own scaling departs from a logarithm, so the thesis is stated for low intrinsic dimension. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-816](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-816.md) | Learners inferring what a novel word means from its use reason about a speaker who chose the word to be informative about the referent, so the size principle in word learning is a consequence of that inference and not a separate rule of generalisation | Frank, Goodman, Lai and Tenenbaum (2009), [LIT-824](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-824.md), read in [NOTE-627](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-627.md), derive the size principle from an informative speaker and present the word learner as inverting that speaker. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-472](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-472.md), the derivation and one experiment in which mean bets matched the inversion; in those displays an informative-speaker learner and a plain size-principle learner coincide, so whether learners reason about the speaker is open. [THEORY-785](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-785.md) is the same inversion for listeners in reference games. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-817](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-817.md) | Once an agent's actions affect the percepts it receives, maximal prediction of those percepts is generally not what thermodynamic efficiency requires: in percept-action loops with feedback, maximally predictive agents generally extract less work than the most efficient agent | Fiderer et al. (2025), [LIT-041](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-041.md), read in [NOTE-032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-032.md), prove that without feedback the work-efficient agents are exactly the maximally predictive ones that randomise and forget their actions, and that with feedback one binary memoryless channel separates predictive, max-entropy-action and efficient agents; from that they assert that with feedback maximally predictive agents are generally inefficient. The record holds as proved, in [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md), only the one channel. It does not say that efficiency under feedback is a trade-off between prediction and forgetting: in the proved example the efficient agent is memoryless. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-818](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-818.md) | In two-scale Lorenz 96 without time-scale separation (ε = 0.5, K = 18, J = 20, F = 10), a discrete-time closure for each resolved variable that fits the one-step discrepancy of a fourth-order Runge–Kutta step as a NARMAX series, with one autoregressive lag, at most two lags of the resolved variable and at most one moving-average term, reproduces the mean, spread, distribution, autocorrelation and neighbour cross-correlation of x₁ (Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance 0.005) and, with observations every 0.05, extends the 20-member ensemble forecast lead time at anomaly correlation 0.6 from 2 to 4 time units over a polynomial-plus-AR(1) closure; the model structure was chosen by trial and error, differs between the two observation spacings, and carries no error bound | Chorin and Lu (2015), [LIT-1304](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1304.md), read in [NOTE-1028](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1028.md). A data-driven closure with one or two steps of discrete memory, plus one moving-average innovation, is enough on this test to reproduce the resolved statistics and to double forecast skill against a memoryless-in-x closure. It is the record's first evidence that a short discrete memory suffices in a chaotic system with no scale gap. It is one system, the structure was tuned, and there is no bound, so it does not give the controlled prediction error [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) asks for. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-821](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-821.md) | For every α < 1/15 there are weak solutions of the 3D incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box, Hölder-continuous of exponent α in space and time, that satisfy the local energy inequality; in the construction their dissipation measure is a nonnegative function of time alone, equal at each time to the rate at which the total energy falls, zero while the local energy equality holds and positive on all of space during a short final interval in which the solution's energy is drained to zero; uncountably many such solutions share one initial datum and one dissipation measure; for them the local coarse-grained energy flux into vanishing scales converges to that measure, so the transfer is one-way at every place and time in the limit and spread uniformly over the box, with its timing chosen by the construction, not forced by the equations | Isett (2017; ARMA 2022), [LIT-1305](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1305.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1027](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1027.md): the first continuous, indeed C^α with α < 1/15, weak Euler solutions satisfying the local energy inequality with nonzero dissipation, and a Cantor family of them sharing one initial datum and one dissipation measure. In the construction the dissipation measure is a function of time alone, so in the limit of vanishing scale the energy flux runs one way at every place, as in [THEORY-772](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-772.md), but in a Hölder class and spread uniformly over the torus rather than set in pipes. It is switched on only while the constructor drains the solution's energy to zero at the end of its life. Where, when and how fast the energy goes are inputs; the exponent is far from 1/3; nothing ties these solutions to Navier–Stokes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-823](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-823.md) | Tetris players rotate pieces more often than planning a placement and then executing it would require, rotate them early and check the column more the higher the drop, because these moves are epistemic actions: physical action that stands in for mental computation at the moment of use | Kirsh and Maglio (1994), [LIT-1054](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1054.md), read in full in [NOTE-878](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-878.md), with Kirsh (1995), [LIT-1076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1076.md), read in [NOTE-871](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-871.md), argue that the extra, early and checking moves of Tetris players are epistemic actions: physical moves whose primary function is to cut the space, time or unreliability of the player's own computation. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-360](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-360.md), only the early-rotation timing and the drop-length difference after the wall check. Over-rotation and the rise of the check with drop height rest on figures without printed numbers, and the saving is argued from a three-player pilot, not measured. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-824](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-824.md) | Economics working papers increasingly back their claims with design-based identification: in NBER and CEPR working papers the share of claims supported by difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, an RCT, regression discontinuity or synthetic control rose about fourfold from 1990 to 2020 | Garg and Fetzer (2024; arXiv v2 2026), [LIT-079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-079.md), read in full in [NOTE-083](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-083.md), read the rise in their extraction's design-backed share as a change in economics: "economic papers have increasingly incorporated causal inference methods to substantiate their claims over the past three decades". The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-674](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-674.md), only the extraction's series, whose edges were never checked against human labels and whose per-decade slope nearly vanishes with method-mix and graph-volume controls. This is the paper's reading, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-825](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-825.md) | Hyperbolic graph embedding models trained on task losses that never mention the hierarchy do not place a tree's root nearest the origin, and their distance from the origin orders hierarchical levels only partly | Yang, Zhou, Ying, Chen & King (2023), [LIT-871](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-871.md), read in [NOTE-669](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-669.md), assert for hyperbolic graph models in general what they measured for HGCN on two synthetic trees: the root is not innermost and radius reads level only partly. The general form was the lead clause of [THEORY-421](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-421.md) until that account was narrowed to the measurement on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4); it is filed here so that it stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-826](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-826.md) | In work groups, a member's displayed mood spreads to the others, and pleasant emotional contagion improves the group's cooperation and reduces its conflict | Barsade (2002), [LIT-706](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-706.md), read in [NOTE-551](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-551.md), presents emotional contagion as a general phenomenon of work groups and states its effect on group process causally: "this contagion improved cooperation, decreased conflict". The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-123](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-123.md), only what her two studies measured: ad hoc student groups, one actor as the source, and a process link that is a correlation with measured contagion. This is her wider claim, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-827](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-827.md) | The rubber hand illusion is a perceptual illusion driven by multisensory integration: the difference in reports between synchronous and asynchronous brushing is produced by the stimulation, not by participants' expectations | Ehrsson et al. (2022), [LIT-1264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1264.md), read in [NOTE-997](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-997.md), conclude that the rubber hand illusion is a perceptual illusion driven primarily by multisensory mechanisms ([NOTE-997](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-997.md), C8), from the synchrony difference's independence of hypnotisability in Lush et al.'s 353 participants. Lush and Seth's reply, [LIT-1267](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1267.md), shows that uniform but unequal expectations predict the same null. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-766](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-766.md), only the report differences and that the standard controls do not equalise expectations. This is the perceptual reading, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when that narrowing set it aside. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-828](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-828.md) | Fine-tuning from one pretrained model typically lands near the edge of a task-specific low-loss region in weight space that contains the convex hull of the fine-tuned models, and averaging their weights, as model soups and stochastic weight averaging do, works by moving inward | Gueta, Venezian, Raffel, Slonim, Katz and Choshen (2023), [LIT-658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-658.md), read in [NOTE-515](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-515.md), conclude that fine-tuning "typically" yields models on the boundary of a region whose centre is better, and read model soups and SWA as picking points inside it (§§8–9). The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-105](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-105.md), only the probe-loss comparisons of hull points with members and the BitFit result, for RoBERTa-base on English classification. This is their geometric thesis, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-830](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-830.md) | In human visual cortex the content of a sustained seen image is carried by a stable population code that lasts as long as the image, not by a sustained level of activity, and frontoparietal cortex marks only its onset; so a sustained experience rests on sensory representation and its discrete updates on frontoparietal representation | Vishne, Gerber, Knight and Deouell (2023), [LIT-644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-644.md), read in full in [NOTE-499](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-499.md), conclude from their intracranial recordings that sustained visual experience may rest on a stable sensory representation, with frontoparietal representation serving discrete updates, and propose a stable "experience subspace". Their measurement, in ten patients and for images up to 1.5 s, is the Active [THEORY-102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-102.md). This is the general claim that measurement was filed to support, held Proposed until a second method or cohort and a case where percept and input come apart test it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-832](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-832.md) | For strict combining functions and m attribute-sorted lists of N objects whose orderings are probabilistically independent, no correct top-k algorithm does essentially better than Fagin's Algorithm in the worst case with high probability: every one needs on the order of N^((m−1)/m) k^(1/m) accesses | Fagin (1996/1999), [LIT-1108](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1108.md), as reported by Fagin, Lotem and Naor (2001), [LIT-1115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1115.md), Sections 1 and 3, read in [NOTE-924](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-924.md): "his algorithm is optimal with high probability in the worst case if the aggregation function is strict ... and if the orderings in the sorted lists are probabilistically independent." Strict means the combined grade is 1 exactly when every grade is 1. Not read in the original; not re-derived. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-834](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-834.md) | A member of a discipline who has been trained into its paradigms yet remains rooted in experience those paradigms omit or distort is better placed than its insiders to perceive those omissions and distortions as anomalies, and better placed than outsiders who share the experience to have them taken up, because insiders share the assumptions that produced the anomalies and outsiders lack the professional authority to press them | Collins (1986), [LIT-1312](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1312.md), read in an authorized Portuguese translation in [NOTE-1042](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1042.md): the "outsider within". An argument from the sociology of knowledge and Kuhn, illustrated by anomalies Black feminist sociologists did detect. It does not say that every outsider within sees them, that insiders cannot, or that what the outsider within reports is true; and it offers no comparison of who detects what. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-838](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-838.md) | The emphasis the news media give to issues raises the importance their audiences assign those issues, independently of any change in the audiences' attitudes toward the issues: the media influence what people think about more than what they think | The agenda-setting hypothesis, as McCombs and Shaw (1972), [LIT-1335](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1335.md), state it after Cohen and the Langs, read in [NOTE-1046](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1046.md). Their evidence is an aggregate correlation in one sample, held as [THEORY-842](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-842.md); the direction from media to public is argued there, not identified. The later literature the programme produced is not read here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-841](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-841.md) | Knowledge of the particular circumstances of time and place is held dispersed among many people and cannot be conveyed to a central authority in statistical form, so decisions that depend on it are better taken by those who hold it, and a price system lets them fit their decisions together by conveying the relative scarcities each needs without the causes behind them | Hayek (1945), [LIT-1337](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1337.md), read in [NOTE-1036](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1036.md). An argument, not a result: the essay gives examples (the tin shortage, the shipper, the arbitrageur) and an analogy to the rates of substitution a single mind uses, and no model of how well prices convey what decisions need. It says nothing about what prices fail to carry, and it does not argue that removing any particular public constraint decentralizes decisions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-852](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-852.md) | Under Szeidl and Szucs's structural model and its identifying assumptions (an owner's ideology fixed across episodes; the government's online advertising budget not driven by the outlets' slant), both owner ideology and favor exchange drove the Hungarian portal Origo's reduced coverage of corruption in 2013–2016: favor exchange alone cut it by 29–44%, the new owner's ideology alone by 63% after 2016, and the two together by 74%, so they are substitutes; and a ban on targeted government advertising would have raised it by 41–79% | Szeidl and Szucs (2021), [LIT-1315](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1315.md), read in [NOTE-1039](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1039.md). Table IV's estimates (weight on profit β ≈ 1.4–1.6, government preference for slant δ ≈ 420–510, both with intervals excluding zero) and Table V's decomposition and counterfactual ban. Conditional on a static model per episode, on advertising being the only reward and corruption coverage the only slant, and on the identifying assumptions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-853](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-853.md) | Giving players more information shrinks what an information designer can make them do: for one player, being more informative in Blackwell's sense, being a garbling's source and leaving a smaller set of Bayes correlated equilibria in every decision problem are the same order; for many players the incentive order is individual sufficiency, which neither implies nor is implied by sufficiency of the players' joint information | Bergemann and Morris (2019), [LIT-1313](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1313.md), read in [NOTE-1034](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1034.md), §4.2. A third face of Blackwell's order: the better-informed receiver is the harder one to steer. For many players the right order is not the statistical sufficiency of their joint information. Bayesian players only; for bounded ones a garbling can make a receiver easier to steer and easier to inform at once. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-854](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-854.md) v2 | A public ranking can raise its own validity through the reactions it provokes: where a unit's published rank affects the inputs to its next rank, as when applicants choose by rank and their choices feed the selectivity score, or raters who know little but the last rank fill the reputation survey, rank differences that began as measurement noise can become real differences that the ranking then correctly reports | Espeland and Sauder (2007), [LIT-1330](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1330.md), read in [NOTE-1050](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1050.md). The paper defines self-fulfilling prophecy so that it covers reactions that "increase the validity of the measure by encouraging behavior that conforms to it", and points to two channels that close through the ranking's own inputs. The paper does not measure either channel. Nor does it show that the starting differences were noise rather than quality, beyond citing Sauder and Lancaster. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-857](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-857.md) | Remedies for algorithmic governance offered as access or as transparency can run against the people they are meant to serve: inclusion in a data system also gives its operators access to the included, and transparency can be demanded of the governed while the governing system stays opaque, so what an access or transparency remedy does depends on who is made visible to whom | James, Hynes, Whelan, Dreher and Humphry (2023), [LIT-1342](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1342.md), read in [NOTE-1041](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1041.md). "Access is however bidirectional, and access 'down' for powerful players is politically consequential"; under Robo-debt transparency "was arguably demanded of welfare recipients". The paper does not show that such remedies usually backfire, or say when they will. It also does not claim that transparency is worthless. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-858](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-858.md) | Insulating a regulator from future political revision fixes in place the interests of whoever designs the insulated regime: it relieves the underinvestment that electoral pressure on prices causes when the designers serve consumers, and entrenches capture, removing the electoral pressure that would correct it, when they serve the regulated industry | Schram and Ule (2024), [LIT-1340](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1340.md), read in [NOTE-1053](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1053.md). The authors' general conclusion. Its evidence is one laboratory study in which capture was assigned and independence was a fixed price, so it says nothing yet about real independent agencies, about how capture arises, or about designs between the two extremes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-859](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-859.md) | Regulatory capture can operate through the evaluative framework a regulator adopts rather than through its decisions: when experts design a standard from an ideologically motivated view of the public interest that consistently marginalizes important public values, outcomes can favour an interest with no lobbying or improper exchange; US antitrust's consumer welfare standard is offered as a strong case | Short, Hill and Brown (2025), [LIT-1327](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1327.md), read in [NOTE-1051](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1051.md). The definition is theirs; the evidence for the case is their survey ([THEORY-833](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-833.md), Active) and a history drawn from secondary sources. It does not say that every expert–public disagreement is capture, that capture is always wrong (its strength depends on the experts' claim to truth and on whether public views were heard), or that the mechanism is a self-reinforcing loop. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-864](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-864.md) | When a generative model reproduces a prejudiced narrative learned from its training data, the resulting testimonial injustice runs through a credibility excess assigned to the model, so that hearers believe the amplified account over the testimony of those it discredits, rather than through a hearer's prejudiced judgement of a present speaker | Kay, Kasirzadeh and Mohamed (2024), [LIT-1338](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1338.md), read in [NOTE-1049](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1049.md): "In the algorithmic setting, the injustice requires a credibility excess assigned to the algorithm". A conceptual analysis, illustrated with reported cases. It does not say that users do overtrust models (the paper measures nothing), that deliberate fabrication is testimonial injustice in Fricker's sense, or that the amplification is a loop with any stated condition. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-865](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-865.md) | In Claude language models, a sparse set of residual-stream directions that a corpus-averaged Jacobian lens identifies as verbalizable (the J-space) is causally privileged for verbal report, for holding instructed concepts, for unspoken intermediate steps of reasoning and for passing one argument to many functions, while continuation, anomaly detection and line wrapping use the same information without routing through it; it carries workspace-like content only in a middle band of layers, holds on the order of tens of active directions and under a tenth of activation variance, and is amplified and relayed by the weights more than other directions | Gurnee, Sofroniew et al. (2026), [LIT-1347](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1347.md), read in [NOTE-1069](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1069.md) (main text in full, appendices in part). It is the functional analogue of conscious access, in the access sense only, found in a transformer and tested by intervention. The sharp edge: one company's models studied by that company, a lens whose own statistics draw the layer band, a flexible/automatic split partly defined by the result, and an explicit refusal to say anything about phenomenal consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-866](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-866.md) | Expert texts of Shamatha, Transcendental and Stillness Meditation describe their so-called contentless goal-states as lacking thoughts, perceptions, images and memories but keeping many forms of content, and as differing across the practices in attentional stability and vividness | Woods, Windt & Carter (2022), [LIT-1351](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1351.md), read in the submitted preprint in [NOTE-1070](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1070.md). An evidence synthesis of 135 texts by eight teachers codes 65 features of the goal-states: the same across practices on 14, different on 4, unclear on 47. The states lack everyday content but keep wakefulness, calm, stillness, bliss, knowing, freedom and unity; Shamatha's has far greater attentional stability and vividness. The sharp edge: it is a finding about how teachers describe the states, not about what practitioners experience, and "not truly contentless" depends on counting calm or simplicity as content. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-867](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-867.md) v2 | The geometry of the colour similarity space does not mark the four unique hues, nor the difference between the black–white axis, along which every grey is a mixture of both ends, and the opponent axes, along which each half shows only one end; so a structuralism on which phenomenal character is fixed by similarity relations alone cannot account for how colour experiences are composed | Aldé (2026), [LIT-1348](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1348.md), read in full in [NOTE-1055](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1055.md). Two arguments, the unique hues objection and the opposing dimensions objection, from colour facts the paper takes as accepted. The decisive premise of each, that no adequate geometric property marks the facts, rests on inspection of CIELAB and extrapolation to better models; no analysis is reported. The target is similarity structuralism only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-868](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-868.md) v2 | The structuralist methods and evidence in consciousness science support only that experiences have structure or stand in relations to other experiences, not that an experience is nothing but its relations; the stronger, metaphysical thesis implies that relational knowledge fixes what an experience is like, that every new experience changes all the others, and that a system with a single experience is impossible, and each consequence is doubtful | Negro (2025), [LIT-1346](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1346.md), read in full in [NOTE-1054](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1054.md). The distinctions (three structuralisms; having, being in and being a structure) are sound and the arguments valid. Each argument's decisive premise is an intuition or a conceivability claim, and a structuralist such as Lyre ([THEORY-880](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-880.md)) accepts the holism Negro takes to be absurd. The paper also says that making judgement constitutive saves the view only by aligning it with eliminativism, which bears directly on [CLAIM-412](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-869](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-869.md) | In Claude language models, projecting out the most active J-space directions in early workspace layers lowers the rate of felt, first-person, sensory language in the models' narrations of their own processing and in their descriptions of another person's experience, while norm-matched perturbations along other directions do not and the text stays coherent; so in these models the experiential register of report depends on the access-like workspace and is not specific to self-report | Gurnee, Sofroniew et al. (2026), [LIT-1347](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1347.md), §3.5.3 and §A.23, read in [NOTE-1069](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1069.md). The authors conclude that "the J-space supports the model's propensity to provide rich experiential reports, whether about itself or another entity". The sharp edge: the measure is a register of text graded by another model, on five or six prompts per condition, in one company's models; and the effect holds for reports about others, so it is not evidence of anything the self-reports are about. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-870](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-870.md) | Experienced Transcendental Meditation practitioners report more pure awareness than matched counting controls, and multivariate EEG separates the meditation period from counting and from rest, but the reports are not shown to track any EEG feature | Chandia-Jorquera et al. (2026), [LIT-1354](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1354.md), read in the bioRxiv v3 preprint in [NOTE-1058](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1058.md). 33 practitioners against 33 matched controls who counted: higher and more variable retrospective pure-awareness traces (d = 0.77, 1.32); 65% balanced accuracy separating meditation from counting, on entropy and aperiodic EEG; 88% sensitivity separating meditation from rest, on low-frequency phase coherence. The sharp edge: the authors found no robust association between the reports and the EEG, so this is a finding about a practice period and about reports, not a neural signature of an experience with little content. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-871](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-871.md) | Instructed reappraisal lowers reported negative affect to aversive pictures while the responses of the amygdala, periaqueductal gray, hypothalamus and other subcortical regions to the same pictures show evidence of no change; the regions it reduces are cortical, mainly higher visual and parietal | Bo et al. (preprint 2023, published 2024), [LIT-1359](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1359.md), read in full from the bioRxiv v2 preprint in [NOTE-1061](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1061.md). Reported negative affect fell under reappraisal (d = 0.92, n = 358). Every subcortical region engaged by negative pictures, amygdala subregions and PAG included, showed 10:1 evidence of no change under reappraisal, as did most cortical emotion-responsive regions; the eight regions reduced were all cortical. BOLD and one rating per trial; it does not show that the unchanged response is part of what is felt, though the authors write as if it were. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-872](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-872.md) | A self-model compresses the sensory effects of a system's own activity by positing one stable common cause, at fast and slow timescales; there is such a pattern in the signal, so the self is real as a pattern and unreal as a substance, and realists and anti-realists about selves who accept this agree on the facts and differ on the criterion of reality | Gładziejewski (2025), [LIT-1360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1360.md), read in full in [NOTE-1056](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1056.md), §4.1, after Hohwy & Michael (2017) and Letheby & Gerrans (2017), neither of which the record holds. An interpretation, not a result. The paper calls its self section "an initial sketch". It does not say that the self-model exaggerates the self's unity, though the exchange that filed the work said so. It says the single common cause is a compression, and that the verdict on selves turns on criteria. Its one candidate for a self-model that misdescribes is a dissociative case better compressed by two narrative selves. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-873](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-873.md) | Claims to be conscious are produced by an automatic internal model, and since such models are schematic, the intangible, what-it-is-like essence people report is that model's caricature of a real process, proposed to be attention, or the deep selective processing of information that attention, the global workspace and integration share; a theory that explains how neurons produce a feeling without explaining how the feeling comes to be encoded for report (Arrow B) does not explain the reports | Graziano (2024), [LIT-1358](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1358.md), read in full in [NOTE-1071](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1071.md): the attention schema theory and its "deep illusionism", in an essay with no new data. Arrow B is an argument. The identification of the target with attention rests on covariation with report cited from others, and the merging of attention, workspace and integration is asserted. Its "small" illusionism keeps the modelled process real and denies the reported phenomenal essence, so it is the strong illusionism of [THEORY-633](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-633.md) with a named target, not the weak kind. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-874](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-874.md) | Whether a view of mind is organicist or informationalist is a dimension orthogonal to whether it is cognitivist or embodied, and the enactive approach of The Embodied Mind is set apart from other embodied views by organicism with experiential primacy and reciprocity, not by sensorimotor emphasis | Ward (2026), [LIT-1356](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1356.md), read in the accepted manuscript in [NOTE-1065](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1065.md). Views differ on where cognition's processes are (skull or brain–body–world) and, separately, on what the meaning of mental states depends on (information, or organization distinctive of the living). Embodied predictive processing, extended functionalism and cybernetics are embodied and informationalist; the enactive approach is organicist, and further marked by experiential primacy and reciprocity. The sharp edge: it is a taxonomy argued from examples and exegesis. It does not argue that organicism is true, and the line between distinctive and characteristic properties of life is left without a criterion. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-875](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-875.md) | Phenomenal binding of the parts of an experience can be modelled as agreement, on overlaps, of measured similarity structures assigned to the parts by a presheaf, and the broad quale is fixed by its parts exactly when that presheaf is a sheaf; a sheaf failure may mark disunity, as proposed for binocular rivalry, or context dependence within one unified experience, as in the Ebbinghaus illusion, and the framework does not yet say which | Lee-Youngzie, Tsuchiya, Robinson, Dietz & Monti (2026), [LIT-1352](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1352.md), read in full in [NOTE-1059](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1059.md). A hypothesis article with no data. It proposes the presheaf and two readings of its failure, disunity for rivalry and context dependence for the Ebbinghaus illusion, without a criterion between them. It does not identify unity with a global section, since it assumes unity always holds. Its global section is measured data, its worked topology example is malformed, and by its own definition of gluing the rivalry case is not a sheaf failure. It answers [QUESTION-255](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-255.md) only by showing that a sheaf failure need not be disunity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-876](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-876.md) | Phenomenal consciousness is the coherent functioning of an embodied agent's generative model of its sensorium, coherent in space, time and cause and run either coupled to sense data (perception) or decoupled from it (imagination); embodied grounding, the model's capacity to inform and be informed by action–perception cycles at behavioural timescales and the history of such coupling by which it was learned, is necessary, so that integrated information or a functional global workspace without it does not suffice | Safron, Klimaj & Sheikhbahaee (2026), [LIT-1345](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1345.md), read in full in [NOTE-1057](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1057.md): Integrated World Modeling Theory as restated in a symposium paper, whose earlier, fuller statements (Safron 2020–2023) were not read. Asserted, not argued here. The sharp edge is that the theory does not require current sensory coupling, so its quarrel with grounding- free accounts is about developmental grounding and the capacity for coupling. "Embodied grounding" comes in "sufficient degrees (and kinds)", with no threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-877](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-877.md) | Learning a generative model of sensory data extracts real patterns in Dennett's sense, so the manifest image is a structural description of the sensory signal, constrained by its external source but silent on what realizes the structure; two subjects whose sensory streams match, one envatted, therefore have equally veridical manifest images, and what differs between them, the realizers, lies outside what perception can represent | Gładziejewski (2025), [LIT-1360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1360.md), read in full in [NOTE-1056](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1056.md), §§2–3, drawing on Chalmers's structuralism and veridicalism (2018, 2022), which the record does not hold. The cognitive half rests on a realist reading of predictive processing and on an analogy between free energy and description length. The veridicalism follows only if manifest content is wholly structural, which is assumed. Projective properties (cuteness) are allowed at one end of a continuum. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-878](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-878.md) | Instructed reappraisal of aversive pictures engages anterior prefrontal, temporo-parietal and cerebellar regions that show evidence of no response to negative emotion generation, beside a larger set of regions engaged both by generation and by reappraisal: in this task part of regulation runs in regions apart from generation, and most of it in regions shared with it | Bo et al. (preprint 2023, published 2024), [LIT-1359](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1359.md), read in full from the bioRxiv v2 preprint in [NOTE-1061](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1061.md). Two fMRI samples (n = 182 and 176), voxelwise Bayes factors, every effect replicated in both. Sixteen regions are engaged by reappraisal and show 10:1 evidence of no response to negative against neutral pictures without it; fourteen, the larger set, are engaged by both. The selective set best predicts how much reported negative affect falls. One instructed strategy, one stimulus type, BOLD only; nothing shows the selective regions do the regulating. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-879](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-879.md) | Representing a sensory quality, even in the distinctively sensory way, does not make there be something it is like for the subject to have it: a quality can occur unnoticed, as for an absent-minded driver, so what it is like to experience a quality is a further property that needs awareness, and a representational theory of sensory qualities leaves open what makes a state experienced | Lycan (2000; rev. 2023), [LIT-1355](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1355.md), read in full in [NOTE-1068](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1068.md). The entry defends the distinction in its own voice (§4.2, §5.1), crediting Carruthers (2000) for the distinction and Armstrong, Nelkin, Rosenthal and Lycan for the claim that qualities can go unnoticed. It is argued, not shown. Its one case, the driver "on autopilot", is the case Block reads the other way, and the entry gives no evidence that the driver's perception was not experienced and forgotten. It concerns the quality experienced, not emotion or affect, and it does not say what awareness is. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-880](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-880.md) v2 | The specific phenomenal character of an experience is fixed by its place in a quality space, the structure of all the discriminations a sensory system can make, and that structure is mirrored many-to-one in neural feature maps; whether the state is conscious at all is left to a separate general mechanism; so experiences are holistic, a change anywhere in the space can change every experience in it, and spectrum inversion is excluded actually by the asymmetry of colour space and nomologically by its ties to the other senses | Lyre (2022), [LIT-1344](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1344.md), read in full in [NOTE-1060](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1060.md): neurophenomenal structuralism as a programme. The thesis is assumed and motivated, not shown. Its neural evidence is one cited imaging study of colour in V4. The reduction it draws rests on metaphysically necessary supervenience, which the author says he cannot argue for. It is filed so that the objections read with it, Negro ([THEORY-868](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-868.md)) and Aldé ([THEORY-867](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-867.md)), have a stated target. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-881](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-881.md) | Across humans, macaques, marmosets and mice, loss of behavioural responsiveness under anaesthesia goes with lower whole-brain pairwise integrated information ΦR in resting fMRI, and its return goes with ΦR's return, including when central thalamic stimulation restores responsiveness during continued anaesthesia; ΦR tracks the macaque arousal score better than the original Φ, causal density, net information flow or functional connectivity | Luppi et al. (2026), [LIT-1357](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1357.md), read in full in [NOTE-1064](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1064.md) from the open-access version of record. It extends the same group's 2024 result ([LIT-949](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-949.md), [THEORY-240](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-240.md)) from human propofol and disorders of consciousness to four species and six regimes, and adds a causal reversal in two macaques. The sharp edge: the state measured is responsiveness, which the authors call "presumably consciousness" and grant is "an imperfect marker of unconsciousness"; the measure is pairwise, linear-Gaussian and content-free; and one mouse regimen fails the main analysis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-882](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-882.md) | Consciousness in an inferring system requires three things: a unified generative model of its world; entry to that model by a precision-weighted competition that coherent inferences win; and epistemic depth, the recursive sharing of the model back through the hierarchy, carried by a hyper-model that predicts and sets precision at every level; awareness then varies with epistemic depth, not with the richness of contents, and a first-person perspective, a self-model and agency are not required | Laukkonen, Friston & Chandaria (2025), [LIT-1363](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1363.md), read in full in [NOTE-1063](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1063.md) from PsyArXiv v3. A conceptual proposal with no data and no simulation. The three conditions are asserted necessary; their joint sufficiency is argued for AI and then withdrawn for phenomenal experience in a footnote. The formal part (Table 1) is a hierarchy with layer-wise precision hyper-parameters, from which none of the properties the text gives epistemic depth is derived. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-883](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-883.md) | Under active inference, the contents of consciousness are posterior beliefs about the hidden states of world, body or brain, and a posterior is conscious when it has the capacity to inform discrete, counterfactual policy selection, at a timescale slow enough to abstract from sensory flux and with enough precision to tell alternatives apart; on this account no conscious content changes without a change in the posterior, and a stimulus given precision by an attention or saccade policy should reach awareness sooner than a retinally matched one | Whyte, Corcoran, Robinson, Smith, Moran, Parr, Friston, Seth & Hohwy (2026), [LIT-1364](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1364.md), read in full in [NOTE-1062](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1062.md) from arXiv v2. The "hard core" the paper reads off the active inference models of rivalry, access, no-report, interoception and meta-awareness. The first two parts follow from the framework; the criterion of access is "an inference to the best explanation" from what the models needed in order to report. The authors scope it to humans and similar animals and are agnostic elsewhere. Neither prediction has been tested in the paper. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-884](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-884.md) | A retained state supports exact answers to a declared family of questions after every finite sequence of a declared family of total deterministic revisions exactly when each of its fibres lies within one class of the coarsest revision-invariant refinement of agreement on current answers; that refinement can be strictly finer than what present answers require, and at most K* − K revision sequences, beyond the current answers, are needed to tell its K* classes apart | Aevyra (2026), The Ledger of Will, [LIT-1376](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1376.md), read in full in [NOTE-1091](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1091.md): Proposition 4, "revision closure", with its proof in §4.4 and finite checks in Appendix A.9. The authors call it "a finite-machine refinement construction in the tradition of Moore and Nerode", not a new theorem. It answers [QUESTION-112](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-112.md) in one case only: a finite family of total deterministic revisions declared in advance. It does not say how to choose the family, which is that question's hard part, and it is not an efficient construction. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-885](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-885.md) | Politics is more prone than markets to increasing returns, and so to path dependence, because it is dense with compulsory institutions and policies, rests on collective action and is opaque, so that institutions, collective action and shared interpretations of politics all feed back on themselves; and once on a path political actors leave it less readily than market actors, because competition and learning correct weakly, elected officials discount the future at the electoral cycle, and institutions are built to be hard to change | Pierson (1997 working paper; published 2000), [LIT-1372](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1372.md), read in full in [NOTE-1076](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1076.md) through its precursor only, the EUI Jean Monnet Chair Paper 44. An argument with no data and one illustration (two failed US health-care reforms, 1993–96). It extends North's claim for institutions in general ([THEORY-429](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-429.md)) to a claim about politics as a domain. It does not show that any political outcome was locked in by an early contingent event. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-886](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-886.md) | Event boundaries are perceived where perceptual prediction error rises transiently; at those points working-memory event models are reset and opened to sensory input, so that information from before a boundary becomes harder to retrieve after it | Zacks, Speer, Swallow, Braver & Reynolds (2007), [LIT-1382](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1382.md), read in full in [NOTE-1084](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1084.md) from the PMC author manuscript. Event segmentation theory: a theory and review, with a partial network simulation and mostly correlational evidence. Prediction error is never measured in people, and the one neural prediction checked (anterior cingulate responses at boundaries) failed. It is a theory of a passive observer of others' activity; it does not cover one's own intentions, and does not mention the doorway effect. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-887](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-887.md) | When an attribute is concentrated on well-connected nodes, many nodes can see it in a majority of their neighbours though it is globally rare, and the share that do grows with the correlation between degree and attribute, as the network becomes more disassortative and as its degree distribution becomes heavier-tailed | Lerman, Yan & Wu (2016), [LIT-1390](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1390.md), read in full in [NOTE-1085](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1085.md) from the PLOS ONE version. The "majority illusion": with 5% of nodes active, 60–80% of nodes in a heavy-tailed synthetic network can see an active majority among their neighbours; in disassortative real topologies, 60–70% with 20% active. A binomial model from the joint degree distribution predicts the share. The edge: the attributes are assigned by the authors on every network, real ones included, so this shows what topology permits, and nothing about what people perceive, believe or do. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-888](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-888.md) | Walking through a doorway into a new room, rather than as far within one, lowers recognition of an object being carried, through retrieval interference between the event models of the two rooms that both hold it, not through a longer retention interval, a passing cost of updating, or loss of the encoding context; outside the originating paradigm, with passive movement and no extra load, it has not appeared | From the Radvansky lab's doorway studies, [LIT-1392](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1392.md), [LIT-1384](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1384.md) and [LIT-1385](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1385.md), read in full in [NOTE-1083](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1083.md), [NOTE-1082](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1082.md) and [NOTE-1081](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1081.md), and the independent conceptual replication of McFadyen et al., [LIT-1387](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1387.md), read in [NOTE-1079](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1079.md). The pattern (a cost on the carried object, worse after two new rooms, not helped by returning) replicates within the lab's paradigm; the interference account is reached by eliminating alternatives, and the independent study found no loss of hits, only more false alarms under load. It is about recognizing object labels, not intentions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-889](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-889.md) | Among white Southerners today, those living in counties where a larger share of the 1860 population was enslaved are somewhat less Democratic, less supportive of affirmative action, more racially resentful and colder toward black Americans, by about a tenth of a standard deviation per standard deviation of slave share; the difference is not accounted for by the present black share of the population, and in voting it appeared after Reconstruction rather than before the war, which supports its origin in the incentives that emancipation gave planters to repress black labor and votes, and its local transmission thereafter | Acharya, Blackwell and Sen (2016), [LIT-1388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1388.md), read in full in [NOTE-1089](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1089.md) from the journal PDF on the second author's site, without the online appendix. The association is well supported; the causal reading rests on 1860 controls, a cotton-suitability instrument with an untestable exclusion restriction, and a direct-effect estimate. The transmission mechanism has the weakest evidence: a parent–child correlation in 241 Southern respondents not linked to county slavery. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-890](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-890.md) | Culture shapes action less by setting its ends than by supplying a repertoire of skills, habits and styles from which people build strategies of action, so strategies outlast the ends they serve; in settled periods culture constrains through the cost of retooling, while in unsettled periods explicit ideologies govern action directly but structural opportunities decide which of the competing ideologies survive | Swidler (1986), [LIT-1367](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1367.md), read in full in [NOTE-1075](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1075.md) from a course copy of the published article. A theoretical argument against the Parsonian values model, built on illustrations (the culture-of-poverty debate, the Protestant ethic, Walzer's Calvin) and on the paper's Figure 1. It reports no data, and its research questions, which would test it, are left open. It does not say that values are inert: within an established strategy they "fine-tune the regulation of action". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-891](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-891.md) | In dyads of untrained dancers facing each other, shared music and visual contact each raise interpersonal movement synchrony, independently and in different movement components: lateral and hand movements synchronize through seeing the partner, anteroposterior movements such as head bobs through the shared music, and vertical bounce through both; which factor drives a component's synchrony can be read from its spatial direction and not from the timing of the synchrony | Bigand, Bianco, Abalde & Novembre (2024), [LIT-1424](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1424.md), read in full in [NOTE-1093](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1093.md) from PubMed Central. A 2 × 2 within-dyad experiment, 35 dyads, that removes the shared external drive and the coupling channel independently and finds synchrony from each in different components, no interaction, and a timing signature that cannot tell them apart. It answers [QUESTION-063](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-063.md) in part: separate interventions on drive and channel do discriminate, and a timing-only measure does not. Direction of coupling, and a perturbation of one member, are not in it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-892](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-892.md) v2 | Psychopathy as the PCL-R measures it is one dimensional construct rather than a type: its items form four correlated factors, interpersonal, affective, lifestyle and antisocial, explained by one superordinate factor, and its affective features are tied psychometrically, genetically and longitudinally to its antisocial ones, so that no one component is its essence | Hare and Neumann (2008), read in [NOTE-1094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1094.md). The PCL-R's twenty items load on four correlated factors, which pair into Factor 1 (interpersonal, affective) and Factor 2 (lifestyle, antisocial) and are explained by one superordinate factor. The affective features are tied to the antisocial ones, so the authors deny that any component is the disorder's core, and they read the evidence as dimensional. Filed for the record's question on corporate psychopathy, which asks which of these features could be said of a corporation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-893](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-893.md) v3 | Reward has separable components: 'liking', its hedonic impact, measurable without report by orofacial taste reactivity in humans, apes, monkeys and rodents, and 'wanting', its incentive salience; brain stimulation and sensitization can raise 'wanting' without raising 'liking', so motivation can grow while pleasure stays flat or falls, and 'liking' reactions can occur without any subjective feeling of pleasure | Berridge and Kringelbach (2015), read in [NOTE-1110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1110.md). Reward splits into 'liking', 'wanting' and learning. 'Liking' has objective, cross-species orofacial markers. Lateral-hypothalamic stimulation and incentive sensitization raise 'wanting', which can grow "even if the drug became less pleasant". Objective 'liking' reactions can occur "without any subjective pleasure feeling at all". Filed because it bears directly on the record's reading of valence as ordering-potential ([CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-895](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-895.md) v2 | Incentive sensitization: repeated drug exposure can make the mesolimbic 'wanting' system lastingly hyper-reactive to drug cues and contexts, so that cue-triggered incentive salience grows, persists for years and even increases during abstinence, while 'liking' need not rise and may fall; sensitized 'wanting' can oppose the person's cognitive desire, and incentive salience can run without any reportable change in feeling | Berridge and Robinson (2016), [LIT-1461](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1461.md), read in [NOTE-1109](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1109.md) from the PMC author manuscript. A review by the theory's authors. Strong in rats and moderate in people for drugs; weak for behavioural addictions, where the authors call the evidence emerging and the mechanism unknown. Filed separately from [THEORY-893](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-893.md), which holds the liking–wanting dissociation, because what [QUESTION-267](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-267.md) and [CLAIM-433](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-433.md) need is the sensitization result: a ranking whose strength is re-keyed to cues, cut loose from both pleasure and the person's goals, and lasting. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-896](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-896.md) | A finite game in strategic form has the finite improvement property, every path of strict unilateral improvements being finite, exactly when it has a generalized ordinal potential, a real function on strategy profiles that rises with every strict unilateral improvement; so in a finite game an ordering along which every improving move climbs exists exactly when there is no improvement cycle, and every sequence of improving moves ends at a pure equilibrium | Monderer and Shapley (1996), [LIT-1462](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1462.md), unread: reported by Duersch, Oechssler and Schipper (arXiv 1003.4274) as Lemma 2.5. A finite game has the finite improvement property iff it has a generalized ordinal potential. The record proves the finite case here: a potential that rises with every improvement forbids cycles, and an acyclic improvement graph on finitely many profiles has an integer potential, the length of the longest improvement path into each profile. It is the precise form of "an ordering prevails" ⇔ "no improvement cycles", and it is ordinal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-898](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-898.md) | In Gangneung, South Korea, in 2022, people outwardly ignored routine retaliatory missile launches and beach-front military sites, while a missile malfunction at night under a news embargo was followed by tweets voicing fear of war with North Korea and blaming the government and military | Ku & Finch (2024), [LIT-1478](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1478.md), read in full from the CC BY version of record in [NOTE-1133](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1133.md). Chance observation of one afternoon and a keyword-filtered tweet sample of one night, offered as an illustration of "ontological agency", not a test. The authors read the inaction as coping that lets securitisation reproduce itself, not as resistance to it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-899](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-899.md) | In an infinite, well-mixed population whose members each sample the quality of their own type, imitation of success has the expected update of a single Cross Learning bandit agent (the Taylor replicator dynamic), and the weighted voter model, in which members broadcast their type in proportion to their sample and adopt the first type they perceive, has the expected update of Maynard-Cross Learning, π_a ← π_a + (r_k / v^π)(1[a = k] − π_a), the Maynard-Smith replicator dynamic; the population vector is the policy and no member learns | Soma et al.'s Propositions 1 and 2, read in full from arXiv v6 in [NOTE-1132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1132.md), with both proofs and the aggregation in Eqs. 8–14 re-derived. An exact identity of expected updates under idealizing assumptions: infinite N, large well-mixed neighbourhoods, and imitation decoupled from evaluation. Each member is one parallel action sample, α = 1/N plays the learning rate, and the macro-policy is a stateless bandit policy over the members' types. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-902](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-902.md) | In 30 four-person student groups discussing 15 choice dilemmas, a member's self-reported closure to influence on the next issue rose with their influence over prior outcomes, increasingly so along the sequence, and the groups' influence networks thinned and their discussions shortened while the rate of consensus did not change: evidence for a reflected-appraisal step by which influence concentrates in deliberating groups | Friedkin, Jia & Bullo (2016), [LIT-1482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1482.md), read in full from the CC BY version of record and its supplement in [NOTE-1126](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1126.md). Friedkin–Johnsen dynamics on each issue, not DeGroot. Closure and centrality both come from members' post-discussion chip allocations, and prior closure is not controlled. Supports the individual step and some structural trends; the predicted end state, one closed member and consensus on that member's view, was not reached. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-905](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-905.md) | In simulations of the two imitation protocols, populations small enough to be finite often settle on a suboptimal option because pure imitation can remove a type entirely, and once settled the protocols give no way to re-explore when the environment changes; variants in which members compare quality estimates converge faster than blind weighted voting, at the cost of more communication and comparison | Soma et al.'s simulations and limits section, read in [NOTE-1132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1132.md). With ten options and arbitrary parameters that the authors call qualitative, swarms of about 500 track the replicator dynamic and smaller ones often lock onto worse options. The authors state that pure imitation can delete a type and has no mechanism for escape in non-stationary environments. Hybrids that compare qualities are faster. Simulation-scoped, not a theorem. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-906](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-906.md) | In five formerly stable democracies selected because they later autocratized (South Korea, India, Hungary, Venezuela and Turkey), formal emergency powers, extraordinary powers functionally equivalent to them, and emergency rhetoric each contributed, on the authors' unsourced country accounts, to weakening democratic institutions | Dagan & Benvenisty (2026), Israel Democracy Institute, [LIT-1487](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1487.md), a web summary read in full in [NOTE-1129](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1129.md). Not peer-reviewed, no sources or method given, cases chosen on the outcome. Good for the three channels and the Hungarian description; not for a causal link, which the authors themselves call "not inevitable". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-911](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-911.md) | Of 853 national states of emergency declared from 1949 to 2017, 115 were reported as unlawful in declaration, conduct or duration; 97 of those followed political turmoil and 14 natural disasters, democracies were less likely than autocracies to run one, and unlawful emergencies lasted 321 days on average against 115 | Bjørnskov, Voigt & Khesali (2022; working paper 2021), [LIT-1473](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1473.md), read in full from the ILE working paper of August 2021 in [NOTE-1125](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1125.md). Unlawfulness is coded from news and NGO reports and from durations past the constitutional maximum, and the authors call the cases "suspected to be unlawful". Descriptive counts and weak logits; nothing here shows that emergency measures outlive the emergency. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-914](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-914.md) v2 | In fear conditioning, extinction does not erase the original threat association but adds a competing inhibitory one, which is why extinguished fear can return with time, a change of context, an unsignalled aversive event or renewed pairing | Craske, Treanor, Conway, Zbozinek & Vervliet (2014), [LIT-1500](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1500.md), read in full from the PMC author manuscript in [NOTE-1137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1137.md). The paper summarizes Bouton's model and the four return-of-fear phenomena that support it, and translates them into exposure practice. The evidence is cited, not reported: the source is a clinical translation, and a promotion needs the primary literature. It does not show that exposure therapy in patients works by inhibitory learning alone. The authors allow that habituation also plays a part. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-916](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-916.md) | In the DeGroot–Friedkin model, where a group reaches DeGroot consensus on each issue and each member's self-weight on the next issue equals their control over the last, with fixed relative interpersonal weights, self-weights converge from every non-autocratic start to one equilibrium ordered by the eigenvector centralities of those weights: power accumulates above a centrality threshold, is autocratic exactly when the network is a star and democratic exactly when it is doubly stochastic, and members whom no path of influence reaches end with none | Jia, MirTabatabaei, Friedkin & Bullo (2015), [LIT-1146](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1146.md), read in [NOTE-1135](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1135.md) from the version of record posted on the author's site; proofs skimmed. Theorems about a model, not findings about groups. The empirical companion, [LIT-1482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1482.md) ([THEORY-902](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-902.md)), uses anchored dynamics and a changing network, whose attractor is autocracy rather than this interior equilibrium. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-919](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-919.md) | Departments of the French Empire more shielded from British trade by the Napoleonic blockade added more mechanized cotton-spinning capacity during it and kept a larger industry through 1887, with more productive spinning firms in 1840 and higher industrial value added per capita in 1860 but not detectably from 1896 | Juhász (2018), [LIT-1489](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1489.md), read in full from the December 2015 draft in [NOTE-1122](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1122.md). A difference-in-differences on 88 departments, then the trade-cost shock as an instrument for 1812 spinning capacity. The long-run first stages are weak (Kleibergen-Paap F 3–8). The protection was a war blockade, followed by post-war tariffs, so this is persistence of a protected industry's location, not evidence about how protection ends. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-921](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-921.md) | How far fear falls during an extinction or exposure session, or across sessions, does not predict how much fear is expressed at follow-up, in animals, human laboratory samples and fearful human samples | Craske et al. (2014), [LIT-1500](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1500.md), read in full from the PMC author manuscript in [NOTE-1137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1137.md), citing six studies. The authors read it as "divergence in response systems": fear expressed during exposure and the learning that exposure produces need not change together. That is the basis of their case against habituation-based exposure. The paper reports no data, and the cited studies are mostly analog samples. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-924](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-924.md) | Elo ratings are the row means of a win-probability matrix's log-odds; they reproduce the matrix exactly when the log-odds have no cyclic component, and adding a copy of one agent shifts the ratings of the others | Balduzzi et al. (2018), [LIT-1508](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1508.md), Propositions 1 and 3 and appendix A, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1155](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1155.md), proofs followed. Elo is the uniform average of log-odds, and a fixed point matches only row sums. It is exact iff log-odds sum to zero around every triangle, so it has no predictive power in rock-paper-scissors, and duplicating an agent moves the ratings of agents that beat or lose to it. Cardinal throughout. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-925](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-925.md) | In a cooperative stochastic game with decentralised actors and a centralised critic, a baseline for each agent that averages the critic's value over that agent's own alternative actions under its own policy, the other agents' actions held fixed, leaves the expected policy gradient unchanged, so each agent can be credited with the advantage of its actual action over that counterfactual average without a default action or an extra simulation; the counterfactual values come from the learned critic, not from the environment | Foerster et al.'s counterfactual baseline (COMA, Eq. 4 and Appendix A of arXiv v3), read in full in [NOTE-1152](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1152.md), with the zero-expectation step re-derived. A proved property of the estimator, not of performance. Its counterfactual is "had the agent acted as it usually does", not "had it not acted", and its values are a learned critic's, trained on occasions when each alternative was taken; it presupposes those occasions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-926](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-926.md) | In a game where each player can transmit n bits before a win or a loss becomes unattainable, every antisymmetric pattern of wins and losses among ⌊2ⁿ⌋ strategies, a cycle through all of them included, is realized by some set of pure strategies | Czarnecki et al. (2020), [LIT-1504](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1504.md), Theorem 1 and Propositions 1–2, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1146.md), proof followed. Strategies announce an identity, then throw or take the game as the pattern says. Go is at least about 1000-bit communicative (log₂ 180! ≈ 1094), so it has cycles of length 2¹⁰⁰⁰. Ordinal: only the sign of outcomes matters. The paper states it for patterns with draws too, which also needs a draw to stay attainable. The strategies are weak by construction. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-927](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-927.md) | In a sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layer trained without balancing losses, the gate came to give large weights to the same few experts, which the authors attribute to self-reinforcement, favoured experts being trained more and so selected more; in one 256-expert language model, the squared coefficient of variation of expert importance or load as an auxiliary loss reduced the peak-to-mean load from 17.8 to at most 1.47 and test perplexity from 39.8 to 35.6–35.7 | Shazeer et al. (2017), section 4 and Appendix A, read in full in [NOTE-1145](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1145.md) from arXiv v1. The imbalance is reported in one paragraph, with Table 6's no-loss row as its evidence: one architecture, ten epochs, no variance. The mechanism is the authors' explanation, not a tested result. The fix penalizes unequal use regardless of competence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-928](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-928.md) | Two softmax reinforcement learners whose reward memories decay at rate α follow coupled replicator equations plus a term α Σ x_j log(x_j / x_i) toward uniform play; without decay the dynamics are conservative, Hamiltonian in zero-sum games, and with decay they are dissipative | Sato & Crutchfield (arXiv 2002; PRE 2003), [LIT-1520](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1520.md), read in full from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1144](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1144.md), Eqs. 1–13. The entropy-like term is what memory decay becomes under softmax choice; re-derived in the reading. The model updates every action's memory at the same rate, so it is the full-information case, not Q-learning as usually run. | Proposed |
