| [THEORY-929](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-929.md) | A joint action-value that is a non-decreasing function of per-agent values, each conditioning only on its agent's own history, makes the profile of the agents' individually greedy actions a greedy joint action, which suffices for decentralised greedy execution and is strictly more expressive than a sum; it cannot represent a joint value in which an agent's best action depends on what the others do at the same step | Rashid et al.'s QMIX (ICML 2018), read in full in [NOTE-1154](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1154.md), with QTRAN ([NOTE-1141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1141.md)) for the strictness. Monotonicity is sufficient for the greedy-profile property and not necessary. It presupposes a real- valued joint value: what it adds is that each member's ranking of its own actions agrees with the collective's whatever the others do, an ordinal separability condition. It is Wolpert and Tumer's factoredness stated for values. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-930](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-930.md) | In empirical games built from about a thousand sampled search agents in eight small board games, and in the AlphaStar league, Nash cluster size peaks at intermediate transitive strength and narrows toward the strongest and the weakest strategies, while Blotto, the disc game, Kuhn poker and noisy Elo games do not show that profile | Czarnecki et al. (2020), [LIT-1504](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1504.md), section 6 and supplements E–I, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1146.md). Agents were MinMax at depths 0–9, loss-seeking MaxMin and MCTS, with 50 seeds each, about 1000 distinct per game after duplicates were removed. Games: Hex, Go and Quoridor on small boards, Tic-Tac-Toe, its misère form and Connect Four. AlphaStar's league shows its training system's geometry, the authors say. A qualitative profile with a fitted skew-normal curve and no test. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-931](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-931.md) | A learner that ascends its own return after one anticipated naive gradient step of its opponent, differentiating through that step, reached tit-for-tat-like reciprocity in 81% of fifty exact-gradient runs of the memory-one iterated prisoner's dilemma, where pairs of naive gradient learners ended at the mutual-defection return, and settled at the mixed equilibrium of iterated matching pennies where naive learners did not converge; shown for two players, one-step shaping and access to the opponent's parameters | Foerster et al.'s LOLA (AAMAS 2018), read in full in [NOTE-1150](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1150.md) from arXiv v4, with the update rule re-derived. Empirical, in two small games and a grid game. Shaping here is mutual and produced cooperation, not capture; in matching pennies, a harmonic game, it damped the cycling of naive learners. Table 3's naive-learner tit-for-tat figure (20.8%) does not square with their return (−1.98), and the NOTE says so. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-932](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-932.md) | The replicator-plus-entropy model of Boltzmann Q-learning in two-player stateless games is exact for frequency-adjusted Q-learning, not for Q-learning, whose expected update carries an extra factor of each action's selection probability and whose trajectories in 2×2 games depart from the model depending on initialization | Kaisers & Tuyls (AAMAS 2010), [LIT-1511](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1511.md), read in full in [NOTE-1140](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1140.md), correcting the model of Tuyls, Verbeeck & Lenaerts (2003), [LIT-1501](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1501.md), which is not read. The derivation of the discrepancy is short and was checked in the reading; the experiments are three games, one temperature, compared by eye. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-933](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-933.md) | Individual-Global-Max, that the agents' individually greedy actions form a greedy joint action, is strictly weaker than additive or monotonic factorisation: every single-state matrix game with a unique optimum satisfies it, yet in 177 of 310 random three-by-three two-agent games value-decomposition and monotonic mixing failed to learn the optimal joint action that an IGM-only method found; a sufficient condition is that the sum of individual values, shifted by a state value, equals the joint value at the greedy profile and bounds it from above elsewhere | Son et al.'s QTRAN (ICML 2019), read in full in [NOTE-1141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1141.md), with Theorem 1 and the single-state observation re-derived. IGM presupposes a real-valued joint value and constrains only the optimum: members may rank everything below it differently from the collective. With full observability it is nearly empty; its content is whether members acting on local histories can each pick their part of the optimum. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-934](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-934.md) | Under Bush–Mosteller learning with negative payoffs, the continuous-time limit is a replicator term in benefits plus a probability-matching term, which alone drives choice probabilities to success probabilities | Börgers & Sarin (JET 1997; working paper 1993), [LIT-1505](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1505.md), read in full in [NOTE-1149](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1149.md). When reinforcements may be negative, probability removed from a punished strategy is redistributed, and the limit is dp_j/dt = p_j(Ū_j* − p\|Ũ\|q) + Ū_j*(σ_j* − p_j). With payoffs of equal absolute size only the matching term remains. The limit is stated with its proof omitted. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-935](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-935.md) | In two two-player Markov games whose learned cooperative and defecting policies, played against each other, both give Prisoner's Dilemma payoffs, independent deep Q-learners responded oppositely to capacity: more hidden units raised aggression in a fruit-gathering game, where tagging a rival is the harder policy to implement, and lowered lone hunting in a wolfpack game, where coordination is; in the gathering game, aggression was learned where apples were scarce or a tagged rival stayed out long | Leibo, Zambaldi, Lanctot, Marecki and Graepel (2017), read in full in [NOTE-1151](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1151.md) from arXiv v1. A descriptive simulation with no seeds or spread reported, policies classed by training environment, two agents, fixed conditions, apples on a fixed respawn timer, and a mismatch between the text's and Figure 7's settings for batch and network size. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-936](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-936.md) | In two-agent rock–scissors–paper played by softmax reinforcement learners, nonzero tie rewards give quasiperiodic tori and Hamiltonian chaos without memory decay, and limit cycles and chaotic attractors with it, over a large share of the tie-reward range simulated | Sato & Crutchfield (arXiv 2002; PRE 2003), [LIT-1520](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1520.md), read in full in [NOTE-1144](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1144.md), pp. 2–3 and Figs. 1–3. Numerical results for one game, two agents and the parameters shown; the zero-decay, zero-sum case was first reported in Sato, Akiyama and Farmer (PNAS 2002), which is not held. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-937](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-937.md) | When a mixture of experts is trained on the error of a single expert chosen stochastically by the gate, or on the negative log-likelihood of the mixture, an expert that fits a case better than the gate-weighted average gains responsibility for it; on a four-class vowel task, mixtures of 4 or 8 linear experts learned in about half the epochs of backpropagation networks of equal size, at equal accuracy, and divided the task by class pair, leaving all but 2 or 3 experts with mixing proportions effectively zero | Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan and Hinton (1991), read in full in [NOTE-1147](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1147.md) from a scan of the published article. The gradients of Eqs. 1.4 and 1.5 were re-derived when filed. The task is small (two formants, 75 speakers, 25 runs per system) and has two natural subtasks; the idle experts are read by the authors as economy, and their recovery is not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-938](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-938.md) | Cross learning has the expected motion of the replicator dynamic and follows it on any finite horizon in the continuous-time limit, but for every learning speed the discrete process converges with probability one to a pure strategy profile, even in games where the replicator dynamic cycles | Börgers & Sarin (JET 1997; working paper 1993), [LIT-1505](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1505.md), read in full from the 1995 working paper in [NOTE-1149](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1149.md). Two players running Cross's rule with payoffs in (0, 1): expected change equals the discrete replicator step (Proposition 3); the slow-learning limit is the Taylor replicator dynamic at each finite time (Proposition 4); for every step size the process is absorbed in a pure profile with probability one (Proposition 5). The equivalence is pointwise in time, not uniform. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-939](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-939.md) | In a multi-agent system run against a world utility, a private utility is factored, ranking each agent's own alternatives with the others fixed as the world utility ranks them, exactly when it is an increasing function of the world utility given the components the agent cannot affect; the world utility minus its value with the agent's effect set clamped is factored, and in a sixty-agent bar problem clamping to the average action learned better than clamping to absence or using the world utility itself | Wolpert & Tumer's NASA report ([LIT-1506](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1506.md)), read in full in NOTE-1153 because their Advances in Complex Systems paper ([LIT-1515](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1515.md)) could not be reached. The characterisation is stated with its proof deferred; the "if" half and the WLU's factoredness were checked when filed. Factoredness is ordinal, member by member, and needs no scale shared among members. The WLU is not a causal counterfactual: it re- scores the actual history with one member's part replaced. Removal was not the best clamp. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-940](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-940.md) | In a finite symmetric zero-sum game, successive Nash clusters are weakly ordered by relative population performance, and a strategy that beats every member of a population containing a whole cluster lies in a strictly earlier cluster | Czarnecki et al. (2020), [LIT-1504](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1504.md), Definition 3 and Theorems 2–3, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1146.md), proofs followed and re-derived. RPP is the population value of Balduzzi et al. (2019), [LIT-1509](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1509.md). It holds for any Nash clustering of any finite symmetric zero-sum game and does not depend on the spinning-top hypothesis. The order is weak, since clusters can tie, and cardinal, since RPP uses payoff magnitudes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-941](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-941.md) | If every player of a finite game switches from its last action to each other action with probability proportional to its positive conditional regret, the empirical distribution of play converges almost surely to the set of correlated equilibria | Hart & Mas-Colell (Econometrica 2000; handout 1996), [LIT-1521](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1521.md), read in full in [NOTE-1142](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1142.md). Convergence is of time-averaged joint frequencies to a set, not of play to an equilibrium; the common history is the correlating device; inertia is needed; and interior correlated equilibria that are not pure Nash cannot be the limit. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-942](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-942.md) | The α-Rank chain over pure strategy profiles, built from Fermi-imitation fixation probabilities in finite populations with rare mutation, has a unique stationary distribution at every finite ranking intensity; as the intensity grows without bound its transitions become those of Markov chains confined to the sink strongly connected components of the game's weakly-better-response graph, each of which lies inside a single chain component of the replicator flow | Omidshafiei et al. (2019), [LIT-1516](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1516.md), Theorems 2.1.2, 2.4.24 and 2.5.1, read from arXiv v4 in [NOTE-1156](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1156.md), proofs followed. Irreducibility is immediate, and the α → ∞ limit is of transition matrices. The link to the replicator flow rests on a volume-preservation step that is asserted, not carried out. Not shown: what the stationary distribution tends to, how it splits among several sinks, or invariance to duplicated strategies, which the reader found it lacks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-943](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-943.md) | When a center with no ground truth pays each rater a strictly proper scoring rule on the distribution of a reference rater's report implied by her own report, under a common prior and a known signal model in which raters' signals are stochastically relevant to one another, truthful reporting is a strict Nash equilibrium, but not the only one: equilibria in which every rater reports the same signal regardless of what she observed also exist | Miller, Resnick and Zeckhauser's Proposition 1, read in full in [NOTE-1139](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1139.md) from the January 2005 draft, with the proof and the worked example (p(H) = .5, f(h \| H) = .85, f(h \| L) = .45; honest l scores −0.69, false h −0.75 under the log rule) re-derived. The same example has two uninformative equilibria, which the authors set aside as not focal. The scheme replaces ground truth with the center's model of how honest signals correlate. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-944](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-944.md) | The value of the zero-sum game between two populations' evaluation matrices does not depend on which Nash equilibrium is used, is unchanged by adding agents that behave as mixtures of existing members, and is not positive for a population whose agents are all behavioural mixtures of the other's | Balduzzi et al. (2019), [LIT-1509](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1509.md), Propositions 2 and 5, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1143](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1143.md), proofs followed and re-derived. Relative population performance is a game value, so equilibrium selection never arises. Behaviourally redundant members leave it unchanged, and a population contained in another's behavioural hull cannot beat it. It scores populations, not members, it is cardinal, and populations not nested by hull can still beat one another in a cycle. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-945](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-945.md) | When each agent's Q-function is approximated as an average of pairwise terms and expanded about the mean action of its neighbours, the first-order term vanishes and the approximation error is a second-order remainder bounded by the curvature of the pairwise Q-function, leaving a two-body problem between an agent and its neighbours' average; with homogeneous agents, mean field Q-learning converges to the Nash Q-value under assumptions the authors call strong, and learned tasks of 500 and 1000 agents where independent and centralized-critic baselines failed | Yang et al. (2018), read in full in [NOTE-1148](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1148.md) from arXiv v5. The expansion and the remainder bound were re-derived when filed; the appendix states an equality where only an inequality holds, which leaves the bound intact. The cancellation of remainders is argued from homogeneity, not proved, and the contraction step needs a high temperature while the convergence theorem assumes a greedy limit. The approximation requires agents interchangeable within a neighbourhood. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-946](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-946.md) | In the zero-sum meta-game on an antisymmetric evaluation matrix the maximum-entropy Nash equilibrium is unique; when the meta-game has only one Nash equilibrium, adding exact copies of an agent splits that agent's mass evenly and leaves every Nash average unchanged; the equilibrium is uniform exactly when every agent's mean log-odds is zero, and uniform on the top-rated agents when the matrix is a pure gradient | Balduzzi et al. (2018), [LIT-1508](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1508.md), Proposition 4, Lemma 1 and Theorem 1, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1155](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1155.md), proofs followed. The paper claims invariance to redundant copies without the uniqueness condition. Its proof covers the Nash set, not the maximum-entropy selection. A counterexample checked by script (one copy of a null agent moves an outside agent's Nash average from −0.5 to −0.2) shows the condition is needed. Cardinal: payoffs are log-odds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-947](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-947.md) | For Blackwell approachability of an approachable polytope under partial monitoring with a known signal law, there are efficient algorithms whose average vector payoff reaches the target at expected distance O(T^-1/3) for general signals and O(T^-1/2) when the signal law does not depend on the decision, the worst-case optimal rates for those two classes | Kwon and Perchet (2017), [LIT-1526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1526.md), read in [NOTE-1159](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1159.md). The rates are for the average payoff's distance to the target, uniformly over Nature's choices, with approachability assumed (Perchet's condition). Optimal means not improvable in the worst case over games. It gives no guarantee for individual stages or rolling windows, and none when the signal law is unknown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-949](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-949.md) | When several LoRAs take turns over one denoising trajectory, each given the same share of steps, the result depends on the schedule and not only on the shares: switching at every step scored worst (a composition win rate against weight merging near 38%, against about 59% when each LoRA kept five consecutive steps), shortening the turns late in sampling scored worse than keeping them fixed, and which LoRA acted first mattered more than the order of the rest, the character first scoring best and the style first slightly below a random order | Zhong et al. (2024), [LIT-1529](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1529.md), read in [NOTE-1160](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1160.md). An ablation of LoRA Switch judged by GPT-4V against weight merging. It says that equal shares of steps do not fix the outcome; it does not say how large the order effect is beyond noise, or how much each LoRA contributes to the image, which was not measured. The authors' explanation, that core elements should come first, is theirs and untested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-950](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-950.md) | For a finite partial-monitoring game in which every two actions whose cells meet can estimate their loss difference from their own two signals, RelExp3's expected regret satisfies lim sup E[R_n]/√n ≤ 8√(2K_loc(1+F)(2+F) log K), with K_loc the most actions whose cells share a point and F the number of feedback symbols, and no other game-dependent constant; a two-action game shows that a factor linear in F cannot be avoided in general | Lattimore and Szepesvári (2019), [LIT-1524](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1524.md), read in [NOTE-1162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1162.md). For the class of games Bartók (2013) studied, the leading constant of the √n regret depends only on K_loc, F and log K, asymptotically. It is the first such result against adversaries. The constant reached before the asymptotics set in still depends on large game constants. It is a bound for one algorithm in a sub-class of the easy games, not a characterisation of the constant. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-953](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-953.md) | On Isaac's structuralist account, the strongest evidence that a quality-space model targets phenomenal experience, and not only behaviour or neural activity, is convergence between models of the same space derived through different behavioural procedures, since experience is what those procedures share; the convergence observed is coarse, with discrepancies that often exceed each method's own uncertainty, and the models average over subjects, so what they converge on is a standard observer | Isaac (2025), [LIT-1361](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1361.md), read in [NOTE-1163](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1163.md): why a third-personal science of quality spaces counts as a science of experience. Relations between experiences, unlike bare qualities, show up in behaviour, so they can be compared across subjects; and models from different behavioural routes that converge are taken to target what the routes share. The argument does not exclude a shared stimulus geometry or a shared decision process as the common factor, the convergence is partial by the paper's own account, and averaging over subjects makes the target an ideal observer, which the paper leaves as an open puzzle. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-959](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-959.md) | Perceptual constancies are invariants of transformations that act within experience, not only of physical transformations or planar projections, since perceived shape and depth match no linear projection and the transformations can be realized with no physical change; on Isaac's structuralist account, after Cassirer, it is these invariants, co-present in experience with the varying appearances they abstract from, that make experience represent an objective world and so distinguish subject from object | Isaac (2025), [LIT-1361](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1361.md), read in [NOTE-1163](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1163.md): the group-theoretic layer of a structuralist account of experience. The paper's evidence supports the weaker half: constancy needs invariance under transformations internal to experience. The stronger half, that this invariance is what makes experience objective and induces a subject–object distinction, is Cassirer's, argued from the co-presence of two levels of experience, and the paper gives no way to tell invariant extraction with a subject from invariant extraction without one. "Group-theoretic" is used loosely: the paper's own examples are groupoids or toy models. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-965](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-965.md) | Sparse-autoencoder features of a large language model's residual stream are units the model computes with: they track abstract concepts across languages, modalities and concrete or abstract instances, and intervening on one changes the model's behaviour in the way its label predicts, better than directions found from a few labelled examples | Templeton et al. (2024), [LIT-1533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1533.md), read in [NOTE-1178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1178.md), with Bricken et al. (2023), [LIT-1545](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1545.md), for the one-layer case. The thesis of both papers: features are the model's own units, shown by steering. The authors' own hedges: steering needs features clamped beyond their observed range; the reconstruction error rides along; "we haven't rigorously evaluated our features against other steering methods". The record holds a result against it for known causal variables ([THEORY-968](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-968.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-967](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-967.md) | In a two-layer attention-only transformer, attention heads change function during training: heads in the first layer that predict simple n-grams early later become the previous-token heads of the induction circuit, a bracket-matching support head, or supporting members of a circuit with second-layer n-gram heads, giving up simple n-grams as they do, and particular n-grams pass from one head to another; so later circuits form partly by repurposing components that already had a role | Wang, Hoogland, van Wingerden, Furman and Murfet (2024), [LIT-1535](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1535.md), read in [NOTE-1188](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1188.md). "Heads 0:1, 0:4, 0:7 ultimately become the two previous-token heads and (layer 0) Dyck head respectively. However, these heads appear to start out as simple n-gram heads." Layer-0 multigram heads lose information about simple n-grams from stage LM3, as path patching and composition scores show them coming to feed layer-1 bracket-matching heads. The "ago" n-gram moves from head 0:0 to head 1:0. Whether the late roles are built from the early ones, or merely follow them in time, is not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-982](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-982.md) | Claude 3.5 Haiku routinely computes intermediate steps within a single forward pass and plans its outputs ahead, representing a target before the text that leads to it and writing towards it, as Lindsey et al. propose from their case studies | Lindsey et al. (2025), [LIT-1541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1541.md), read in [NOTE-1181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1181.md): the introduction ("Claude 3.5 Haiku routinely uses multiple intermediate reasoning steps 'in its head'"; "It displays signs of forward planning") and the discussion's sections on plan formation and working backward from a goal. The case studies show each mechanism on chosen prompts, and the same article has a case without it: on a jailbreak the model "doesn't know what it plans to say until it actually says it". The authors report a satisfying graph for about a quarter of the prompts they try. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-986](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-986.md) v2 | Analogous features and circuits form across neural networks trained on different architectures, data and tasks, so that a feature or circuit found in one model can be expected in others, as Olah, Cammarata, Schubert, Goh, Petrov and Carter propose under the name universality | Olah et al. (2020), [LIT-1543](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1543.md), read in [NOTE-1182](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1182.md): Claim 3, the universality hypothesis. Curve detectors and high-low frequency detectors are reported in AlexNet, InceptionV1, VGG19 and ResNetV2-50, with InceptionV3, a Places365 model and conv nets trained from scratch named in the text. The authors: "the only evidence we can offer today is anecdotal". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-989](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-989.md) | On the abstracts of the Journal of the ACM, the held-out likelihood of infinite-depth hierarchical LDA is higher than that of flat LDA at every fixed topic count in a range bracketing hLDA's own posterior topic count, about 140, though the authors expect flat LDA to win once the topic count is free | Blei, Griffiths and Jordan (2010), [LIT-1542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1542.md), §6.3 and Fig. 9, read in [NOTE-1176](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1176.md). One corpus, five-fold cross-validation, hyperparameters integrated out. It is evidence that a single-path hierarchy can earn its constraint in prediction, near its own size. It is not evidence that a hierarchy predicts better than a flat mixed-membership model in general: the paper itself says the flat model should dominate at large topic counts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-990](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-990.md) v2 | In transformer language models of every size, including large ones with MLPs, induction heads, extended to fuzzy matching of similar tokens and abstract patterns, are the mechanism of most in-context learning, as Olsson et al. propose | Olsson et al. (2022), [LIT-1538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1538.md), read in [NOTE-1173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1173.md). The paper's thesis: circuits with the induction head's mechanism, matching "[A*][B*] … [A] → [B], where A* ≈ A and B* ≈ B are similar in some space", "implement most in-context learning in large models". For large models the authors grade their own evidence correlational (Argument 1), weakly interventional (Argument 2), plausibility (Argument 4) and analogy (Argument 6). Their strongest alternative is that other composition heads, formed in the same window, carry more of it above some size. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-995](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-995.md) | The attention heads in GPT-2 small that take over the indirect-object prediction when its main name mover heads are knocked out exist because the model was trained with dropout, which optimized it to be robust to disabled components, as Wang, Variengien, Conmy, Shlegeris and Steinhardt hypothesize | Wang et al. (2022), [LIT-1540](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1540.md), read in [NOTE-1167](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1167.md), §3.4: "We hypothesize that this compensation phenomenon is caused by the use of dropout during training. Thus, the model was optimized for robustness to dysfunctional parts." The compensation is real (a 5% loss of logit difference after knocking out the three name movers); the cause is not examined. Appendix F: "Both the reason and the mechanism of this compensation effect are still unclear." | Proposed |
| [THEORY-997](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-997.md) | When a pretrained language model is fine-tuned on a task it initially fails, it acquires the task mainly by reconnecting components it already has rather than by recruiting new ones: the circuits found before and after keep most of their nodes and change most of their edges, as Wang, Hu, Du, Cheng, Wang and Zou propose from LoRA fine-tuning of Pythia-1.4B on arithmetic | Wang et al. (2025), [LIT-1539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1539.md), read in [NOTE-1183](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1183.md). Their EAP-IG circuits (top 5% of edges) change edges 2.8–4.3 times as much as nodes over LoRA fine-tuning on five arithmetic tasks. A record simulation shows that a fixed edge budget on a transformer-sized graph gives the same contrast when only edge-level noise is resampled, so the counts do not yet show reorganization. Fine-tuning only, one model for most results, arithmetic only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1000](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1000.md) v2 | For fine-grained nodes of transformer language models generally, attribution patching corrected for attention saturation is a reliable prefilter for activation patching: nodes it ranks low rarely have large single-node patching effects, so verifying nodes in its order finds the important ones at a small multiple of the cost of an oracle, as Kramár et al. expect | Kramár, Lieberum, Shah & Nanda (2024), [LIT-1531](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1531.md), read in [NOTE-1190](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1190.md). The measured case is four Pythia models, three prompt pairs and two small distributions. The paper's own diagnostic is what would let a single new setting be checked without exhaustive patching. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1001.md) | In a transformer whose candidate circuits are sets of shared elementary coordinates, how circuits interact during training is set by what they share: circuits that share a unit cooperate, and circuits that need the same layers for different roles compete, so that which circuit wins is decided by the initialization of units beyond its own, with sharp boundaries between competitors and soft ones between cooperators, as Musat, Pimentel, Zucchet and Hofmann read their three-layer scan | Musat et al. (2026), [LIT-1530](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1530.md), read in [NOTE-1177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1177.md). In projected SGD training of a three-layer single-head attention-only transformer on in-context bigrams, three induction circuits are possible, and the winner depends on initial strengths outside the winner itself. The authors explain the pattern by cooperation through a shared unit and competition for layers. The evidence is one scan over two initial strengths with every other coordinate zeroed, in projected training. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1004.md) | In Pythia-1B, OLMo-1B and BLOOM-1B, the crosscoder features that most affect subject–verb agreement change over pretraining: at early checkpoints they detect particular tokens and subtokens, at later ones grammatical categories; in BLOOM, language-specific features give way to features shared across English, French, Spanish and Portuguese while Hindi and Arabic keep language-specific ones; and which features matter keeps shifting after task accuracy has stopped improving | Bayazit, Mueller and Bosselut (2025, ACL 2026), [LIT-1555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1555.md), read in [NOTE-1186](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1186.md). Crosscoders trained jointly on the middle layer of two or three checkpoints, with features scored by their relative indirect effect on agreement minimal pairs at each. The reconstruction quality (C1) and RelIE's agreement with single-feature ablations (C2) are measured; the trends in this title are read by the authors from annotated features. It describes; it does not predict later checkpoints, and it cannot tell a feature carried forward from one re-learned in the same direction. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1008.md) | Mixed memberships fitted by a fifteen-block MMSB to 871 yeast proteins' curated physical interactions carry information about the proteins' top-level MIPS functions beyond what the functions' base rates give: after mapping blocks to functions on 87 proteins, thresholded memberships predicted the other proteins' annotations with about 87% accuracy, against about 70% for random guessing at the right proportions | Airoldi, Blei, Fienberg and Xing (2008), [LIT-1553](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1553.md), §4.3.2 and Figs. 10–12, read in [NOTE-1179](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1179.md). The batch's one check of inferred mixed memberships against labels the model never saw. The reported margin is over a weak baseline, so it shows less than it seems: probably some information, not yet how much. It says nothing about whether the fifteen blocks are the fifteen functions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1013](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1013.md) v3 | In trained vision networks, units or other directions in a layer's activation space are typically meaningful features, and the weights between understood features implement algorithms that can be read off them, so that features and their circuits are the units in which such a network can be understood, as Olah, Cammarata, Schubert, Goh, Petrov and Carter propose | Olah et al. (2020), [LIT-1543](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1543.md), read in [NOTE-1182](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1182.md): Claims 1 and 2 of the essay. The evidence is a set of examples in InceptionV1 (curve, high-low frequency and dog head detectors; the curve, oriented dog head and car circuits), argued with feature visualization, dataset examples, synthetic stimuli, tuning curves and the weights. The essay names polysemantic neurons as the main obstacle. It gives no count of how much of a layer is understood. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1014](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1014.md) | In a language model, a behaviour that looks like one mechanism, whether picked out by one contrast or by one cluster of next-token predictions, is often carried by several distinct pathways of sparse features that converge on the output without fully intersecting, as in Pythia-70M's agreement across a relative clause, its prediction of "to" before an infinitival object, and its incrementing of sequences | Marks et al. (2025), [LIT-1532](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1532.md), read in [NOTE-1187](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1187.md): §3.3, §5 and Appendix C. Agreement across a relative clause: subject-number features promote verb forms directly, and a second pathway carries the number to the clause's end through PP/RC boundary features. Cluster 475: one mechanism detects verbs and adjectives that take infinitival objects, another nominal objects before an object complement. Cluster 382: general succession features and token-specific induction features. "While the clusters … seem at first to each represent a single mechanism, circuit-level analysis reveals in both cases a union of distinct mechanisms." | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1016](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1016.md) | The features a sparse autoencoder recovers from a language model are a resolution set by the dictionary's width and sparsity penalty, not a unique set of the model's units: as the dictionary widens, features split into families of finer features, and splits also merge, so that the number of features is not well-posed | Bricken et al. (2023), [LIT-1545](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1545.md), read in [NOTE-1191](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1191.md), Feature Splitting and Discussion; and Templeton et al. (2024), [LIT-1533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1533.md), read in [NOTE-1178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1178.md), for the same splitting at 1M, 4M and 34M features in a large model. In a one-layer model one base64 feature becomes three, then more; in Claude 3 Sonnet a San Francisco feature becomes two, then eleven. The authors offer two pictures, an idealized set seen at varying resolution and feature manifolds with no finite description; both deny that one width is the right one. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1021](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1021.md) | In transformer language models, attribution patching agrees well with activation patching for small patches of single heads and their queries, keys, values and attention patterns, for nodes late in a circuit relative to the metric, and for circuits that route information through attention, and agrees badly for large patches such as whole residual streams, for the first MLP layer and the early layers of deep circuits, where nonlinearities move out of saturation, and where an effect needs several features at once, as Nanda proposes | Nanda (2023), [LIT-1581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1581.md), read in [NOTE-1201](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1201.md). The post's map of where the first-order estimate can be trusted. The record holds it from one task in the post, from the mathematics of the estimate ([THEORY-1023](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1023.md)), and in part from Kramár et al.'s test on Pythia ([THEORY-996](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-996.md)), which found misses behind saturated attention, as this predicts, and tested no residual-stream nodes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1022](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1022.md) v2 | The curve units of InceptionV1's mixed3b detect curves as such: curves, not correlated stimuli, cause their firing, they respond to curves in general whatever their colour, fill or texture, and they have no meaningful secondary function, their weak responses to edges and angles being part of the same curve-detecting algorithm, as Cammarata, Goh, Carter, Schubert, Petrov and Olah claim | Cammarata et al. (2020), [LIT-1575](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1575.md), read in [NOTE-1198](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1198.md). The article's four claims (causality, generality, purity, family) taken together, as the authors state them. Generality and the family are measured ([THEORY-1028](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1028.md)). Causality rests on feature visualization and attribution. Purity rests on feature visualization with a diversity term and activation-binned labels, while most of the unit's firings, and 45% of its contribution to expected value, are not shown to be curves. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1026.md) | In transformer language models, locating where a forward pass carries information about a fact and finding where a weight edit best changes the expressed fact are different questions, because an edit at one layer can override information accumulated across other layers, so that many layers could hold a fact and some happen to, as Hase, Bansal, Kim and Ghandeharioun propose | Hase et al. (2023), [LIT-1578](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1578.md), read in [NOTE-1194](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1194.md), §6: "Causal Tracing answers a question about where factual information is carried in representations in a Transformer forward pass, and this question turns out to be a different question than the editing question of where is best to intervene"; and, for why edits work where facts are not traced, "Many layers could store a fact, and it happens that some do". The authors note that this would be surprising, since layers cannot be swapped freely. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1027](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1027.md) | In audits of language models for hidden objectives, sparse-autoencoder features add to what black-box attacks and semantic search over the training data can find, surfacing knowledge the model does not disclose even where the data that taught it is not semantically similar to the context in which it is applied, as Marks, Treutlein et al. suggest | Marks, Treutlein et al. (2025), [LIT-1584](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1584.md), read in [NOTE-1193](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1193.md): §§4–5 and Appendix F. In the blind game the fastest team used SAE features, but semantic search with its query finds the same documents. Post hoc and unblinded, SAE features surface RM-bias knowledge from bias demonstrations and from the Assistant token, where semantic search fails. The model's objective is named in its training data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1030.md) | In transformer language models, each hidden unit of a feed-forward layer acts as a key–value memory, its input weights detecting patterns in the prefix and its output weights promoting the tokens that follow them, and a layer's output composes many such memories while the residual stream refines the prediction from layer to layer, as Geva, Schuster, Berant and Levy propose | Geva et al. (2021), [LIT-1576](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1576.md), read in [NOTE-1200](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1200.md): "feed-forward layers in transformer-based language models operate as key-value memories, where each key correlates with textual patterns in the training examples, and each value induces a distribution over the output vocabulary", and "we thus expect our qualitative empirical observations to hold across diverse settings". Evidence in one model, correlational only. ROME's storage hypothesis ([THEORY-1011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1011.md)) borrows the name and reads keys and values at another level. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1035](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1035.md) | In trained neural networks, polysemantic neurons arise from the loss-optimal allocation of a layer's limited capacity among features: a feature is shared between neurons when its marginal loss reduction from capacity equals that of the features it shares with, so that sparser, higher-kurtosis inputs, which make returns to capacity diminish, produce more polysemanticity, and the block structure of the embedding, which architecture shapes, sets how many features each neuron mixes, as Scherlis, Sachan, Jermyn, Benton and Shlegeris propose | Scherlis et al. (2022), [LIT-1625](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1625.md), read in [NOTE-1205](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1205.md). The paper's account of polysemanticity in general: capacity allocation at the loss optimum, driven by sparsity, with architecture deciding block size. The general first-order condition holds for any loss under two stated assumptions; its application to trained networks, and the role of architecture, rest on toy models only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1039](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1039.md) | In autoregressive transformer language models, factual associations are recalled through middle-layer MLP modules acting as key–value memories, and any fact could be stored equally in any one of the middle MLP layers, as Meng, Bau, Andonian and Belinkov conjecture | Meng et al. (2022), [LIT-1536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1536.md), read in [NOTE-1166](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1166.md), §2.3: "we conjecture that any fact could be equivalently stored in any one of the middle MLP layers". It was one clause of [THEORY-1011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1011.md), which is Rejected for its other part, the claim that the traced middle layers are where a fact is stored. Hase et al. (2023), [LIT-1578](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1578.md), read in [NOTE-1194](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1194.md), measure edits succeeding at nearly every layer of GPT-J whatever tracing says ([THEORY-1024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1024.md)). That is what this conjecture predicts, but it is not evidence of storage, since an edit can work wherever a layer can write the needed output ([LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1040](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1040.md) | The units of the early layers of trained vision networks fall largely into neuron families, sets of variants of one feature across orientation, colour or scale, which reflect structure in the network rather than a convenience of the person sorting them, and the same families form across models, as Olah, Cammarata, Schubert, Goh, Petrov and Carter propose | Olah et al. (2020), [LIT-1624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1624.md), read in [NOTE-1206](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1206.md). The article's organizing hypothesis: early vision's units come in families, some of them real structure (said to be recoverable by factorizing weight matrices), and the families recur across models. The census ([THEORY-1042](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1042.md)) is by eye in one model; neither the factorization nor a second model's sorting is shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1044](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1044.md) | For the infinite hidden Markov model the beam sampler reaches the posterior in fewer iterations than the single-site Gibbs sampler, and is less sensitive to initialization and hyperpriors, particularly when hidden states persist and emissions are uninformative, at a cost per iteration close to the Gibbs sampler's | Van Gael, Saatci, Teh and Ghahramani (2008), [LIT-1622](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1622.md), read in [NOTE-1204](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1204.md). Two synthetic designs (an almost cyclic 4-state HMM, length 800, 20 runs; persistent 4-state HMMs with self-transitions to 0.999, length 4000, 60 starts), a well-log series and a text task. The beam sampler is exact by construction ([THEORY-1037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1037.md)); how much faster it mixes is shown only in iterations and by eye. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1047](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1047.md) | The curve units of InceptionV1's mixed3b implement a simple algorithm that can be read off their weights and written down in a few sentences: families of Gabors, lines and early curves, each a set of rotated copies of one unit, tiled along the curve's tangent, with negative weights against similar shapes of opposing orientation, rotational and scale equivariance reducing the circuit's more than 50,000 parameters about fifty-fold, so that a network written from this description reimplements them and the description accurately reflects the circuit, as Cammarata, Goh, Carter, Voss, Schubert and Olah claim | Cammarata et al. (2021), [LIT-1629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1629.md), read in [NOTE-1207](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1207.md). The article's account of how curve detectors are built, and its claim that the account is the circuit. The family structure and the echo edit are measured ([THEORY-1038](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1038.md)); that the description is complete, and that the reimplementation matches the natural units beyond strong cases, is shown by figures only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md) | On the Black Queen Hypothesis of Morris, Lenski and Zinser, losing a costly function whose product leaks to neighbours is favoured by ordinary individual selection in large free-living microbial populations, and the loss proceeds until the remaining producers just supply the community, so that most cells come to depend on a rare few with no relatedness, cooperation or collective required | Morris, Lenski & Zinser (2012), [LIT-1568](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1568.md), read in [NOTE-1212](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1212.md). A loss-of-function mutant invades when its resource saving B = (Q_A − Q_M)/Q_A exceeds its cost C, which falls as other cells' leaky activity protects it. Because protection falls as producers become rare, the loss is frequency dependent and stops short of community-wide loss. The evidence is Prochlorococcus's loss of katG and its dependence on a peroxide-removing community. The dependence it produces is one-way, from beneficiaries to helpers, and involves no collective. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1049](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1049.md) v2 | On McCutcheon and colleagues' survey, bacterial endosymbionts lose their own cell-envelope and envelope-transport genes together below about 400 kb, and begin to lose translation genes (ribosomal proteins, tRNAs, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases) below about 200 kb, so that the smallest-genome symbionts cannot be self-sufficient and their membranes, transport and protein synthesis are presumably supplied by the host, as for organelles | McCutcheon, Garber, Spencer & Warren (2024), [LIT-1571](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1571.md), read in [NOTE-1213](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1213.md). The envelope goes first, near 400 kb, and translation starts to go below about 200 kb, the authors' "tipping point". Such symbionts have three-membrane envelopes and among the most biased proteomes in bacteria. They can only work if the host provides what they no longer encode. The host's role is inferred, not shown: the mechanisms are, in the paper's word, mysteries. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1050](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1050.md) | In Athreya, Czuppon and Gokhale's adaptive-dynamics model of an incipient endosymbiosis, mutual dependence (the product of the partners' obligacies) evolves ahead of reproductive cohesion (the product of their adhesions) early on, but only under the mapping in which each partner's free-living growth depends on its own obligacy alone while dissociation depends on both partners' adhesions; the authors' own appendix shows the bias vanishing under matched mappings and reversing under the opposite one, and their survey of real symbioses cannot test it | Athreya, Czuppon & Gokhale (2025), [LIT-1570](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1570.md), read in [NOTE-1211](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1211.md). In the exponential version of the model, all four traits rise monotonically. Each partner becomes more obligate than adhesive, because a gain in adhesion is "damped by the other adhesion" in the dissociation rate. Table S1 shows this is a consequence of that mapping: matched mappings give no bias, and the opposite mapping biases trajectories towards cohesion. The record's summary of the result, "even when investments are uncorrelated", is true of the traits' genetic correlation but not of their functional coupling, which is what decides it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1051.md) | In Athreya, Czuppon and Gokhale's model of an incipient endosymbiosis, the partner with the larger and faster-growing population evolves faster and becomes fully obligate first, a Red King effect in which the collective's shared fate aligns interests; the other partner's dependence then stays where it was, rises to full dependence, or falls to none, according to whether partners are born or die inside the collective, and dependence rises at all only if the collective's carrying capacity is high enough, so a full transition to a mutually dependent, co-reproducing pair is a parameter-dependent outcome and not the default | Athreya, Czuppon & Gokhale (2025), [LIT-1570](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1570.md), read in [NOTE-1211](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1211.md). With the symbiont's population larger and faster, its obligacy reaches 1 first. In the base model the host's R₀ is then exactly 1, so host obligacy is neutral. With within-collective deaths the host goes fully obligate, and with within-collective births it goes back to independence. Obligacy rises from zero only if the collective's carrying capacity exceeds about aK_HK_S/d; collective growth rate does not matter. The authors take the model as a null: a transition "is far from an inevitable outcome of the existence of a higher level of selection". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1052](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1052.md) | A quasi-static attractor describes an open system only while the drift of that attractor in state space is slow against the system's slowest relaxation, scaled by the distance to the tipping threshold; rate-induced tipping is the failure of that time-scale separation, and it can occur while the parameter itself moves slowly, if the attractor is sensitive to it, and with no slowing of any mode | Ashwin, Wieczorek, Vitolo and Cox (2012), [LIT-1654](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1654.md), read in [NOTE-1215](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1215.md). Shown for the linear tipping-radius model, where the sufficient condition for tracking is a rate comparison, and stated for a fast-slow example ("rate dependent tipping occurs when the slow and very slow timescales are no longer separable"). Proposed because for nonlinear systems the paper says "no exact analogy possible" and gives no general condition. It bears on [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md), whose constraints hold over a window between time scales. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1055.md) | In models of decoherence, the information a small fraction of the environment holds about a system rises steeply to a plateau at the system's entropy H_S, so many disjoint fragments each carry nearly all of it, and this redundancy is high only for the pointer observable; Zurek identifies it with objective existence, many observers learning the pointer state independently and without disturbing the system, though the paper argues and does not prove that a plateau in mutual information gives each observer the same record | Zurek (2009), [LIT-1640](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1640.md), section II and Figs. 2–3, read in [NOTE-1229](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1229.md). Redundancy R_δ = 1/f_δ, the number of disjoint fragments each holding (1 − δ)H_S of the information about S, is large for states made by decoherence and absent for random states, and peaks sharply at the pointer observable. Those are model results the review cites. The step from redundancy to objectivity ("Large redundancy implies objectivity") is an identification. The later caveat, that mutual information alone does not guarantee independently accessible records, is not in the paper. Proposed for that step. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1056](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1056.md) | In angular synchronization with outlier offsets, a polynomial-time spectral relaxation, the top eigenvector of the Hermitian matrix of measured phase offsets, recovers the angles once the share of good offsets exceeds about 1/√n on the complete graph, within a factor √((L − 1)/(2 log₂ L)) of the information bound that limits every algorithm, while exact maximum likelihood is a non-convex search costing O(mLⁿ) exhaustively; in this model the price of recovering the global configuration cheaply instead of optimally is a constant factor in evidence, which vanishes for L ≤ 6 | Singer (2011), [LIT-1655](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1655.md), §§2, 4 and 5, read in [NOTE-1224](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1224.md) from arXiv v2. The threshold p > 1/√n comes from a cited rank-one deformation theorem adopted to a non-Gaussian mixture and a heuristic comparison with random correlation, confirmed by simulation at n = 100 and 400; the near-optimality ratio compares it with an information bound for a different success criterion. Proposed for both steps. It does not say that recovery is cheap on every graph, under every noise model, or for fine angular resolution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1073.md) | An aggregate variable much slower than the behaviour producing it becomes an environment the components tune to whether or not it summarizes the underlying regularities well, which helps coordination; if it summarizes them poorly the system likely fails in the end, later the larger the separation | Flack (2017), [LIT-1630](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1630.md), read in [NOTE-1216](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1216.md), §6. Argued informally, with social institutions and the macaque power distribution as illustrations, and no model or data. Proposed. It does not say slowness makes an aggregate accurate, or that separation alone makes the components use it: in Flack the aggregate constrains only through the components' tuning to it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1074](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1074.md) | In Di Biagio and Rovelli's relational account two classical subsystems' perspectives merge, agreeing on a variable's value and on each other's, when they couple to that variable or to each other, and a coupling to a complementary variable can remove a relative fact from a perspective that did not interact; that this answers the combination problem and keeps perspectives consistent is shown only in worked examples computed relative to a single outside system | Di Biagio and Rovelli (2025), [LIT-1676](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1676.md), read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1214](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1214.md), §VI and Apps. D–E. The merge, and the disturbance of a third party's relative fact, are computed in a three-system example and in Wigner's friend. Proposed because the general claims, a solution to RQM's combination problem and consistency of perspectives, are asserted. Every computation is relative to one outside system, where agreement is automatic. This is the same gap [THEORY-621](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-621.md) and [THEORY-1080](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1080.md) name. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1080](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1080.md) | In relational quantum mechanics as Rovelli first stated it, the relation between two observers' descriptions is itself a quantum fact relative to a third system, so no observer's view can be deduced from another's and there is no description in toto, only a net of partial descriptions; the views are held consistent only in that the third system predicts correlated outcomes, which is shown for a single measurement and asserted in general | Rovelli (1996), [LIT-1635](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1635.md), read in arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1227](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1227.md), §§II.D, III.D, IV.A–B. The first half (no deducible relation between views, no in-toto description) is Rovelli's stated position, well supported by his text. Proposed because of the second half: consistency is shown for one case (von Neumann's correlation, p. 9) and left to the reader in general (p. 15). Rovelli's own relativity analogy breaks where relativity supplies an invariant, which bears on [QUESTION-021](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-021.md) by analogy only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1081](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1081.md) | Di Biagio and Rovelli locate the Frauchiger–Renner contradiction and the violation of the Local Friendliness inequalities in one step, a superobserver using facts relative to a friend he holds in full quantum control as if they were his own, which is the classical sum rule applied where those facts are not stable for him; on that ground they base quantum ontology on facts relative to systems, with an absolute macroreality emerging only approximately and only relative to systems for which decoherence is strong | Di Biagio and Rovelli (2021), [LIT-1666](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1666.md), read in [NOTE-1226](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1226.md), §2 (pp. 7–11). The translation of Frauchiger and Renner's assumption (C) and of Bong et al.'s absoluteness of observed events into the use of eq. (3) across contexts is the paper's and is clear. That nothing else goes wrong is cited to others, inter-observer agreement is one sentence, and an agent reasoning about himself is left undone. Proposed for those. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1084.md) | Simon proposes that ill structured problems can be handled by an alternation between a solver working on a problem that is well structured at each moment and a recognition and retrieval system that keeps modifying the problem space from memory or the environment, that a serial solver gains nothing by assembling the problem space at the outset, and that nothing but the size of the knowledge base may separate ill from well structured problems, so that no qualitatively new mechanisms are needed | Simon (1973), [LIT-1634](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1634.md), read in [NOTE-1232](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1232.md). The alternation is described for an architect, matched to a 1923 account of battleship design by an organization and to the NSS chess program, and argued from the seriality of the solver; nothing is implemented or tested, and Simon states the last part as what his analysis "suggests" and as "reason to be optimistic". Proposed for want of a test. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1086](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1086.md) | A fundamental metaphysics bears on the metaphysics of the lifeworld only through features that admit no approximation; without any, a relational world can approximate one of separable individuals, and the independence of social theorizing from fundamental metaphysics is then real but contingent, on the size of Planck's constant, not principled | Jaksland (2024), [LIT-1673](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1673.md), read in [NOTE-1230](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1230.md), reconstructing an argument Barad "only ever alludes to". It is a conditional and the author leaves its antecedent open: whether any ontological feature is all-or-nothing is "an open question". He finds individualism "immediately more agreeable" as approximable, and the dualisms the harder case. The contingency half is argued (a counterfactual on Planck's constant); the no-approximation half is a candidate list, not a demonstration. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1091](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1091.md) | Agential realism has no answer to the measurement problem as it stands: holding that measurement never disentangles apparatus and object, it cannot borrow relational quantum mechanics' treatment of the wave function as bookkeeping without giving up the ontological holism, and its appeal to an improper mixture does not explain why one value is found | Faye & Jaksland (2021), [LIT-1672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1672.md), read in [NOTE-1220](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1220.md), §5. Proposed: the authors present it as a challenge ("There might be other more subtle ways"), and conclude only that consistency with quantum mechanics is unshown ("a leap of faith"), not that agential realism is incoherent. The exchange of 2026-10-27 reported it as "an unresolved measurement problem", which is the strength the text supports. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1092](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1092.md) | Read over the sensor domains, the discrepancies between each observation and the restrictions of others can single out a faulty sensor where the consistency radius alone does not: in Robinson's simulated search, a 2° bearing bias was attributed to the right sensor, without prior knowledge of it, because every large discrepancy involved that sensor's domains, while the radius was lower than in the unbiased case | Robinson (2017), [LIT-1658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1658.md), Example 24, Case 2 (pp. 26–28 of arXiv v3), read in [NOTE-1221](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1221.md). One simulated case, one noise realization, read from a figure. Proposed until a stated procedure is tested over trials, including faults in the restriction maps, which enter the discrepancies in the same way as faults in the data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1095](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1095.md) | In Toner and Tu's hydrodynamic model of a flock, true long-range orientational order survives in two dimensions, where the Mermin–Wagner theorem forbids it at equilibrium and the model's own linearized theory loses it, because the convective coupling of the velocity field to its own transport, relevant below four dimensions, keeps the transverse velocity fluctuations bounded; the authors' heuristic is that motion keeps changing each member's neighbours, so originally distant members come to interact | Toner and Tu (1995), [LIT-1670](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1670.md), read in [NOTE-1228](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1228.md) from the arXiv preprint. The linear theory's loss of order in d ≤ 2 and the relevance of the convective nonlinearity below d = 4 are calculations. The survival of order in d = 2 follows from χ = −1/5 < 0, which is exact only if a cubic vertex stays irrelevant ("we strongly suspect"), or from χ = (z − d)/3 with z < 2, which is expected "on physical grounds". The change-of- neighbours mechanism is a heuristic. Proposed for those two steps. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1097](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1097.md) | A Markov blanket, in any formulation including sparse coupling at nonequilibrium steady state and time-varying blanket states, does not individuate a system: where it falls is fixed by modelling choices made before it is found, so it presupposes the boundary it is used to find, and it cannot represent a boundary the system produces | The wider claim dropped when [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md) was narrowed to Friston's 2013 formulation and promoted on 2026-10-27 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4: a narrowing's dropped claims go to Proposed entries). Both critiques argue the general form, and the record holds neither of the later formulations it would have to reach. Its promote_when is [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md)'s own, moved here unchanged. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1098](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1098.md) | On Karnkowska and colleagues' genome analysis, the oxymonad Monocercomonoides exilis lost its mitochondrion only after the organelle's essential functions had been removed one by one, Fe–S cluster assembly to a bacterial-type SUF system shared with mitochondriate relatives and then the glycine cleavage system by loss, and the loss left the rest of the cell canonical, with no compensating changes found | Karnkowska et al. (2019), [LIT-1574](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1574.md), read in [NOTE-1243](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1243.md). The SUF replacement of the mitochondrial Fe–S pathway is shared by all examined Preaxostyla, including relatives that keep a mitochondrion-related organelle, and those relatives' organelle still houses the glycine cleavage system that M. exilis lacks. So the organelle lost its jobs in at least two steps before it was lost. Apart from the mitochondrion, peroxisomes and mitophagy, the cell's systems are those of an ordinary eukaryote. The order is inferred, not dated, and absence is limited by annotation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1099](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1099.md) | On Kay and colleagues' relaxed-clock dating of pre-LECA gene duplications, most duplications in eukaryotic gene families of archaeal origin, including actin, tubulin, vesicle-trafficking and nuclear-targeted families, predate the onset of duplications in genes of alphaproteobacterial origin at about 2.2 billion years ago, which the authors take as the start of mitochondrial endosymbiosis, so the host was elaborating its cytoskeleton, endomembranes and nuclear machinery before the mitochondrion; each date is a maximum age for its paralogues' functions, many intervals reach below 2.2 billion years, and the order of phagocytosis and the mitochondrion is left open | Kay et al. (2026), [LIT-1566](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1566.md), read in [NOTE-1234](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1234.md). A dated species tree places nFECA at 3.05–2.79 Ga, mFECA at 2.37–2.13 Ga and LECA at 1.80–1.67 Ga. Against an endosymbiosis marker at about 2.2 Ga, 85% of archaeal-origin duplications are older, and most non-alphaproteobacterial bacterial duplications are younger. The authors reject mitochondria-early scenarios and argue against serial endosymbiosis. The sharp edges are that duplication dates bound functions from above, that the priors shape which family can be older, and that the authors themselves cannot order phagocytosis and the mitochondrion. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1100](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1100.md) | On Sørensen and colleagues' review, a bacterial endosymbiont becomes genetically integrated, the authors' mark of an organelle, when host proteins imported into it replace genes it has lost, and this does not require gene transfer from the endosymbiont: in the Paulinella chromatophore and the nitroplast, the two systems with hundreds of imported proteins, the replacing genes are mostly the host's own or come from other bacteria | Sørensen, Stiller, Kröninger & Nowack (2025), [LIT-1560](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1560.md), read in [NOTE-1241](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1241.md). Protein mass spectrometry of isolated endosymbionts found hundreds of host proteins imported into Paulinella's chromatophore and more than 350 into the nitroplast, where they fill gaps left by lost genes. In Paulinella the imported proteins come mostly from the host's own genes, with some from gene transfer from the chromatophore and from other bacteria. In the nitroplast no gene transfer from the symbiont has been found at all. So the route to an organelle is import, and the endosymbiont's genes need not move. The origins are stated in summary, not counted, and the import mechanisms are unknown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1101.md) | Tobiasson, Luo, Wolf and Koonin find, on 5,850 eukaryotic gene stems, that normalized stem length does not behave as a clock of acquisition time: alphaproteobacterial stems are longer than Asgard ones for the 70% of stems below 0.3 and shorter only above 0.35, oxidative-phosphorylation genes presumed acquired together vary by more than two orders of magnitude, and information-processing genes have short stems; they suggest that adaptation after acquisition lengthens stems, so that relative timings drawn from stem lengths alone, including mitochondrion-late orderings and transfer waves, are not supported by the method | Tobiasson, Luo, Wolf & Koonin (2026), [LIT-1558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1558.md), read in [NOTE-1242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1242.md). They test the stem-length method of Pittis and Gabaldón on their own trees and reproduce its mitochondrion-late signal only for long stems. Below 0.3, where 70% of stems lie, the order reverses, and genes presumably acquired together scatter widely. They conclude that "even normalized stem lengths are determined primarily by factors other than the gene acquisition time". The paper still favours a late mitochondrion, on other grounds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1102.md) | On Pittis and Gabaldón's stem-length analysis of the LECA proteome, families of alphaproteobacterial origin and mitochondrial location sit closer to their prokaryotic relatives, after correction for each family's rate, than families of other bacterial origin, which sit closer than archaeal families, and the authors read this as late acquisition of the mitochondrion by a host whose proteome was already chimaeric; the reading of length as time assumes proportional rates before and after LECA, the alphaproteobacterial difference from other bacteria is marginal, and stem length also shortens when a closer relative is sampled | Pittis & Gabaldón (2016), [LIT-1595](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1595.md), read in [NOTE-1240](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1240.md). Of 1,078 LECA families, bacterial ones have shorter normalized stems than archaeal ones (P = 1.38e-25), and alphaproteobacterial ones shorter than other bacterial ones (P = 0.044). Origin tracks location: alphaproteobacterial with the mitochondrion, other bacterial with endomembranes, archaeal with the nucleus. A plastid control runs the right way. The sharp edges are that stem length measures distance to the closest sampled relative, so sampling can move it, and that the chimaeric host could have come from partners or from transfer, which the paper cannot tell apart. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md) | On Shigenobu and colleagues' genome of Buchnera sp. APS, the aphid symbiont keeps the genes for the amino acids its host cannot make and has lost almost all of those its host can, uses host-made glutamate and aspartate as precursors, and lacks phospholipid synthesis and nearly all its own transcriptional regulators, so that its metabolism interlocks with the host's and it presumably lives only inside the bacteriocyte, a state reached by gene loss from an E. coli-like ancestor | Shigenobu et al. (2000), [LIT-1596](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1596.md), read in [NOTE-1236](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1236.md). The first complete genome of an obligate insect endosymbiont: 640,681 bp, a subset of E. coli's. What is shown is gene content. The interlocking of host and symbiont metabolism is inferred from it and from earlier physiology. That Buchnera cannot live outside the bacteriocyte, and that the host supplies its membrane lipids, are the authors' inferences. The paper names no mechanism of loss beyond a homeostatic niche: it says nothing of drift. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1104](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1104.md) | In Tobiasson, Luo, Wolf and Koonin's constrained-tree survey of widespread eukaryotic protein families, Asgard archaea are the largest single prokaryotic source, with about half the likelihood weight in the best-resolved families and the lead in nearly every functional system, while Alphaproteobacteria contribute a small, coherent set centred on the mitochondrion and other bacteria about a third of families, scattered across functions with no pathway from one donor; the authors read this as one Asgard host lineage, one endosymbiont and piecemeal gene transfer rather than further symbioses, a reading the gene ancestries alone cannot establish | Tobiasson, Luo, Wolf & Koonin (2026), [LIT-1558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1558.md), read in [NOTE-1242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1242.md). In 4,290 well-resolved eukaryotic–prokaryotic clusters, Asgard takes 50% of likelihood weight and leads in almost every functional class. Alphaproteobacteria account for mitochondrial translation, oxidative phosphorylation and 4Fe-4S assembly. About a third of clusters point elsewhere, with no functional pattern except a narrow Myxococcota signal. The authors infer a complex Asgard ancestor, a late mitochondrion and "no indication of another symbiotic event". The composition is shown; the scenario is read off it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1105](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1105.md) | In Bernabeu, Manzano-Morales, Marcet-Houben and Gabaldón's reconstruction of the last eukaryotic common ancestor's proteome, two bacterial phyla besides the mitochondrial ancestor, Myxococcota and Planctomycetota, each account for a share of the proteome comparable to that of Alphaproteobacteria and Asgard archaea under thresholds calibrated on those accepted partners, and stem-length distributions order the acquisitions as waves, Asgard first, then Planctomycetota, then the mitochondrial ancestor and Myxococcota together; the authors read this as serial associations with several partners, while conceding that their data cannot say whether any donor was a symbiont | Bernabeu, Manzano-Morales, Marcet-Houben & Gabaldón (2026), [LIT-1561](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1561.md), read in [NOTE-1237](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1237.md). Under thresholds chosen to maximize assignments to Alphaproteobacteria and Asgard, Myxococcota (3.92% of the proteome) and Planctomycetota (2.24%) pass in every dataset, beside Alphaproteobacteria (3.99%) and Asgard (3.28%). A control removing Alphaproteobacteria from the database does not reproduce their pattern. Stem lengths put Planctomycetota before the mitochondrion. The authors "challenge models depicting eukaryogenesis as a one-off event resulting from a binary symbiotic interaction", and also say their data "do not provide information on the host or endosymbiotic nature of any partner". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1106](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1106.md) | On Campbell and colleagues' comparison of cicadas, hosts whose endosymbiont Hodgkinia has split into many interdependent lineages compensate by sending more Hodgkinia cells to each egg, up to about six times as many, with Sulcia numbers and the transmission route unchanged, so that every egg still receives every lineage; the authors take the raised titre as a host adaptation driven by the symbiont's fragmentation and a cost of it | Campbell, Łukasik, Meyer, Buckner, Simon, Veloso, Michalik & McCutcheon (2018), [LIT-1590](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1590.md), read in [NOTE-1235](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1235.md). Measured: Hodgkinia cells per egg from 4,889 in a single-lineage cicada to 30,154 in M. septendecim, with Sulcia at 2,572 to 5,643; marker genotypes present in every egg sampled; the same route under the light microscope. Not shown: a trend across complexity beyond M. septendecim, or that splitting came first. The authors also speculate that a larger transmitted population weakens bottlenecks and could feed further splitting. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1107.md) | On Sørensen and colleagues' scenario, an endosymbiont becomes an organelle in steps: the host first targets effector proteins into it; an imported host protein redundant with one of its functions then lets the endosymbiont's own gene decay, making it dependent; and a general import pathway, once evolved, brings in hundreds of proteins; this genetic integration arises only in permanent, vertically transmitted associations, and host effector control without vertical transmission, as in rhizobia, does not lead to it | Sørensen, Stiller, Kröninger & Nowack (2025), [LIT-1560](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1560.md), read in [NOTE-1241](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1241.md). Their closing scenario orders the steps from endosymbiont to organelle: effectors first, then dependence through one redundant imported protein, then many imported proteins once a targeting signal evolves. Rhizobia, targeted by about 700 host peptides yet not vertically transmitted, are their case of control without integration. It is a scenario built from systems at different stages, not a sequence observed in any one. | Proposed |
